News.title: Inside rise of Gen Z mafia paying boys £160 to kill in tourist spots… with ‘no rules’ on bloodshed & chilling new tactic
News.content:
FROM gunning down civilians in the street to planting car bombs, a deadly new class of teenage gangsters are terrorising Europe, ripping up the traditional mafia ‘rulebook’ to commit acts of unspeakable violence.

Welcome to Daltons Mafia – a brutal syndicate originating in Turkey and ruled by 29-year-old Berat Can Gökdemir – who are now targeting tourist hotspots, including Spain and France.





Armed with AK47s and explosives, the brazen gangsters revel in murder sprees and traffic heroin and cocaine – all while flaunting their sick exploits across TikTok and Instagram.

Impoverished teen drug mules and hitmen have no fear of the police – and regard prison time as a glorious networking opportunity.

“They don’t use any rules,” mafia investigator Osman Çaklı told The Sun, adding that “their main aim is to destroy everything”.

The Daltons – named after a bumbling gang of comic book villains – began as a collection of child gangs committing petty theft in the suburbs of Istanbul, Turkey, according to reports.

But in the last two years, the Gen Z mafia have exploded in the German capital of Berlin and are infiltrating southern France, Italy and Spain.

Chilling videos posted online show attacks on shop owners or wads of cash from drug deals – with some clips even filmed inside prison cells.

“Thousands of videos [are] filmed from inside cells”, sociologist Marcello Ravveduto told The Sun, adding that inmates dance to music and “show off life behind bars as if it were a reality show”.

Online mafia clips overlap with the manosphere because they “share a dominant masculinity”, explained Ravveduto.





“In both we find the cult of virility, money as the measure of worth, redemption through force, a hierarchy that rewards whoever dominates.”

Germany has rarely been under the boot of mafiosos – unlike their neighbours in Italy and Eastern Europe.

But Berlin is now facing “an unprecedented surge in lawlessness” said a new report from the Global Initiative against Transnational Crime.

Gun crime has spiked – doubling from 2024 to 2025 – and since January there have been nine shootings on people or property.

New Gen Z mobsters are more violent than traditional mafias, according to Turkish journalist and investigator Osman Çaklı.

“Normally underground life has its own rules, the traditional mafia maybe kidnaps the [shop] owner, hits them, maybe shoots them in the foot”, he said.

“But when it comes to them [the Gen Z mafia] they don’t use any rules.

“Let’s say it’s a bar or a pub – they walk in and they can kill everyone in the pub. Their main aim is to destroy everything.”



Where once the mafia used single-shot firearms, the Daltons “use AK47s and explosives”.

More than 5,000 kids dealing drugs for different Gen Z mafias have been locked up in Turkish prisons in the last three to four years, said Osman.

Many are seduced into the mafia online – and transformed into disposable gunmen.

“There is no training”, said Osman, adding: “They just find one person online and put money in his pocket and send them to kill their target.”

Teen mobsters are killing for a pittance – paid just £160 (10,000 Turkish liras) for murder, rising to £1,600 (100,000 Turkish liras) for high profile assassinations.

Chillingly, Osman added that recruits “are learning by doing”.

Describing their crimes, he said: “They go to one store and they say ‘if you want to continue your business you must pay out.’ If shop owners refuse, they start to show unseen violence against them.

“It is something new in Turkish mafia-style”, he added.



Some members are just 15 years old, with many lured in by the promise of wealth and luxury plastered across the digital mafiosphere.

Disturbing videos show violent extortions – or boast luxury cars and designer watches over a backing track of melodic trap music.

Flagrant displays of criminality across TikTok and Instagram have outraged older mafia bosses – who regard the videos as reckless and stupid.

Osman explained that older mafioso committed their crimes “in a very hidden way and nobody used to know what was going on”.

Gen Z mafia on the other hand “intentionally show everything that is going on – they put videos on social media”.

Ravveduto said “the tension is real” between old-school mafia bosses and the younger mafiosos.

He said: “The old guard built its power on the myth of silence.

“A boss who shows himself is a boss who exposes himself, and whoever exposes himself becomes fragile in front of investigators and rivals. From that point of view, the showing-off on TikTok looks like recklessness, almost vulgarity.”



Osman points out that the Daltons Mafia is built up of children who grew up surrounded by poverty and crime – and have no fear of being arrested.

He said: “For normal people like us it is, of course, frightening to be caught by police, but for them its a risk worth taking.

“They go to prison and gain new networks in the prison – the benefit is more than the harms.”

Ravveduto agreed, adding “prison is the university of the underworld” and considered a rite of passage for child delinquents.

Thousands of child criminals have been arrested in Turkey after trafficking Class A drugs and shooting dead shopkeepers who fail to do their bidding.

Police in Germany have also been scrambling to crack down on the rise in shootings, extortion and violence – seen especially in Berlin but also across Stuttgart, Frankfurt, Cologne and Hamburg.

In November 2025, the Berlin police launched a new Iron Taskforce in February this year they added another called “Telum” – meaning weapons – to battle the spike in gun trafficking.

German investigators trying to crack down on the lawless teens have found themselves on disturbing “death lists” with bounties placed on their heads, reported newspaper Bild.



Cops have so far failed to arrest any members of the Daltons Mafia, according to one Berlin-based member who spoke to Osman.

Osman trawled through court documents from June and confirmed that the names of those arrested were not those of the Gen Z mafia.

The Berlin police force declined to comment.

Turkey has spawned three main Gen Z mafia syndicates – of which the biggest are The Daltons.

The other two are the Casper Mafia – also named after a cartoon character – and the Çirkinler which translates to “The Uglies”.

The three gangs engage in bitter turf wars on the streets of Germany with The Uglies and the Caspers both gunning at rivals The Daltons.

But all three are ruthlessly expanding their territory with The Daltons snaking into Marseille, southern France.

The Casper Mafia and the The Uglies meanwhile are establishing a presence in Spain, Italy and Georgia.



But German police are cracking down on the lawlessness.

One suspected thug, 21, who punched a businessman in the face alongside three masked accomplices, was charged in June.

And Berlin’s Iron Taskforce is currently handling 126 cases involving gun trafficking and violent extortion, according to German newspaper Tages Spiegel – though it is unclear whether suspects are members of The Daltons.

News.title: Man ‘sexually assaults’ girl, 16, at train station before passengers confront him and he flees – as cops release CCTV
News.content:
'ASSAULT' PROBE Man ‘sexually assaults’ girl, 16, at train station before passengers confront him and he flees – as cops release CCTV

A 16-YEAR-OLD girl has allegedly been seriously sexually assaulted at a train station, as police release CCTV.

The reported incident happened at around 10.30pm at White Hart Lane station in Tottenham, North London.

A man is alleged to have approached the teen and sexually assaulted her before being confronted by passengers and fleeing onto a train.

Police have now released CCTV of a man they believe may have information that could assist their inquiry.





British Transport Police detectives are asking anyone with any information that may assist them to come forward.

The force said: “Detectives would like to speak to the man pictured, as they believe he may have information that could assist their ongoing investigation.

“Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016 or call 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 875 of 7 July.

“Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Trump ‘smuggled off Air Force One in catering cart to board secret flight’ away from Nato summit amid Iran threat
News.content:
DON A MISSION Trump ‘smuggled off Air Force One in catering cart to board secret flight’ away from Nato summit amid Iran threat

DONALD Trump was reportedly smuggled off Air Force One in a catering truck last month in an elaborate ruse after a threat from Iran.

The US president was secretly swapped onto a different plane as he left a Nato summit in Turkey on July 8, according to the Washington Post.



Journalists and even White House staff were tricked by the plot, believing they were on the same plane as the president as it left Ankara.

Trump had publicly boarded Air Force One – but it was a decoy.





He was then smuggled off the plane into a catering truck by a door on the other side of the plane.

It had reportedly been raised right to the plane door so the president couldn’t be seen at all as he slipped out.

Trump was accompanied by aides as he duped onlookers.

The US president was then driven in the truck and snuck onto a smaller military plane, Air Force C-32A, according to reports.



War Secretary Pete Hegseth shared the secret flight with Trump.

A US official told the Post he boarded from the outside, “to make the flight appear typical”.

Both planes were painted with blue and white, and emblazoned with the presidential seal.



But the public had been told that Trump would fly on the older plane which he boarded in plain view before sneaking off.

The US president had announced he would travel on the “former Air Force One” to leave Turkey, instead of the plane he had arrived on, a newer jumbo jet gifted to him by Qatar.

He had started using the newer Boeing 747-8 just days earlier.

The cunning plot to use Air Force One as a decoy flight – carrying the media and some White House staffers – came after a night of heavy US strikes on Iran.

The “deception operation” was triggered by a credible threat to Trump from Iran, a US official said.



Questions had been raised about the security of the Qatari jet as Iran ramped up threats on the president’s life.

Both flights landed at RAF Mildenhall and Trump appeared before TV cameras and descended the decoy plane’s stairs.

It is not clear how he snuck back onto the former Air Force One.

White House communications director Steven Cheung said: “The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats.”



The White House did not confirm the secret flight swap.

News.title: Family of 13-year-old hit-and-run victim heartbroken as killer set for release after just two years
News.content:
THE family of a 13-year-old boy killed by a hit-and-run drunk are devastated the driver could be freed from prison after just two years.

Kaylan Hippsley died in 2024 when he was hit by Harley Whiteman, 19, who then abused paramedics treating the teen.



He was jailed for six years, increased to nine after Kaylan’s family appealed.

But Whiteman, now in an open prison, has since had his sentence cut to just four years, so is to be freed in October under Labour’s early release scheme.



Kaylan’s family in the Rhondda, South Wales, urged PM Andy Burnham to keep him locked up.

His sister Chloe Williams said: “We as a family are calling on Andy Burnham to review our case and demand immediate action.

“The decision to move Kaylan’s killer to an open prison after barely two years goes against everything the Court of Appeal ruled.

“It feels like justice has been stolen from us.

“We will not accept this. We demand that he serves his full sentence behind closed doors. Kaylan deserves nothing less.”

And cousin Julie Craig said: “It beggar’s belief that after two years he’s allowed back into the community.



“It’s absolutely devastating.

“This just feels like a kick in the teeth.”

News.title: Cops seize three tons of cocaine worth over £200m at British port after drugs concealed in bananas sent from Colombia
News.content:
NEARLY three tons of cocaine with a street value of £232million was discovered in a container of bananas.

Border Force officers with sniffer dogs found the drugs in the consignment from Colombia.



The National Crime Agency was alerted and officers seized the dope at London ­Gateway Port in Essex on Friday.

They then watched as a man in a truck drove the shipment — minus the cocaine — to a warehouse, where a crime gang had “a massive panic” on finding the drugs missing.



The NCA raided the site near Buntingford, Herts, and eight Brits and one Dutchman were arrested.

A source said: “They must have thought they had been turned over by criminals but, worse than that, the NCA went steaming in.

“It’s the biggest seizure of cocaine in the last few years and this will cause serious grief in the criminal underworld.

“There could be massive fall-outs over the loss of the drugs.’’

The nine arrested, most in their 20s, have all been bailed ­pending enquiries.

NCA officers were still searching the warehouse on Monday.



The largest ever seizure of cocaine in the UK came in Southampton in 2024.

A total of 5.7 tons was found hidden in banana containers heading to Europe from Colombia.

News.title: Fuel prices have soared and what has Labour done about it? Sat back and raked in an extra £1BILLION in tax
News.content:
ANDY BURNHAM says he wants to “pull every single lever” to bring down the cost of living.

He’s off on a summer tour of the country, in what No10 calls “listening mode”, asking ordinary people how the Government can make their lives easier.



It’s a nice image — the Prime Minister, freshly back from holiday, rolling up his sleeves and heading out to the regions to hear from the public before he’s even properly unpacked his boxes in Downing Street.

I’d love to believe it. I really would.



But if these last few months have taught us anything, it’s that the political elite still seem completely disconnected from how the real world operates outside the M25 and the M60.

The latest figures from the RAC, released last week, tell their own story.



Petrol has climbed to around 161p a litre.

Diesel has surged to roughly 181p.

Filling a standard 55-litre family diesel car has breached the £100 mark once again.

Since the Iran conflict flared up, UK drivers have been forced to find an extra £5.5billion just to keep their tanks full for work.



Around 70 per cent of that has landed on diesel drivers — the tradespeople, the hauliers, the people who actually keep this country moving.

And what has the Government done about it?

It has sat back and let the Treasury quietly pocket close to £1billion in extra VAT.

As pump prices rise, so does the taxman’s take.

Ministers are, in effect, making money from the very crisis that is squeezing working families and pushing up the cost of everything else.



So while Mr Burnham talks about pulling every lever, the lever he really should be reaching for is the one sitting right in front of him at the pumps.

In his first week in the job, he announced a cut to VAT on household energy bills and a £2 cap on bus fares, both presented as “everyday fixes”.

Fine as far as they go — but they don’t go very far at all for the millions of people whose working lives simply cannot be organised around a bus timetable.

Like so many metropolitan leaders before him, Burnham seems to have a shaky grasp of how towns, villages and rural counties actually function.

For millions of people, driving isn’t a lifestyle choice.



It’s how they earn their living.

A nurse doing a 2am shift at a regional hospital doesn’t benefit from a bus fare freeze.

A care worker doing her rounds between elderly patients can’t plan her day around a patchy rural timetable.

A plumber, an electrician, a carpenter — none of them can lug their tools on to the number 42.

Farmers and hauliers, who keep the supermarket shelves stocked, certainly can’t move Britain’s goods by public transport.



These are the people generating the tax revenue that keeps the country running, and yet they’re the ones being squeezed hardest to pay for it.

Even if you wanted to swap the car for the bus, good luck.

One in five buses fails to run on time.

Average bus speeds in major cities have dropped by 23 per cent since 2010.

In London, the average bus now crawls along at 8.6mph during peak hours — slower than 50 years ago.



In Manchester and Birmingham, congested routes barely outpace a brisk walk.

Meanwhile, 15 per cent of the entire bus network outside London has vanished since the pandemic.

At the same time, Burnham is happy to take credit for a rail fare freeze that his predecessors actually announced, even as a season ticket from Crawley to London Bridge still costs £4,856 a year — around a fifth of a minimum-wage worker’s salary.



Bus caps and rail freezes make for tidy photo opportunities.

They give increasingly image-conscious politicians something shiny to stand next to.

But they mean very little to people whose jobs cannot be squeezed into a timetable dreamt up in a city-centre office.

Those people need help at the pumps, and they need it now.

The existing 5p fuel-duty cut, still in place thanks to The Sun’s Keep It Down campaign, predates this latest crisis and simply isn’t enough on its own.



Cutting VAT on household energy bills is welcome, but it won’t take a single penny off the cost of filling a van.

Other countries have already worked this out. Italy cut diesel taxes by 15p a litre.

Greece targeted reductions of up to 13p for hauliers and professional drivers.

Ireland slashed excise duty by 27p on diesel and 23p on petrol.

Even further afield, Thailand, the UAE, South Korea and Australia have all stepped in with targeted relief.



Britain, by contrast, has simply let the Treasury enjoy the windfall while treating drivers as an easy top-up to the public purse.

So here’s my message to Mr Burnham as he sets off on his listening tour: Actually listen.

Cut VAT from 20 to 15 per cent and you knock 7p off a litre of petrol and 8p off diesel overnight.

Pair that with a genuine duty cut and you’d finally be delivering something that matters to the people who keep this country moving, rather than another photo beside a bus.

Cheaper transport is great for those who can use it.



But Britain’s tradespeople, carers, farmers and hauliers have no alternative but to drive.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They’re not a bottomless cash machine, and they’re certainly not the enemy.

It’s time to stop posing beside buses and start backing the workers who actually keep Britain moving.

News.title: Andy Burnham must find a way to keep PC Andrew Harper’s killers behind bars or face public’s fury
News.content:
Find a way

ANDY Burnham has apparently been told by hand-wringing civil servants that it’s “not possible” to block the early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers.

They need to be told to try harder.



There are a few hundred inmates serving time for manslaughter.

Burnham needs to order officials to find a way to bar those serving the longest sentences from being freed.



That would minimise the threat of any legal challenges from lags and ensure remorseless thugs Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole stayed behind bars.

As the petition to keep Bowers and Cole locked up ticks up towards one million, the public’s demand is crystal-clear.



They expect Burnham to meet the hopes HE raised in the first place.

The Prime Minister must realise he has the power to overrule Government officials and lawyers all too often stuck in their comforting bubble of State uselessness and a lack of accountability.

With a massive majority behind him, this issue boils down to a question of sheer will.

Push boat out

HOW much longer must Brits put up with migrants and people-smugglers making a mockery of our open borders?



Yesterday’s raid on UK waters by a mega-dinghy carrying a record 230 illegal asylum-seekers opened up a new front in the small boats crisis.

It’s clear that far from the gangs being smashed, the criminals are running rings around French cops.

Their new tactic of packing as many as possible on a single craft — enough yesterday to fill a Boeing Dreamliner jet plane — could soon make 1,000 arrivals a daily occurrence.

It’s not just the sheer numbers. The cost is becoming astronomical, too.

In 2023, the Home Office estimated each migrant costs taxpayers £106,000 minimum over four years in free housing, healthcare and other benefits.



That means yesterday’s mega dinghy could cost nearly £25MILLION.

That’s a staggeringly high price to pay while Burnham & Co leave Britain without any kind of plan.

Betting slip

FOR a bloke who claims to love sport and champion working-class culture, Andy Burnham seems surprisingly keen to demonise anyone who likes a flutter.

The Prime Minister says he will boost our High Streets by making it harder to open vape shops and . . . bookmakers.

But bookies are not anti-social enterprises. They provide good jobs and help keep sports like racing and rugby league afloat.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In any event, it’s hard not to conclude Burnham’s plan is purely performative.

Thanks to Labour’s tax raids on gambling, what’s actually happening is hundreds of betting shops are closing.

News.title: Brit tourist, 66, dies in horror parasailing accident while on holiday with husband in Benidorm
News.content:
HOLS TRAGEDY Brit tourist, 66, dies in horror parasailing accident while on holiday with husband in Benidorm

A BRITISH tourist has died in a horror parasailing accident in Benidorm while on holiday with her husband.

The 66-year-old crashed onto rocks after a powerful gust of wind caused the line tethering her parachute to the boat to snap.



The woman went into cardiac arrest, but desperate efforts to revive her she was pronounced dead at the scene.

It was not immediately clear whether the unnamed holidaymaker’s husband was injured in the ordeal.



He is believed to have suffered broken ribs and was reportedly “walking wounded” following the horror crash.

The tragedy unfolded in Benidorm’s Rincon de Loix are at around 6pm on Monday after a sudden change in weather conditions.

Prior to the incident, a red flag was raised, warning holidaymakers at the famous Costa Blanca resort.

Witnesses described chaotic scenes as the parasail spiralled out of control.

After the line snapped, the couple hurtled towards jagged rocks as they were left at the mercy of the wind.

One witness said: “It was clear they were going to crash.”



A police investigation has been launched and remains ongoing.

This comes after a 16-year-old British cheerleader was killed in a horror boat accident while holidaying with her family.

Abbie Lainton, from Swindon, died “in a terrible accident” off the coast of a Caribbean island that also left her two siblings injured.

Abbie died after she was badly burnt when a tourist boat carrying around 35 people suddenly ignited and blew up off the coast of the Dominican Republic.

She was rushed to intensive care but died three days later.



Her siblings remain in hospital.

Authorities said 24 people were injured with 11 taken to hospital for treatment for burns.

Gisell Segovia and her husband Navin Torres, 35, were on the boat when it blew up and saw Abbie badly injured after the explosion.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Navin told The Sun how he was with the Brit teen as she fought for her life, calling Abbie “a warrior” who “did not go out without a fight”.

Authorities have not yet revealed the cause of the fire but have launched an investigation.

News.title: PM asks justice secretary to find way to keep PC Harper's killers in jail
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told his justice secretary to find a way to exclude PC Andrew Harper's killers from an early release scheme designed to ease prison overcrowding.

Burnham is confident a solution can be found to remove Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter in 2020, from the government plan, the BBC has been told.

Downing Street had earlier warned it would not be possible to exclude "one or two offenders" convicted of manslaughter from the early release of prisoners.

PC Harper, 28, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged behind the getaway car of three teenagers who had fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Under changes to the Sentencing Act made this year, Cole and Bowers, who were found not guilty of murder, will become eligible for release from custody next January after serving half of their sentences.

They are in a category of prisoners - those who have committed certain serious violent or sexual crimes - who until now would have had to serve at least two-thirds of their sentence in jail before being considered for release.

It is not yet clear how the government will prevent Cole and Bowers from being treated the same as other prisoners with similar sentences.

If ministers said, for example, that prisoners with manslaughter convictions could not be considered for the scheme, that would have an instant impact on many other inmates.

A government spokesperson told the BBC: "The prime minister has asked the Justice Secretary to work through further options to keep a greater number of the most serious offenders in prison, including the killers of PC Harper."

A source said the Justice Secretary Alex Norris would set out "in due course" how the government would exclude Cole and Bowers from early release.

The prime minister has been making daily calls while on holiday to find a solution, sources told the BBC.

Around 5,000 people are expected to be released under the sentencing changes, down from 6,000 after exemptions were previously announced for those convicted of the most serious crimes including rape, child sex offences and grooming.

The third man jailed for the manslaughter of PC Harper - the vehicle driver Henry Long - was given a longer 16-year jail term. Because he received what is called an extended determinate sentence at the time, he cannot be considered for this early release scheme.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts for almost all of England as next heatwave begins
News.content:
Amber heat health alerts come into force across most of England on Tuesday as temperatures start to climb again at the start of the summer's latest predicted heatwave.

The UK's Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is warning that significant impacts are likely across social and health care, including a rise in deaths.

The amber alerts will be in place until Friday evening to cover high and even extreme temperatures expected through this week.

During the peak of the heatwave temperatures across England and Wales will widely be in the low to mid-30s Celsius.

Amber alerts are in place for all regions of England, aside from the North East, which has been given a less intense yellow alert for the same period.

It comes after drought officials declared 71.3% of England is now in drought.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and "for many people, the high streets they grew up with have become unrecognisable".

BBC News has exposed organised crime on high streets across the country, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes and vapes, selling cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco or up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham said "the rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for".

He added: "That's not on. I said we would improve Britain's high streets, and that's exactly what we are starting to do.

"We're putting communities back in control and giving local people a real say over what opens on their high street."

News.title: Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino
News.content:
US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position.

Trump's backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust "through deception" with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Trump's comments are the first time he has come out in defence of Infantino since the FFE plans came to light on 28 July.

"Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino," Trump wrote on social media.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again."

The 2026 World Cup was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico this summer, with Spain crowned champions after beating Argentina in the final.

When addressing the FFE proposals for the first time on 31 July, Trump said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino has a close relationship with Trump and awarded him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize in December 2025.

News.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak: When and where to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: Jewish school heads spend more time on security than education, review finds
News.content:
Headteachers of some Jewish schools are spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than on educational matters, a review into antisemitism in schools and colleges has found.

Sir David Bell, speaking for the first time about his ongoing government-commissioned independent review, told the BBC he had been struck by how many leaders of Jewish faith schools had told him security was their primary concern - and that "sometimes education takes second place to that".

The report, due in the autumn, examines the experiences of Jewish pupils and staff in faith and secular schools and colleges in England.

Sir David said he found that pupils were "subject to regular harassment and abuse".

He said Jewish children and young people "are facing a pressure - and indeed one might say even a crisis - that is not the experience of other communities in this country".

The review is likely to recommend dedicated training for all teachers and improved education about antisemitism for pupils, the BBC has been told.

The BBC has spoken to several headteachers and staff at Jewish schools. All asked not to be named because of concerns over their security and that of their schools.

One headteacher said: "In recent years [security] has become an overwhelming priority and increased a significant amount. There have been weeks where approximately 90% of my time has been spent on security-related matters.

"Security concerns can become one of the many things that headteachers carry with them beyond the school day and, quite literally, can be among the things that keep me awake at night."

News.title: 'I started in my 20s and made £8,000': Why women are often better investors than men
News.content:
It can be "largely attributed to culture", according to Gillian Fleming, co-founder and managing director of UK-based Mint Ventures, a women-led angel investment firm.

"Men historically have been more likely to make family investment decisions, and women have also historically not owned the balance of wealth, but that is changing now," she says.

"Also, money and wealth creation is not a topic that women often discuss, and we would like to change that."

Teleri says she has noticed a shift of late. "Investing is definitely something that women are talking about more, which is always a good thing," she says. "That's the case with my friendship group."

When women do invest in stocks and shares, analysis by Fidelity International found that over three years its female personal investing customers recorded cumulative returns of 50%, compared with 47% for men. The analysis does not identify the reason for the difference, but why may it be the case?

One possible clue to women's slightly higher long-term returns lies in how often they buy and sell their investments, with Barclays data showing that women trade around half as frequently as men.

News.title: England set to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: GB's Hunt comes of age with European 100m gold
News.content:
Amy Hunt had her coming of age moment as she stormed to 100m glory to claim her first senior international title and deliver Britain's first gold medal of the European Athletics Championships.

Hunt announced herself on the sport's global stage last year with world 200m silver in Tokyo - the first individual international medal of her senior career.

Having backed that up with Commonwealth 100m silver two weeks ago, the 24-year-old would not be denied gold this time in Birmingham.

"I have had such a string of silvers and I was starting to get a bit fed up with it, so I thought it was time for gold," Hunt, who won in 11 seconds flat, told BBC Sport.

"My parents gifted me these gold earrings to finally level up, because I wear all-silver jewellery.

"They said it was time for gold - they left me that note two nights ago - so it made me quite emotional.

"It was definitely time for me to come of age here."

It was Britain's second medal on the opening day of action after the hosts took silver in the mixed 4x400m relay.

Yemi Mary John held off Dutch athlete Myrte van der Schoot on the home straight to bring a British quartet also featuring Ben Jefferies, Charlotte Henrich and Toby Harries home in three minutes 10.47 seconds, behind winners Norway (3:09.62).

News.title: Treasury contributed to woman's death, inquest hears
News.content:
The death of a Treasury worker who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers was "materially contributed" to by her employers, an inquest has heard.

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Surrey Coroner's Court heard the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy which would have made clear that if the allegations were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

A spokesperson for the Treasury said it was "considering the findings carefully".

In a statement to the press, Moffat's family said they believed the Treasury failed in its duty of care.

"When she needed support, reassurance and fair treatment, she was left frightened, isolated and convinced her career and reputation had been destroyed," they added.

The inquest, in which a conclusion of suicide was recorded, heard that on 19 May Moffat went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

She was told of allegations she had shared sensitive personal information about colleagues, obtained as part of her job.

Moffat, from London, denied this.

News.title: Cocaine worth £232m found in banana shipment
News.content:
Cocaine with a street value of Â£232m was discovered hidden in a large shipment of bananas from South America.

The 2.9-tonne (2,900kg) haul was smuggled into London Gateway Port in Thurrock, Essex, on Thursday.

The drugs were removed from the container and then delivered to an address near Buntingford, Hertfordshire, where Border Force officers swooped in.

They arrested nine men allegedly connected to the bust, who were later released on bail.

Border Force had been tipped off about the illegal consignment by the National Crime Agency.

News.title: Vandals target playground before it has even opened
News.content:
A play area that cost more than Â£178,000 was vandalised days before it was due to open.

Knowsley Council leader Graham Morgan said he was "absolutely furious" that every piece of play equipment at the Finch Woods play park in Halewood, Knowsley had been spray painted with graffiti over the weekend.

Trees and safety surfacing were also damaged and rubbish was left strewn across the site, with the cost of the damage estimated to run into thousands of pounds.

Morgan condemned the "mindless vandalism", saying "it is the cost to the community that sickens me the most".

News.title: Antiques stolen in 16th Century manor house raid
News.content:
More than 20 antiques were stolen from a National Trust (NT) property during a break-in last month, it has been revealed.

The silver, pewter and brass items were taken from the 16th Century manor house at Baddesley Clinton in Warwickshire, on 30 July.

The most notable piece of the 25 taken was a Georgian silver salver engraved with the coat of arms of the Ferrers, the family who resided at the house for about five centuries, the NT said.

"We very much hope the objects will be returned, so they can be enjoyed by everyone," a spokesperson added.

News.title: Great-grandad with cancer risks his health to help others on 460-mile journey
News.content:
A great-grandfather with bladder and kidney cancer is walking 462 miles (743km) for charity, despite knowing it could impact his own treatment.

John Eryl Parry, 78, from Pontypool, Torfaen, began his coast-to-coast journey at the UK's most easterly point in Lowestoft, Suffolk, on 21 June, and is due to reach St David's Head in Pembrokeshire on 11 August.

He was diagnosed with cancer after he fell off a ladder and was taken to hospital.

John admitted he hadn't told his oncology team about his challenge, but said he was warned by a doctor that his body would "change" during it, and it could impact his treatment plan.

News.title: MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
News.content:
A newly-elected MSP has apologised for the hurt caused by comments in which they talked of the "demonisation" of rape.

Scottish Green Party politician Q Manivannan has also faced criticism for suggesting rape is a "spectrum of things" during a podcast recorded before they were elected to the Scottish Parliament.

Earlier, the Scottish Rape Crisis Alliance (SRCA) - which represents four rape crisis centres - said there is "no hierarchy of rape" and warned the MSP not to minimise sexual violence.

In a statement, Manivannan said clips from the podcast had been "selectively edited" but said they were "sorry" for the upset, and insisted they would never seek to diminish a rape survivor's experience.

The comments, which were made during The Subjective Space podcast , externalrecorded last year, sparked fury after they re-emerged online at the weekend.

News.title: No evidence of data breach after Chinese-made component found in Navy drones, MoD says
News.content:
The Ministry of Defence (MoD) said there is no evidence to suggest a systems or data breach after the Royal Navy's new sea drones were found to include a Chinese-made component.

During what the MoD called a "routine cyber vulnerability assessment" of the drones, the cameras were found to have sent a squark â also known as a heartbeat communication â to a Chinese IP address.

A squark can signal when the system is switched on, is functioning properly, but it can also carry location information.

"A thorough investigation found no evidence of MoD data or systems being accessed, compromised or transmitted externally," an MoD spokesperson said.

"Our assurance and testing processes are designed to identify and address potential vulnerabilities early, and we continue to undertake routine security activity across our systems and equipment," the MoD added.

This is embarrassing for the MoD which, like most Nato countries, has banned Chinese components from military equipment - not least over fears of spying.

The K3 Scout sea drones can remotely carry out surveillance, and according to their supplier, "support a wide range of mission profiles including maritime awareness, force protection, logistics and precision strike".

The supplier of the Royal Navy's 20 new K3 sea drones, Kraken, said it was given assurances about security. But a third party supplier of the drone camera still had Chinese-made components.

Kraken has said it is confident no sensitive information has been shared.

The story was first reported by The Telegraph., external

The security lapse has been addressed, but it is a reminder of the heavy dominance on Chinese supply chains.

Even the defence sector â which has taken measures to prevent espionage â still struggles to source materials, and technologies that are China free, or as cheap.

A Los Angeles judge is weighing whether to throw out an explosive ageism lawsuit brought by a 70-year-old former Venice High School choir director who claims years of relentless workplace bullying forced her to quit.

Wendy Sarnoff, who chaired the school’s music department before resigning in 2023, sued the Los Angeles Unified School District in October 2024 alleging age discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and failure to prevent discrimination.

Sarnoff claims colleagues routinely mocked her in faculty meetings as "old" and "old school," denied her computer training, and told her she was "too old" and "hopeless" when she asked for technical help.

A Los Angeles judge is weighing whether to throw out an explosive ageism lawsuit brought by a 70-year-old former Venice High School choir director ( AP )

According to court filings, harassment from an assistant principal escalated in 2019 with repeated pushes for her to retire, leaving her feeling like the school's "laughingstock." Sarnoff also claims that when her district-issued computer was stolen, LAUSD refused to replace it, forcing her to raise funds on her own to buy a replacement device.

LAUSD attorneys are fighting back, forcefully denying any age bias in court pleadings and accusing the veteran teacher of mistreating her own students.

District lawyers allege Sarnoff routinely called students "stupid," "idiot," and "not bright," once announced her classroom smelled like a "French w********e," and told students, "If you can't sing 'The Star Spangled Banner' you should die."

Sarnoff resigned in 2023 following district investigations into her conduct, though her attorneys state the principal requested she be marked "ineligible for rehire" before she formally handed in her resignation.

Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Cherol J. Nellon heard arguments Monday on LAUSD's motion to dismiss and took the matter under submission.

US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the Fifa president would be a costly move.

open image in gallery Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump presenting the World Cup (PA) ( PA Wire )

The US president wrote: “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

“If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!”

Trump was at the centre of another Infantino scandal in the summer after calling the Fifa president to request a “review” of USA striker Folarin Balogun’s red card, which was subsequently “suspended”, allowing him to play in their round of 16 tie with Belgium.

Uefa and two other confederations have held initial talks about organising competitions themselves amid the backlash against the embattled Infantino.

Europe’s governing body, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which ​oversees football in the ‌Caribbean, North and Central America, have accused Infantino of “deception” and while it is understood they want to give him the chance to resign and leave his position with dignity without seeking re-election in March next year, they want to insulate themselves from the unfolding crisis.

Uefa has previously threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions, which was reiterated even after Infantino’s climbdown in an effort to oust him from power.

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of Fifa’s tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20 per cent to private investors.

But an open letter signed by the heads of Uefa, AFC and Concacaf has urged Fifa to hold an independent review into Infantino’s scheme, while not naming the Swiss directly.

open image in gallery Fifa president Infantino is under immense pressure ( PA )

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” the letter said. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

It comes after member associations began to officially withdraw their endorsement for Infantino’s re-election in 2027, with England and Wales among that contingent.

With a spell of heatwaves and record-breaking temperatures, chances are you’re considering long-term cooling suggestions – rather than a quick fix such as portable air conditioning units.

Indeed, Simon Bones, a leading sustainability expert and founder of intelligent retrofit company Genous, helping homeowners retrofit their homes for a greener future, says there’s been renewed interest… particularly this summer.

“Dramatically so… either for air conditioning on its own (which we actually don’t do), or in combination with other kinds of renewables, where people are thinking about things like heat pumps.

“They’re increasingly asking, ‘can it cool too?’. So I would say it’s been dramatically different from what we would be getting any other time of year.”

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

In answer to the question, Bones says some heat pumps can cool, if configured correctly. “It can get quite complicated, but you’ve got various options.”

Incorporating renewables

When it comes to electricity-consuming items such as fans or air-conditioning, Bones says these can be effective, but use a lot of power.

As an alternative, he suggests installing an air-to-water heat pump with underfloor heating which provides mild cooling by flowing cooler water through the heating circuits.

Moreover, he says any cooling takes a lot of energy, so integrating with solar panels is smart. “Generating electricity from solar panels, storing it and then reusing it from home batteries to heat your home from a heat pump.”

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

“And because you can buy it, store it, use it at a different time and generate it yourself, it means you’ve got more control over it. And it’s much lower carbon because heat pumps in particular, are four times plus more efficient than even the best gas or oil boiler.

“And solar panels as well,” he adds. “They don’t consume anything apart from sunlight, so they’re fully green once they’re in.”

Bones also suggests thinking about cooling as part of a holistic renewable strategy. “It’s really about the financial,” he highlights. “Running air conditioning, they’re powerful units and reasonably expensive.

“And if you’re thinking about using solar panels, they generate power more when it’s hot and sunny, and therefore you’re aligning your production with your demand.”

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

He says they also deflect some of the heat from the roof as a side-benefit, “but on a day like today, the sun is shining and people have air conditioning”.

This means they can help power those active cooling technologies, and reduce the cost of the electricity they need to buy.

Reducing heat gain

Other practical tips for staying cool include insulating lofts, and reducing solar gain from windows.

Bones says to make sure your loft is well insulated (if you have one), to reduce heat coming in. “If you’ve got poor insulation, most people think that’s about heat oil escaping in the winter.

“But the opposite is true. So the loft space will typically, in a normal house, be really hot in the summer. And if you’ve got poor insulation between the loft and your ceiling, that heat comes down through the ceiling as well.”

open image in gallery (Alamy/PA)

He also suggests reducing solar gain from windows. Think triple-glazed windows or those with coatings, though Bones says even normal double-glazing lets in less heat and sunshine energy – helping to keep heat in during the winter.

“If you’ve got windows that face into the sun, the more layers of glazing you have, the less that sunlight comes in. So single glazed windows, you’ll get a lot of heat transfer through from what we call solar gain from the sunshine; triple glazing less so.

“Triple glazing is also a better insulator for different reasons in the winter,” highlights Bones. “So performance glazing generally keeps your house a little cooler in the summer, and warmer in the winter.

“Probably not something most people do purely for that reason,” he underlines. “Financially, glazing is expensive, whereas loft insulation, which we’ve just talked about, is much cheaper.”

And while it feels like the longest heatwave on record, there are still some weeks to go…

“It certainly feels quite long, but I’m sure we’ll all be complaining about the cold weather in a couple of months’ time,” quips Bones.

A U.S. federal appellate court on Monday paved the way for thousands of lawsuits to proceed against Meta Platforms, Alphabet's Google, ByteDance's TikTok, and Snap Inc's Snapchat over allegations that the companies deliberately engineered their social media platforms to be addictive to young users.

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, based in San Francisco, turned down an appeal submitted by Meta and TikTok that sought to overturn a lower court decision requiring the technology companies to defend against more than 3,000 lawsuits filed in federal court. The panel concluded that the companies had brought their legal challenge prematurely.

In their appeal, the tech firms argued that Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act of 1996—a federal statute that generally shields online services from liability related to third-party user content—also prevents lawsuits asserting that the platforms failed to warn the public about their addictive nature.

open image in gallery The San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected an appeal by Meta and TikTok seeking to overturn a lower court ruling requiring them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits ( Reuters )

Under standard legal procedure, most appeals occur after a case has fully concluded with a final ruling or jury verdict. The tech companies contended they should not be required to wait until the conclusion of litigation to challenge the lower court's decision rejecting their immunity defense.

However, the 9th Circuit determined that Section 230 offers a defense against liability rather than broad immunity from being sued, making the early appeal procedurally premature.

The appellate court also denied Meta's request to delay a trial scheduled to begin on Wednesday in a lawsuit brought by 29 state attorneys general. That action alleges the company unlawfully gathered and utilized data from children, designed its social media services to keep young people hooked, and misrepresented consumer safety protections. Meta had argued that the trial should not go forward while its appeal remained pending before the circuit court.

open image in gallery The TikTok Inc. building is seen in Culver City, California ( Copyright 2018 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

The ruling arrived just days after a state judge in New Mexico determined that Meta had created a public nuisance, ordering the company to pay $567 million into a teen mental health fund and to establish enhanced safety features for youth on its platforms.

A spokesperson for Meta declined to comment on the court's decision.

Representatives for TikTok did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the Monday ruling.

open image in gallery Meta has yet to comment on the latest decision ( PA Archive )

Lexi Hazam and Previn Warren, attorneys representing thousands of school districts and individual plaintiffs suing Meta and the other tech platforms in federal court, issued a statement noting that the ruling permits the multistate trial to move forward, along with a trial concerning claims brought by public school districts set for February.

"A trial is how the public finds out what Meta knew about its products' impact on children, when it knew it, and what it chose to do with that knowledge," the attorneys said. "Meta has fought to keep that evidence from the public."

The extensive litigation, brought by state governments, local municipalities, school districts, and individuals, alleges that the social media companies intentionally designed addictive features for young users, contributing to rising rates of depression, anxiety, body-image concerns, and a wider youth mental health crisis across the United States in recent years.

Plaintiffs, including parents, school districts, and state officials, argued that the district court's previous ruling was not a final order and was therefore unappealable at this stage. They also rejected the companies' interpretation of Section 230, arguing the law does not extend protection to claims concerning product design choices and operational practices.

open image in gallery The cases, which have been centralized before U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, seek damages, penalties and restitution from the companies ( AFP/Getty )

The federal cases have been centralized under U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, with plaintiffs seeking financial damages, statutory penalties, and restitution. The technology companies had appealed orders issued by Rogers in 2023 and 2024 that largely permitted the legal actions to continue.

In addition to the federal claims, the companies are confronting hundreds of parallel lawsuits in state courts, including approximately 3,300 claims consolidated in a California state court proceeding.

In the first case to reach trial within the California state court litigation—a closely watched test of how juries might respond to similar allegations—a Los Angeles jury in March found Meta and Google negligent for designing social media platforms that inflict harm on youth.

The jury awarded $6 million to a young woman who alleged she became addicted to Instagram and YouTube during her childhood.

The New Mexico public nuisance finding against Meta followed an earlier phase in that case, in which a jury in March directed the firm to pay $375 million after determining it had misled consumers regarding platform safety.

Both Meta and Google, which have denied all allegations across the legal proceedings, stated that they plan to appeal the decisions.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool agree Barcola terms, Man City close in on Rodri replacement, Man Utd target defender
News.content:
Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Liverpool are hoping to swiftly add to the loan signing of Ronald Araujo by hashing out a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola after reaching a reported agreement over personal terms. Barcola leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger.

Arsenal’s busy transfer window looks set to continue as they move on from their disappointment in not signing Vinicius Jr. They are hunting alternatives in the forward line with Julian Alvarez and the aforementioned Barcola on their list but defensive reinforcements may yet come in the form of Cristian Romero. The Tottenham captain is rumoured to leave Spurs this summer and is eyeing up a switch to their closest rivals.

Meanwhile, Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca – who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected. City seem to be making preparations for that outcome as they close in on the signing of World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.

The Perseid summer light show spectacular is back – and it could be better than ever.

The stunning meteor shower will peak on Wednesday night into Thursday morning and coincides with a total solar eclipse for parts of Europe — though the best time to view the fireballs will come after totality.

As many as 50 to 100 meteors per hour may be visible under ideal conditions, according to NASA. The American Meteor Society estimates 30 to 50 meteors per hour could be seen from rural regions.

Random meteors are visible in dark skies on any given night. Meteor showers tend to put on dazzling celestial shows and happen at predictable times every year when the Earth plows through trails of debris left behind by comets and, sometimes, asteroids. Those remnants collide with Earth's atmosphere at extremely high speeds, producing streaks of light known as shooting stars.

The Perseids are debris from comet 109P/Swift-Tuttle, an icy ball that orbits the sun every 133 years and isn't scheduled for a return visit until 2125. Observations of this meteor shower date back over 2,000 years.

The Perseids are a perennial favorite because they tend to produce brilliant fireballs. Summer temperatures also make this shower popular.

open image in gallery A composite image made from 726 photographs taken over three hours from midnight showing the rotation of the earth around Polaris, the North Star, in the night sky over Ashton Windmill, Somerset (Ben Birchall/PA) ( PA Archive )

"We don't have to suffer through a cold winter night to get a good view of meteors," said astronomer Zach Vanderbosch with McDonald Observatory in Texas.

The moon will be in its new moon phase during the Perseids' peak, making viewing conditions even better.

"The moon is beautiful, but it's such a diva," said astronomer Aparna Venkatesan with the University of San Francisco. "New moon means we don't have moonlight flooding the sky, and you tend to see way more meteors as a result."

How to see the Perseid meteor shower

To spot the meteors, go outside after dark, away from clouds and city lights.

The best views will be between midnight and dawn when the constellation Perseus is high in the northern sky. The meteors will appear to radiate from that constellation.

Look up and give your eyes a half hour to adjust to the darkness. Vanderbosch recommends picking a patch of sky to focus on until a quick, bright streak passes by — even in your peripheral vision — and to avoid looking at your phone.

"There's just something magical about it," Vanderbosch said.

Where can I see the solar eclipse in the UK and Ireland?

Although exact timings of the 12 August solar eclipse will vary and weather conditions may cloud visibility, in general you’ll be able to see more coverage the further south-west you are, said Royal Museums Greenwich.

First contact should be visible from 6.08pm in Scotland through to 6.18pm in Truro, Cornwall. From 7.05pm to 7.15pm destinations in the UK will see the eclipse reach its maximum, and by 8.10pm the moon will no longer be covering the sun in all areas.

For those who are planning to view the solar spectacle, eclipse glasses are crucial.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's damning Liverpool claim, being doubted by players, club's telling response
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola's tenure at Liverpool has not started brilliantly. But the Basque boss took time to settle at Bournemouth too before hitting top speed.

Having guided the Cherries into Europe for the first time in their history, Iraola was earmarked as the man who would take over the Reds' reins from Arne Slot. But since being hired in June, his side hasn't prospered.

In a friendly against Monaco on Sunday, Liverpool went 2-0 up inside 30 minutes but were defeated 3-2. Pre-season matches have to be taken with a pinch of salt, but the manager's post-match comments have sparked concern, as he damningly admitted his squad "cannot sustain the level we want" for entire matches.

There is also work to be done in the transfer market and some supporters can be forgiven for having reservations with the new Premier League campaign just over 10 days away. However, patience will be key with Iraola, as his spell with Bournemouth began in an equally underwhelming fashion.

‌
