Jamie Carragher admits Liverpool transfer 'worry' and issues Man Utd warning READ MORE :

In 2023, he was appointed to replace Gary O'Neil. This was the Basque coach's first job in England, having previously managed AEK Larnaca, Mirandes and Rayo Vallecano.

To say he failed to fly out of the gates is an understatement. After just nine games in charge, his team were winless and sat 19th in the Premier League. Sack rumblings had begun.

View 3 Images Iraola joined Bournemouth in 2023 (Image: Getty)

‌



Iraola brought with him a stark change to how O'Neil and other coaches who came before him like Eddie Howe had done things. Ex-Cherries forward Antoine Semenyo said he and many other players doubted their manager and initially struggled with a more intensive approach to match preparation.

"I didn't see it at the start," said Semenyo, speaking on All Out Football's In The Mixer. "When he came in, he had his way of playing and it was very new to us, the way he structured the weeks.

"We didn't really have any days off, so it's very hard for a team to go from having Wednesday/Sunday off to having no days off. It was very different at the start. The results weren't going our way and the fans were saying he needs to be sacked. Everyone slowly got used to the system and it just went up from there."

View 3 Images Liverpool's players must keep the faith (Image: Getty)

‌



Liverpool's players are likely experiencing just this at the moment, with predecessor Slot often being criticised for the amount of time he gave them off. But if faith is shown in Iraola, it appears that he can deliver.

In an interview given in 2025, the manager claims the Bournemouth board heavily backed him and that they were the ones who showed him data that belied the poor early results. Eventually, things started to click.

A 2-0 home win against Newcastle in November 2023 kick-started a run of seven unbeaten league matches. Bournemouth finished 12th in Iraola's first campaign and his second saw improvement as they placed ninth. But it was last term that Iraola's vision really became a reality, as his Cherries finished sixth and secured a historic place in the Europa League.

Iraola could easily have been shown the door at the Vitality Stadium after this rocky beginning, but the club's trust in him paid dividends. Though his pre-season with Liverpool makes for grim reading, even if the start of this season is underwhelming, he's proven that good things come to those who wait.

Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours

Bruno Fernandes has been a key player for Manchester United since joining the club in 2020 and a former team-mate has spoken about a classy gesture

Brandon Williams says former Manchester United team-mate Bruno Fernandes still messages him and helps him get match tickets. Williams is currently without a club after leaving Hull City in February.

‌



Since 2023, Fernandes has been United's skipper and for all intents and purposes, the face of the club. But it's not just on the field where he is influential.

‌



Defender Williams, who joined the club's academy ranks at the age of seven, left United in 2024 after the expiration of his contract and has faced legal trouble in the years since. But the 25-year-old is still in contact with some of his former team-mates at Old Trafford and Fernandes in particular showed his class with a kind act.

‌



Williams told The Athletic how Fernandes still keeps in touch with him and arranges match tickets. He said: "That's why he's the captain, he's an unreal guy."

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis SUING Crystal Palace over gun banner
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis SUING Crystal Palace over gun banner

Evangelos Marinakis has filed a claim for defamation at the High Court over a banner unfurled by Crystal Palace supporters which depicted him holding a gun to Morgan Gibbs-White's head

View 2 Images Evangelos Marinakis has brought a claim against Crystal Palace (Image: Nicolas Koutsokostas/Getty Images)

Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace over a banner which showed him holding a gun to Morgan Gibbs-White's head.

‌



Lawyers for the Greek shipping magnate filed the claim for defamation at the High Court on Monday. The filing is against CPFC Limited, the commercial entity of Crystal Palace, and "Persons Unknown".

‌



It comes almost a year after the banner was shown by Palace supporters during the 1-1 draw between the two clubs at Selhurst Park on August 24 in the Premier League.

‌



The banner read: "Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption."

Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing and has never been charged with any of the stated offences. Palace refused to comment when contacted by Mirror Football, while Forest didn't respond.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Carabao Cup second round draw in full as Chelsea, Newcastle and Leeds discover opponents READ MORE :

Palace were charged by the Football Association with misconduct in November over the banner. They were alleged to have failed to ensure that supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or provocative way.

‌



In February, the FA fined Palace £50,000 over the incident. The ruling noted: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

The banner came shortly after Forest held onto star player Gibbs-White following interest from Tottenham. Spurs were understood to have triggered the midfielder's £60million release clause, only for him to then sign a new contract with Forest.

View 2 Images Morgan Gibbs-White with Evangelos Marinakis (Image: Nottingham Forest FC)

‌



Gibbs-White then did a video interview alongside Marinakis in which he explained his decision to stay put. "I've felt at home at Forest from the moment I arrived," he said at the time. "The support from the fans, my team-mates, and everyone around the club has been unbelievable.

"I believe in what we're building here – and with the backing of [owner] Mr Marinakis and the enormous ambition he has, I want to be part of making something special. I'm excited for what's to come."

Marinakis added: "There was significant interest from various clubs, but we were determined to build our future with Morgan at the heart of it. I promised our fans we would not only compete, but grow stronger and stronger every season. Today is another big step in that journey."

Article continues below

There has been heightened tensions between Palace and Forest over the past year after the London side lost their place in the Europa League. Palace qualified by winning the FA Cup in 2025, only to be ejected by UEFA, who found they had broken third-party ownership rules.

Forest ended up taking their place in UEFA's second cup competition, with Palace demoted to the Conference League, which they ended up winning anyway under the management of Oliver Glasner. Glasner left Palace at the end of last season and has now taken over as Forest's manager, working under Marinakis.

Sports.content:
Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has been desperate for reinforcements in central defence following a difficult injury-hit pre-season - and now Ronald Araujo has arrived from Barcelona

View 3 Images Ronald Araujo has joined Liverpool on loan from Barcelona (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool have completed the signing of Ronald Araujo from Barcelona on a season-long loan deal - which could become a permanent switch if the Reds active the £47.14million option to buy.

‌



The 27-year-old Uruguay international moves from the Nou Camp in one of the more surprising switches of the summer so far. Last term he was still serving as the skipper for the Spanish giants, but has now opted for a move away after seeing his minutes decline.

‌



He is the second defender to arrive at Anfield this summer after Jeremy Jacquet completed his switch from Rennes, further bolstering a backline that already has Virgil van Dijk as its leader. Joe Gomez has been injured in pre-season and has struggled to remain consistently fit.

‌



Araujo has chosen the No 33 shirt - which was last worn a decade ago by Jordon Ibe. The centre-half becomes the fourth Uruguayan to play for the Reds - following in the footsteps of Darwin Nunez, Sebastian Coates and Luis Suarez.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jeff Bezos to become Liverpool co-owner as FSG agree to sell HUGE stake in club READ MORE :

Suarez remains one of the greatest Liverpool players of the Premier League era and was quick to reach out to his compatriot, congratulating him on his switch to Anfield.

‌



“We loved watching the English Premier League and everyone in Uruguay gets up early in the morning to catch the games," Araujo told the club's website.

“Of course as a kid I used to watch Luis playing all those fantastic games for Liverpool. We all know what he achieved, the history that he made within this club during his time here. So it’s fantastic.

“From minute one, I’ve been sort of asked about that kind of comparison since I’ve arrived here. I get on really well with him, we’re quite close. Just a few minutes ago I got a good luck message from him saying all the best, you’ve joined a great club and all the very best for your time here.”

‌



View 3 Images Luis Suarez reached out to Ronald Araujo (Image: Getty Images)

Araujo comes into a Liverpool side that have endured a difficult pre-season. On Sunday they squandered a two-goal lead for the second time in a matter of weeks, losing to Monaco in Andoni Iraola's first game at Anfield.

The Reds finished the friendly with youngster Luke Chambers and midfielder Wataru Endo as the centre-back pairing, underlining the need for new arrivals, with £55m signing Jacquet still getting fit.

‌



Iraola was critical post-match and admitted that the team were not capable of sustaining their level for the 90 minutes, raising questions over whether they can implement his philosophy.

"We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes," he said. "Right now we probably don't have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has been desperate for new signings (Image: Ian Horrocks, Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

‌



"We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game."

Iraola has made it clear that Liverpool need to make signings in the summer transfer window if they are to turn around their disappointing second campaign under Arne Slot. The Reds remain in the market for a world-class attacker, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola the number one target.

It has been a summer of upheaval for Liverpool, who changed manager before Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards decided to quit, piling more pressure onto sporting director Richard Hughes. Meanwhile, FSG have been busy negotiating a 30 per cent investment from a consortium which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

Sports.title: Trump warns of 'terrible mistake' if FIFA replaces Infantino
Sports.content:
US President Donald Trump has warned FIFA would be making a "terrible mistake" if it got rid of Gianni Infantino as head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men's World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the FIFA president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: "FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20 per cent to private investors.

But UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC hit out at "deception" and a "fundamental breach of trust" around Infantino's botched plan, the three continental associations each signing a new open letter to the "football family" on Monday, without naming Infantino specifically but referring to a leader who "abandoned their duty" by breaking trust "through deception".

In the three-page document they again criticised the president's World Cup sale plans and rejected FIFA's claim that they had been a "mistake", adding: "There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment - not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol on whether Infantino can continue as the president of FIFA

UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC had been the three confederations to reject Infantino's plan before it was scrapped, while UEFA went further and announced a boycott of FIFA competitions - and last week confirmed the threat remained while Infantino is still in post.

The associations also hit out at the manner of a FIFA management committee meeting held in Morocco last Wednesday - a meeting which ended with a statement publicly backing Infantino - for not instead addressing FIFA's wider senior leadership at its base in Switzerland.

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him," the letter read. "There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness."

US Soccer and Canada Soccer - two of the three federations which hosted the World Cup - also called for meaningful change.

A US Soccer statement read: "US Soccer, Canada Soccer, CFU (Caribbean Football Union) and UNCAF (Central American Football Union) stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens FIFA's governance, transparency and accountability."

The UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC letter came around 24 hours after FIFA itself had hit out at "a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine" the governing body and president Infantino over claims surrounding his conduct at UEFA.

UEFA confirmed on Saturday a "departure payment" was made to a female employee alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino when he was the European organisation's general secretary.

The Daily Telegraph reported the woman received a six-figure sum and UEFA confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, adding it was "in line" with regulations at the time.

The allegations intensified the position of Infantino, who worked at UEFA for 16 years and was its general secretary between 2009 and 2016 before being elected FIFA president, following his aborted plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Image: FIFA president Infantino

While not directly referencing UEFA's statement, FIFA accused Infantino's critics of trying to weaken his authority and have him removed from his role without a due re-election process.

A statement said: "It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president.

"Those who do not have the support of FIFA's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.

"Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

"The FIFA president has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football

"Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA's president or the institution he was elected to lead.

"FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

"FIFA's responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global. Through the FIFA president and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it."

Sports.content:
Panic over, England fans - your team will NOT have to qualify for the 2027 Cricket World Cup.

England's drop-off in 50-over cricket had seen them plummet down the rankings and leave them at risk of missing out on automatic entry into next autumn's event in Africa.

However, the rot was stopped with successive come-from-behind series wins - over Sri Lanka earlier this year and then at home to India in July - leaving Harry Brook's men inside the required top eight in the rankings ahead of the September 30 cut-off.

With South Africa, who are certain of a place as co-hosts, sitting fourth in the standings, ninth-placed Bangladesh also secure direct passage to the tournament proper.

Zimbabwe are in, too, as they are another of the competition's co-hosts.

India, New Zealand, Australia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan - who secured their place with victory over Ireland - are the other guaranteed entrants.

That means two-time champions West Indies, ranked 10th, will have to take part in the qualifying event for the third successive 50-over World Cup.

West Indies - World Cup winners in 1975 and 1979 - successfully reached the 2019 edition in England but then lost in qualifying for the 2023 showpiece in India.

The Caribbean side still have two more ODIs, in India, before September 30 but even if they win those two matches, they cannot move into the top nine in the rankings.

Image: Scotland will be in the qualifying tournament next year

West Indies are now headed for the qualifier in February and March, alongside Ireland, Netherlands, Scotland, USA and five yet-to-be-determined teams.

Under ​a new format for 2027, the ​winner of the qualifier will advance directly ​to the second stage of the World ⁠Cup, while the teams placing second, third and fourth will feature in the first round known ⁠as the Super Series.

That late switch was criticised in a joint statement from the Scottish and Dutch cricket boards, who accused the ICC of "weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket."

Sky Sports News has contacted the ICC for comment.

Sports.title: Vasseur reveals 'most important' target for Ferrari after F1 summer break
Sports.content:
Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur has revealed the areas in which he believes the Italian team need to improve during the second half of the 2026 Formula 1 season as Lewis Hamilton attempts to stay in the title battle.

A highly consistent first 11 races for Hamilton have left him with hope of claiming a record eighth drivers' title, as he sits 50 points behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli at the top of the standings.

While the gap is far from insurmountable, Antonelli's Mercedes has generally appeared to have a performance edge of Hamilton's Ferrari, meaning the Italian squad likely need to find further gains if the 41-year-old is to maintain his challenge.

Ferrari also remain in the hunt for the constructors' title, with Mercedes only 72 points clear despite their early-season dominance.

Vasseur said: "The first half of the season was in stages. Until Spain, Mercedes was flying.

"After Spain, when we came back, we scored more points than Mercedes in the last four or five races."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix.

The Frenchman was speaking after the final round before the summer break in Hungary, during which Ferrari and Hamilton made a series of errors that saw him finish fifth when the car was at least fast enough to be in the podium places.

"Where do we have to improve? If I draw a conclusion based on Hungary, I would say execution," Vasseur continued.

"But execution so far was probably a good one for us from the beginning of the season."

"We know that we have to improve on the engine side and we will do it. The inertia on the engine is much higher than on the chassis."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson analyses Lewis Hamilton's speeding in the pit lane that handed him a five-second time penalty.

Why Vasseur thinks Ferrari can respond to McLaren surge

It has been suggested by rivals, including McLaren's Hungarian Grand Prix Lando Norris, that Ferrari have the best chassis on the grid, but have been held back by their power unit not being as strong.

Ferrari have already once upgraded their engine having been granted the opportunity to do so by the FIA's performance-balancing measures, but it remains to be seen how much more improvement can be brought to the power unit over the second half of the season.

While Vasseur acknowledges there is room for improvement of the engine, he insists the team must continue to work hard to bring further upgrades to the chassis.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix.

"The most important thing will be to be able to keep the pace in the development," Vasseur said.

"McLaren did a good job for a while, but they don't have exactly the same philosophy [as us ]because they are bringing a big package.

"For sure each time they bring something, they are making a huge step. We have a different approach, trying to bring parts every race.

"We have to keep this momentum because there are still 12 races to go. It's a lot. We have a room for improvement on the chassis everywhere, and we have to keep this pace."

Sports.title: Why Dutchwoman Weber is ineligible for 'amazing' home Solheim Cup
Sports.content:
Dewi Weber would relish the opportunity to be involved in a home Solheim Cup in any capacity after being ineligible to feature for Team Europe in the Netherlands.

Bernardus Golf near Den Bosch hosts the biennial contest from September 11-13, live on Sky Sports, where Anna Nordqvist will captain Team Europe's bid to regain the trophy after their 2024 loss to Team USA.

Weber threw herself into Solheim Cup consideration at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship earlier this summer, when a tied-third finish lifted her from outside the world's top 200 to a career-high world No 82.

"I was aware of it [eligibility] the second I got a text from Anna [Nordqvist, Team Europe's captain], who was asking, 'are you an LET team member?' I said no," Weber exclusively told Sky Sports at the AIG Women's Open.

"Then the goal just became, 'well, then you've got to win' and was the goal since."

"I mean it would have been so special [to have featured]," Weber explained. "It's the first time the Netherlands is hosting and I really like that golf course. They've put so much effort into both the place and the event itself.

Sports.title: Rockets relying on others to avoid eliminator after loss to Brave
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets are relying on a favour from Manchester Super Giants after a six-match winning run was ended by Southern Brave at Trent Bridge to deny them direct progress to Sunday's final.

The league leaders must now await the outcome of second-placed SunRisers Leeds' trip to Manchester Super Giants on Tuesday to discover whether they will have to go through an eliminator.

SunRisers can snatch top spot and a ticket straight to Lord's with a win as their net run rate is superior to the Rockets'. But a Super Giants win would move them level on points with SunRisers on 20 and potentially even up to second with a big enough margin of victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In the coin toss for the match between Trent Rockets and Southern Brave, the coin hit Chris Jordan's shoe, forcing a retake!

South African Tristan Stubbs saw Brave home with three balls to spare after hitting 52 not out off 28 balls, but the game changed on Marcus Stoinis' arrival at the crease with the score on 78-3 at halfway chasing 159 for victory.

The Australian dispatched his first three balls for six, four and six to signal his intent and his 46 off 25 changed the game.

The Rockets' total of 158-5 was boosted by an unbroken stand of 66 in 39 balls between Mitchell Santner (35no) and Lewis Gregory (28no).

Prior to that opener Finn Allen (23 off 12) and Aneurin Donald (19 off nine) had created the early momentum.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Trent Rockets' Calvin Harrison and Finn Allen came together to catch Jamie Smith out with a fantastic team effort

Reflecting on Brave's campaign, Stubbs said: "It's been disappointing, but it's a nice way to finish off. In hindsight it's a bit frustrating.

"We gave it our all for the month but in the first three games we lost a couple of close ones and then it's hard to get momentum. I think we've shown at the end what we can do but it took us a while to get there."

Sports.title: Donald Trump says it would be a ‘terrible mistake’ to replace Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the Fifa president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!”

Uefa and two other confederations have held initial talks about organising competitions themselves amid the backlash against the embattled Fifa president.

Europe’s governing body, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which oversees football in the ‌Caribbean, North and Central America, have accused Infantino of “deception” and while it is understood they want to give him the chance to resign and leave his position with dignity without seeking re-election in March next year, they want to insulate themselves from the unfolding crisis.

Uefa has previously threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions.

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of Fifa’s tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20% to private investors.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But an open letter signed by the heads of Uefa, AFC and Concacaf has urged Fifa to hold an independent review into Infantino’s scheme, while not naming the Swiss directly.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” the letter said. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

It was the day after the final game of last season at Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base and, before clearing his belongings on his last day in the building, the departing head coach, Andoni Iraola, spent a couple of hours in his office chewing the fat with his successor, Marco Rose, talking players, pubs and tactics. The story goes that, with time moving on, Tiago Pinto, the club’s sporting director, knocked on the door to advise them there were other things to tackle.

It was an interesting scenario that speaks volumes of the respect between the pair. Long before joining Bournemouth, Iraola cited Rose’s Borussia Mönchengladbach side as one of his favourite teams to watch, the German’s “vertical football” helping them qualify for the Champions League in Rose’s first season in charge.

Rose accepts that Iraola, in absorbing the sales of key players totalling more than £250m last season and qualifying for Europe for the first time, has set a high bar. Remarkably, Bournemouth did not lose a game after the sale of Antoine Semenyo in the second week of January. Rose put it succinctly during pre-season in Austria. “Andoni didn’t leave a lot of space to improve,” he said. “Pressure’s on.”

In his first session, Rose told the players he loved the way they attacked the Premier League last season. Playing in the Europa League, however, represents uncharted territory for a team in the second tier as recently as four years ago. It is why Bournemouth’s hierarchy contacted peers at Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest to understand the realities of juggling the Thursday-Sunday rhythm the competition will bring. Rose is close friends with Oliver Glasner, who is now at Forest, but won the Conference League last season with Palace. “We are not going to Europe just to enjoy, we want to be competitive,” Rose said. “We are not there just to watch.”

Unlike last summer, so far they have retained all key players, chiefly Alex Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, the 20-year-old forward who breezed into double figures in his debut Premier League season and the club consider a generational talent. Kroupi attracted serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, among other European superpowers, but a freak foot injury during a pre-season drill means he is sidelined for at least three months.

At the end of the season, Bournemouth earmarked a centre-back to replace Marcos Senesi and a striker to compete with Evanilson as key priorities and by the start of August the club had recruited Álvaro Rodríguez, whom Rose wanted to sign at Leipzig, and António Silva from Elche and Benfica respectively. Juanlu Sánchez joined from Sevilla to provide competition for Adam Smith, the evergreen 35-year-old into his 14th season at the club, and will also fill the void left by Álex Jiménez, who has joined Fiorentina on loan with an option to sign permanently because he remains suspended in England while under investigation by the Football Association.

Off-field picture

The smallest stadium in the Premier League has been a building site this summer, with the club working to ensure their 11,357-seater ground complies with Uefa regulations. There has been a wider facelift, too, with every seat being replaced, while they are filling in two corners to increase the capacity by 800 this season. Playing in Europe brings the challenge of meeting Uefa’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules, which caps on-pitch spending at 70% of a club’s revenue. Bournemouth finished the 2025-26 season at 82% and they continue to work towards meeting the threshold. Last month the academy was awarded category one status, four years after being category three.

Owner-fan relationship

The American billionaire Bill Foley described himself as a dictator upon buying the club approaching four years ago, but supporters are grateful for his naked ambition. Foley, who made his fortune in insurance, is forthright and somewhat prophetic. In 2023, he said the club would play in Europe within five years – and achieved it in three. It was a similar story with Vegas Golden Knights, whom he vowed would win the Stanley Cup within six years of him launching the ice hockey franchise in 2017 – they won it in their sixth season. Foley recently added rugby union’s Exeter Chiefs to his sporting stable, which extends to Lorient, Auckland FC and Moreirense. Not every decision is universally popular but Foley, who turns 82 in December and predominantly splits his time between California and Vegas, puts his money where his mouth is.

The manager

As a defender, Marco Rose was schooled by Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, and Ralf Rangnick at Hannover, so had quite the education before beginning his coaching career at home town club Lokomotive Leipzig. Klopp told Rose, after promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004, that he would excel in the dugout and he has since managed some of the biggest names: Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham at Borussia Dortmund, Dominik Szoboszlai and Dani Olmo at RB Leipzig. Rose has been compared to Klopp and, naturally, Iraola, given his appetite for high-energy tactics. Bournemouth routed Genoa 10-1 in pre-season so, could his style be even more aggressive than Iraola’s? “I would say [to be] even more aggressive than Andoni is quite difficult,” came the reply. His grandfather, Walter Rose, represented Germany in 1937.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen António Silva has all the attributes to be a bargain buy for Bournemouth. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

These days, £50m is about the going rate for an elite defender. Tottenham paid £52m to sign Jan Paul van Hecke. Chelsea paid the same fee to take Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace. Bournemouth pocketed £50m when Dean Huijsen joined Real Madrid last year, though that price was set by a release clause. They are deals that make Bournemouth’s £25.7m purchase of António Silva, a 22-year-old who has been a regular at Benfica since breaking into the team and has experience in the Champions League, Europa League and 20 caps for Portugal, appear a snip. Silva, who is right-footed but prefers to play as a left-centre back, is a direct replacement for Senesi.

Stat attack

Bournemouth scored nine goals from Opta-defined counterattacks last season, the joint most in the Premier League. But their threat was varied; in only two of their preceding eight top-flight campaigns did they score more set-piece goals than the 14 they managed in 2025-26. It is very rare for a team to be so productive on both fronts.

Set for a breakthrough

It was a November night of ecstasy when Scotland qualified for the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, but for Ben Gannon-Doak it was a bittersweet evening and one that curtailed his club season. The 20-year-old was forced off after 21 minutes, replaced by Kenny McLean who capped the scoring in style. A £25m arrival from Liverpool last August, Gannon-Doak featured in all three of Scotland’s World Cup matches, starting the first and last, and has impressed in pre-season. After being limited to 113 minutes in eight league appearances as a substitute last campaign, there is optimism Gannon-Doak will make his mark.

World Cup impact

Rayan became the first Brazilian teenager to start a World Cup match since Marco Antônio in 1970 when he was named in Carlo Ancelotti’s starting XI for their Group C game against Scotland. The then 19-year-old, signed from Vasco de Gama in January, set up Vinícius Júnior for Brazil’s opener in the 3-0 win and afterwards swapped shirts with Gannon-Doak. Tyler Adams enhanced his reputation, impressing for the USA en route to the last 16. Two new members of Bournemouth’s coaching staff, the set-piece coach, Nicolas Gagnon, and goalkeeping coach, Frederic de Boever, worked with Canada and Belgium respectively. Alex Scott’s inclusion in Tuchel’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida spoke volumes of the Guernsey-born midfielder’s wider standing.

Sports.title: League Two 2026-27 preview: the contenders, hopefuls and strugglers
Sports.content:
Contenders

Salford meekly lost the playoff final and that was the end of days for Karl Robinson as he was sacked. Peter Cklamovski was not the obvious replacement, but the Australian left behind the Malaysia national side for a crack at League Two with the rebranded Ammies, who are back in their traditional orange. Macaulay Langstaff has arrived with the task of providing the goals to finally get Salford up and few would bet against the striker.

Chesterfield fell short in the playoffs, too, but Paul Cook remains one of the best managers at this level, although the loss of Armando Dobra could be significant. Securing the veteran forward Andy Cook was important for Grimsby as they seek to push on and his influence could be telling if he plays enough games. Lee Grant did not get much chance to prove himself at Huddersfield so will be desperate to do so at Walsall, especially after a promising start by knocking Championship side Bristol City out of the EFL Cup. The former goalkeeper will be hoping he is the man to ensure the Saddlers do not stop playing in winter, as has been the case in recent years.

Of those who have dropped down, Rotherham are the more intriguing bet, having brought in Steve McClaren as director of football and Alex Bruce as head coach in an attempt to revitalise the club. Losing Sam Nombe was a blow, but his transfer fee should allow investment. Jon Brady knows what he is doing and could do nothing to keep Port Vale up, but arguably has the most complete squad at this level with Max Watters and Kyle Dempsey standout summer signings.

View image in fullscreen Rotherham will hope to utilise the experience of their director of football Steve McClaren to bolster their chances of promotion into League One. Photograph: WhiteRosePhotos/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Hopefuls

An end‑of‑season slump kept Crewe out of the playoffs last time round, but the returns of Luke Offord and Joe White provide much‑needed quality. Barnet were two points off eighth having returned to the EFL and have kept their developing squad together – apart from Ryan Glover who was sold to Stockport – to give Dean Brennan real belief that his side can improve. Oldham made a steady return to the fourth tier and have added the guarantee of Elliott Nevitt’s goals alongside Oliver Norburn, who was a key member of the Notts County side that went up from this division.

Colin Kazim-Richards has his feet fully under the table at Crawley and has overseen one of their traditional busy summers in an attempt to avoid a relegation battle. The former Sunderland goalkeeper Vito Mannone was an eye‑catching signing, while the talented Malcolm Ebiowei will be aiming to turn his career around. If these two shine, it could make them a surprise package. Relegation and problems off the pitch have put Exeter on a downward spiral, which does not look like being arrested without further incomings. “Absolute tinpoint garbage” was Ian Holloway’s view of Swindon’s friendly performance against Bristol City, which suggests the team still have levels to go. Gareth Ainsworth wants high‑pressing Gillingham to maintain energy levels over the course of the campaign to give them an outside chance of challenging.

George Burley’s son-in-law Chris Hogg joined Northampton in May for his first managerial role and, after sunning himself in Greece, is primed to test himself, but the Cobblers may rue the departure of Cameron McGeehan as they aim to rebuild after relegation. Gavin Cowan transformed Shrewsbury from no-hopers to comfortably staying up but he faces a tricky second album.

John Terry is not the Colchester owner, as the sale of the club rumbles on without a solution. Steve Evans will ensure Bristol Rovers are competitive, but whether that means they can push themselves higher than 14th place last season remains to be seen.

Strugglers

The promoted teams start on the backfoot after managerial changes, as Rochdale lost Jimmy McNulty, while York decided to sack Stuart Maynard midway through preseason, much to the consternation of the fans. Diligence in recruitment, however, gives them optimism, especially Dale bringing back Cian Hayes.

Tranmere survived by a couple of points last time round but will be hoping for an uplift under Darrell Clarke, who has persuaded Will Vaulks and the former Watford winger Tom Ince that Prenton Park is a sensible place to continue their careers. Newport County were also forced into a change in the dugout when Christian Fuchs decided Rodney Parade was not the place he wanted to call home having kept the team up, leaving the club in flux as Chris Todd oversaw preparations for the campaign. The Exiles brought in plenty of experience in the shape of Harrison Biggins and Christian Doidge to strengthen the squad.

The inexperienced Matt Lawlor is set for a challenging first full season in charge of Fleetwood, who are boosted by the signing of Andy Cannon from Wrexham. Steve Cotterill revitalised Cheltenham almost a year ago, but five of their first six summer signings were relegated in May, which does not inspire confidence. After finishing comfortably in midtable, Accrington Stanley may not fear the drop and Cole Stockton is a clever signing but there is a nagging doubt about the club’s efficacy.

View image in fullscreen Managerial inexperience may prove challenging for Matt Lawlor (left) who has much to prove in his first full season at Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Phil Oldham/Shutterstock

Ones to watch

Maldini Kacurri, Grimsby, 20 After starting last season on loan at doomed National League side Morecambe, the Albania international may have wondered if life outside Arsenal was really for him. The defender shone when he stepped up to League Two with Grimsby, guided by David Artell, proving himself capable of coping with the physicality in the lower tiers.

Patrick Mlynarski, Crewe, 18 A Wales youth international, the recently-turned 18-year-old is now in his first year as a professional. The winger made his debut in the EFL Trophy last season, but is yet to feature in the league. Previously part of Everton’s academy, Mylnarski is skilful and powerful, playing on the left, possessing the ability to cut in or beat defenders on the outside.

Will Gray, Shrewsbury, 17 The midfielder made four starts last season and signed his first professional contract in the summer. His manager, Gavin Cowan, has praised his mentality and ability to keep things simple in the centre of the park.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
A consortium including the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, is close to completing a deal for a 30% stake in Liverpool after months of talks with Fenway Sports Group. The investors are led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and who previously was a shareholder and director at Queens Park Rangers.

The Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is another member of the group who will pay in the region of £1.35bn. The deal is effectively agreed, but may take up to a month to complete.

Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (£190bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world, while Saverin is reportedly worth $32bn. This will be Bezos’s first investment in football, but he has previously looked into bidding for NFL franchises. The 62-year-old will receive equity as part of the deal, which Deloitte has advised on.

Bezos is the executive chair of Amazon having relinquished day-to-day control when he stepped down as chief executive five years ago. Under his leadership, the online retailer has diversified into being an entertainment provider and has bought numerous sports rights for its streaming service.

Amazon had live UK rights for 20 Premier League games each season for six seasons until the end of last year and broadcasts the Champions League in several European countries, as well as some NFL games in the US.

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 and have overseen two Premier League titles. FSG sold 3% of the club to the US private equity firm Dynasty Equity in 2023.

It has been a summer of change at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach, Mohamed Salah left on a free transfer and has joined Trabzonspor and Michael Edwards departed his role as chief executive officer at FSG.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Marinakis sues Crystal Palace over fan banner
Sports.content:
The Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Crystal Palace for defamation after supporters of the south London club displayed a banner depicting him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Almost 12 months since the banner appeared midway through the first half of Palace’s 1-1 draw with Forest at Selhurst Park, lawyers for Marinakis lodged the claim for defamation against CPFC Ltd and “persons unknown” at the high court on Monday.

The banner showed the Greek shipping magnate pointing the gun at Gibbs-White, who had been set to join Tottenham last summer before Forest pulled out of the deal, and also featured the message: “Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match‑fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.” Marinakis has previously rejected all those allegations. Lawyers for Marinakis were approached for comment. A spokesperson for Palace did not comment.

Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association in February after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

Last summer, Palace and Forest were at loggerheads after Forest wrote to Uefa to voice their concerns that Palace could be in breach of multiclub ownership rules. The FA Cup winners ended up being demoted to the Conference League, with Forest – who had finished seventh in the Premier League and originally qualified for the Conference League – promoted in their place. Palace went on to win that competition under Oliver Glasner, while Forest reached the Europa League semi-finals.

Glasner has since joined Forest after leaving Palace at the end of his contract in a move that has surprised both sets of supporters. The Austrian said this week that Marinakis had persuaded him to change his mind over dinner in Athens after previously rejecting Forest because they were not in Europe next season.

“Then I had a more detailed look and there are two reasons why I changed my mind and I told him,” Glasner said. “No 1 is I think there is more potential in the squad than they have shown. And No 2 is you, it’s your ambition, because I am very ambitious.”

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille who value Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

Barcelona are confident of signing Rodri from City, but they will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint‑Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30‑year‑old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester player Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of securing a deal for the 18-year-old midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Marcus Rashford has joined United at their County Kildare training camp following the England forward’s post‑World Cup break. The 28-year-old has spent the past season and a half on loan at Barcelona and Aston Villa respectively, in the aftermath of a breakdown in his relationship with the club executive and the former United head coach Ruben Amorim. Relations have now eased and Rashford is focused on working under the United manager, Michael Carrick, although he could still leave before the end of the transfer window.

Sports.title: Are Manchester United returning to relevance under Michael Carrick? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Manchester United finally seem to have something that resembles stability in the dressing room under Michael Carrick. I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.

There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. United don’t have to have an especially amazing season to play 15 more games this season than they did in 2025-26.

That’s not to say that Carrick won’t be successful. There was much that he did last season that was very impressive. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans bolster an area of the squad that desperately needed to improve. A left-back seems almost certain to arrive before the end of the month and there’s probably the need for one more high-class experienced central defender. It’s not clear what Marcus Rashford’s future is after his return from loan at Barcelona, but he has two years left on his contract and could add dynamism and finishing to the left side of the attack. It’s probably not a title-winning squad, but it’s certainly one that should qualify for the Champions League.

Two questions remain that will only be answered as the season goes on. First, Carrick himself: can he cope with the churn of two games a week, and operating with a squad that is at least as fatigued as their opponents? And second, where is the club psychologically? Part of the problem for United, a familiar trait of big clubs who have fallen from grace, is that they have got into a routine of failure, that no success can ever quite be trusted, and every setback is seen as a further example of the terminal decline (although just as damaging would be suddenly believing everything is fine if United were to win, say, their first three games of the season). Retaining clarity of thought and making realistic assessments are perhaps the greatest challenges for a club that has known greatness but is struggling to return to those heights.

What do you see the broader impact of the VAR changes that Fifa made this year being? Do you think that other soccer leagues will see the increasingly automated, faster but less human approach taken by Fifa this summer and choose to adopt it? (I am aware that the Premier League has already chosen to reject much of it) – Dennis.

The most notable changes implemented before the World Cup allowed VAR to review and overturn incorrectly awarded corner kicks, certain attacking fouls and clear mistakes relating to red cards given from a second yellow. The only one of these adopted by the Premier League is to allow VAR to overturn a second yellow leading to a red (VAR cannot recommend that a referee should award a second yellow that would lead to a red). If we have to have VAR, that seems reasonable enough; nobody wants to see a team incorrectly reduced to 10 men.

At the World Cup, the corner issue only rarely came up, but it always seemed slightly odd that incorrectly awarded goal kicks could not be turned into corners. Personally, I would scrap VAR, or at least this form of it, but if incorrect decisions can be corrected quickly and unobtrusively then they probably should be. I understand, though, why the Premier League, aiming for a “light touch” – good luck with that – would be resistant.

Greater use of VAR, though, seemed to be the direction of travel. I suspect relatively soon offsides will be almost fully automated, which probably makes sense so long as it’s almost instantaneous. Whatever doubts there may be about margins of error and frame rates, it’s still going to be more accurate than a 40-year-old running the line 30 yards away, peering through a thicket of players.

More significant is probably the Premier League’s adoption of regulations against timewasting: speeded-up substitutions, players who receive treatment having to remain off the field for 60 rather than 30 seconds, an outfield player having to be withdrawn for 60 seconds after a goalkeeper receives treatment, and a five-second clock on throw-ins and goal kicks. All should speed up the game and improve the spectacle. It’ll be interesting as well to see the level of tolerance for grappling in the box, particularly by attacking players, which was an area in which the Premier League seemed out of step with the rest of Europe last season.

Which of the Premier League’s promoted sides have the best chance of staying up, and why? – Nicholas.

The achievements of Sunderland and Leeds last season, finishing seventh and 14th, will have heartened the promoted sides, but the truth is it will be extremely difficult for all three. Both those sides invested heavily in a way that is impossible for Coventry, Ipswich or Hull. It’s very hard to see how Hull, who were promoted unexpectedly, can survive. Coventry, perhaps, with the euphoria of their Premier League return and the Frank Lampard factor can give it a go, but their summer spending has been modest. Ipswich, with recent Premier League experience, have a chance and have made some intriguing signings in Daizen Maeda, Abdul Fatawu, Issa Diop and Chuba Akpom, but they’ve lost the manager who got them up, with Kieran McKenna opting for a break rather than another Premier League campaign. Gary O’Neil perhaps feels he has unfinished business, but if any of the promoted sides are to survive, they need another club to have a dreadful campaign.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of messing with his mental health after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, are understood to have agreed four-year contracts with the option of a further 12 months. They are expected to have medicals on Monday.

McNeil, who has entered the final year of his Everton contract, appeared to be moving to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season.

They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League, but then pulled out. McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, wrote an emotional post on Instagram saying there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been affected.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

Johnson has been disappointing since moving to Palace, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given he signed a four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid, but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.
