World.title: At least 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia
World.content:
At least 13 people have been killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on the Russian republic of Tatarstan, local officials have said.

They confirmed one child was among those killed, with 75 more people injured as drones hit Nizhnekamsk, more than 1,100 kilometres (680m) from the Ukrainian border. Ukraine's Armed Forces said the city's Tanevo oil refinery had been hit.

It is one of the deadliest single attacks on Russia since the start of Moscow's full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022.

Kyiv has recently stepped up its long-range strikes on facilities it says contribute revenue and logistics to Russia's war on Ukraine.

The strike on Nizhnekamsk lasted several hours overnight and into the morning, according to local sources.

Verified images on social media show large plumes of smoke and flames rising into the sky in daytime, with air raid sirens howling in the background.

The Uzkbek consulate in Tatarstan said seven of those killed were citizens of Uzbekistan.

According to Russian news agency RIA, most of the victims had been staying in a hostel at the time of the attack, and Russia's Investigative Committee said that "civilian individuals who were not involved in any military operations were present" where the drones struck.

The BBC has not independently verified this information. Moscow said that "all those involved in the attacks" would "face inevitable and severe punishment".

Oil refineries in Nizhnekamsk had already been hit once - on 12 June.

"The facilities Ukraine targets are used to carry out attacks against Ukraine, manufacture weapons, support Russia's war effort," said Andriy Kovalenko, head of the Ukraine's Centre for Countering Disinformation.

World.title: Netanyahu's rejection of Trump's 15-point Gaza plan unlikely to be final word
World.content:
In July, after months of delicate negotiations, Trump announced a "major milestone" in the implementation of his plan to end Israel's war in Gaza.

Writing on his Truth Social platform, Trump said that the Board of Peace had reached an agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups in the territory.

The deal is meant to be carried out in phases, with all weapons decommissioned and stored by a new Palestinian administration in Gaza â which reports to the Board of Peace - and Israeli forces withdrawing from the more than 60% of Gaza they currently control.

Senior Hamas officials confirmed that they had agreed to the new framework, conditioning it on mutual compliance by Israel. This was widely viewed as a major potential breakthrough in the conflict. The UK welcomed it and the European Union hailed it as a "crucial step".

However, for more than a week, Israel did not give its formal response.

An Israeli spokesman said only that the roadmap did not "reflect Israel's positions." A far-right member of the government, Itamar Ben-Gvir, wrote on X that the deal was "unacceptable."

Increasingly, mainstream Israeli opposition politicians also raised doubts. They questioned whether all small arms would be decommissioned and the sequencing of the plan.

Finally on Sunday, Netanyahu told his cabinet, "I wish to be precise here: Israel does not accept the 15-point document."

He added: "The IDF [Israel Defense Forces] will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed. And when I say the disarming of Hamas, it means heavy weaponry, lighter weaponry, all weaponry. And we are talking about genuine disarmament, not fictitious disarmament."

In the same statement, the prime minister described President Trump as "the greatest of our friends in the White House" but said that Israel knew "how to stand firm" against unacceptable ideas.

In Israel, there is widespread scepticism that Hamas intends to follow through on its commitments.

The Islamist movement has long seen "armed struggle" as a core precept, its legitimate response to Israeli occupation of Palestinian lands. In recent months, there had been signs of it reasserting its authority in Gaza.

"Israel can certainly never agree to retreating anywhere where the terrorist group that caused the worst massacres since the Holocaust is still there and is still ruling the Strip," Fleur Hassan-Nahoum, an Israeli commentator and former deputy mayor of Jerusalem told the BBC.

She stressed that the "trauma of the Israeli people" from the deadly Hamas-led attacks on 7 October 2023, which ignited the devastating Gaza war, should not be underestimated.

World.title: 'We've had a lot of close calls': Canada wildfire evacuees wonder if they still have homes
World.content:
Earl Kurz and his wife have lived in Peachland, a town overlooking Okanagan Lake in Canada's British Columbia, for 30 years. In the last 10, he said he has grown used to wildfires threatening his community.

But this is the first time he's been forced to flee, and surveying the damage left behind by the Bald Range wildfire, which broke out on Friday and grew in a matter of hours to 53 sq miles (136 sq km) in size, has been difficult.

"It's total incinerated destruction," Kurz said. "The hot spots are just barren areas of nothing except 12 inches of ash."

Officials in British Columbia are still trying to determine how many homes were lost to the fire, which remains out of control as of Monday.

World.title: 30 years later, a former gang member will stand trial for Tupac's murder
World.content:
It's been three decades filled with mystery, conspiracies - and anger.

The drive-by shooting that killed rap superstar Tupac Shakur on 7 September 1996 changed the trajectory of hip-hop and elevated the rapper from the face of the genre to a cultural icon.

His killing became one of popular culture's great mysteries, with countless theories but no arrests until 2023, when Duane "Keffe D" Davis was unexpectedly charged with murdering the famous rapper.

The 63-year-old former gang boss is due to stand trial in Las Vegas, where he is accused of murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang. He's pleaded not guilty. If convicted, he faces life in prison without parole.

The trial is likely to unravel the intricacies of the bitter and deadly East Coast vs West Coast rap rivalries and turf wars between the Bloods and the Crips street gangs that were immortalised in rap lyrics and news reports in the 1990s.

It could also include several celebrity witnesses - including Suge Knight, the former CEO of Death Row Records, who has been thought of as the last surviving witness to Shakur's death.

But the complicated case hinges almost exclusively on one key piece of evidence: a book co-authored by Davis that he has argued is partially a piece of fiction.

Jury selection in the case began on Monday, with opening arguments due to start on 17 August.

World.title: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has signed an order that calls for fewer childhood vaccines and also recommends splitting the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) shots.

"Decades ago, children received only a small fraction of the vaccines required today," Trump said. "In those times, people were much healthier and of course the high rates of autism now observed did not exist."

The president has long cast doubt on the safety of MMR vaccines, but multiple studies have found no connection between the shots and autism.

The order also recommends that the number of childhood vaccines drop to 11 from the existing 18 recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).

Trump's order serves as guidance, not a mandate, since shots required for school attendance are set at the state level, rather than by the federal government.

Speaking in the Oval Office on Monday, the president said his administration "is recognising gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases".

The immunisations recommended for all children under the order are for measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type B, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus, and varicella or chicken pox.

"We're reducing them," Trump said. "It's not only that you're doing fewer vaccines, or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor."

The president suggested the MMR vaccine could be "quite lethal" if given at once. He compared it to pouring a bottle of soda into a child's body.

When a reporter asked for evidence of the "lethal" claim, Trump said: "What I've heard is that there are some people that say it is that way."

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), external, the MMR vaccine carries a very small risk of febrile seizures for young children. Those with health issues, including severe allegeric reactions or weakened immune systems, are advised to consult with healthcare providers before taking the shots.

The agency says "most people who get MMR vaccine do not have any serious problems with it", and that getting the vaccine "is much safer than getting measles, mumps, or rubella".

According to the CDC, there is "no published scientific evidence that shows any benefit in separating the combination MMR vaccine into three individual shots".

Experts say that allowing time between jabs means children are more likely to contract diseases in the interim or that they are more likely to miss appointments if there are multiple shots.

Trump's Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F Kennedy Jr said the proposed changes were meant to give parents choice, not prohibit access to childhood vaccines.

Since taking office in 2025, Kennedy has sought to change and loosen vaccine regulations. During a tense 20-minute interview on CNN last week, Kennedy insisted he had "never questioned the efficacy of the MMR vaccine".

Trump administration officials have said the order means children in the US would receive much less than the 72 shots recommended under the previous vaccine schedule, a figure that assumes annual flu and Covid-19 doses.

Dr Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, said Trump's executive order was "dangerous" and not based on "gold-standard science".

"Delaying or skipping shots is risky, especially as measles continues to spread and children go back to school," Racine said.

Republican Senator Bill Cassidy, who was the deciding vote in the Senate to confirm Kennedy as health secretary, also admonished Trump's executive order on Monday, labelling it "wrong".

"The President does not have the expertise to make these changes," Cassidy, a physician, wrote on X. "Vaccines are overwhelmingly safe. Vaccines are effective. Vaccines DO NOT cause autism."

Experts fear that if parents refrain from getting their children vaccinated as a result of the discredited idea that childhood vaccines are linked to autism, it risks the re-emergence of diseases like measles.

Multiple studies have found no link between the MMR vaccine and autism. A recent high-quality study from Denmark in 2019 looked at 657,461 children and concluded that the data did not support the MMR vaccine causing or triggering autism.

On its website, the CDC recommends that two doses of the combined MMR vaccine be given to children, starting with the first dose at 12-15 months and the second between the ages of four and six.

How often and how many vaccines children in the US receive is based on the times when vaccines will work best with their immune systems and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases, according to the AAP.

There is no medical reason to delay or skip recommended immunisations, the AAP says.

Trump's order also calls for the development of alternatives to aluminium in vaccines, and to test if those alternatives are safer and more effective.

But the AAP, external says studies have found no significant health risks associated with the tiny amounts of aluminium salts in vaccines.

Small amounts of aluminium salts - which are found naturally in soil, water and foods - have been used in some vaccines for decades in order to boost the body's immune response.

That means lesser quantities of the vaccine and fewer doses are needed, according to AAP.

World.title: Another Nigerian star moves to Turkey ahead of historic Super Lig campaign
World.content:
Super Eagles winger Yira Sor has completed his move to newly promoted Turkish Super Lig side Amedspor from Belgian Pro League club Genk, becoming the second Nigerian international to join the club this summer.

Amedspor confirmed Sor’s arrival on Monday via an exciting video through its official social media platforms, welcoming the 26-year-old winger as he brings an end to months of uncertainty surrounding his future at Genk.

Sor had been expected to leave the Belgian club this summer after a difficult spell that was repeatedly disrupted by injuries.

The Nigerian joined Genk from Slavia Prague in January 2023 but struggled to establish himself consistently during his three-and-a-half-year stay in Belgium, with injury setbacks limiting his opportunities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

His move to Amedspor now offers Sor a fresh start as the newly promoted side prepares for its maiden campaign in the Turkish top flight.

The winger made his Super Eagles debut in March and will be hoping that regular football in Turkey can help him regain his best form and strengthen his position within the national team setup.

Sor reunites with fellow Nigerian Orban

Sor’s arrival means Amedspor will have two Nigerian attackers in their squad ahead of the club’s historic Super Lig campaign.

He will link up with fellow Super Eagles forward Gift Orban, who recently joined Amedspor on a season-long loan from Bundesliga outfit Hoffenheim.

Orban’s agreement includes an obligation for Amedspor to make the transfer permanent if the stipulated conditions are met.

The move brought an end to a period of uncertainty surrounding the striker, who had fallen out of favour at Hoffenheim following a loan spell at Italian club Hellas Verona.

Orban scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 Serie A appearances for Verona last season, although his individual contribution could not prevent the club from suffering relegation.

His move to Amedspor gives him another opportunity to revive his career, while Sor will also be looking to make a strong impression in Turkey after an injury-hit period at Genk.

Amedspor turn to Nigerian firepower

The arrivals of Sor and Orban provide Amedspor with a double dose of Nigerian attacking talent as the club prepares to compete in the Super Lig for the first time in its history.

Both players will be expected to play important roles as Amedspor attempt to establish themselves among Turkey’s top-flight clubs following their promotion.

Their moves also add to the growing number of Nigerian players heading to Turkey this summer, with Kelechi Iheanacho among the latest to make the switch after joining Turkish second-tier club Bursaspor.

For Sor, however, the immediate priority will be to stay fit, rediscover his form and make the most of a fresh opportunity with Amedspor as he looks to build on his Super Eagles breakthrough.

World.title: Mararaba-Nyanya bridge, road to be completed in December – Official
World.content:
The Nasarawa State Government has announced that the ongoing construction of the 2.6-kilometre Mararaba-Nyanya Flyover and adjoining road project is expected to be completed by December 2026.

The Managing Director of the Nasarawa State Urban Development Board, Wada Yahaya, disclosed this when he led members of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors National Media Tour, headed by the Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, on an inspection tour of critical infrastructure projects undertaken by the federal and state governments.

The tour provides an opportunity for state governments and project beneficiaries to highlight how ongoing economic reforms and improved fiscal capacity are enabling governments at the sub-national level to undertake and complete critical developmental projects.

According to Mr Wada, the Mararaba-Nyanya project, which covers approximately 2.6 kilometres, is designed to improve traffic flow, ease congestion and strengthen connectivity between the state and the Federal Capital Territory.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the state government is committed to ensuring that the project is delivered within the projected timeline, with December 2026 set as the completion date.

He explained that the project is part of the administration’s broader efforts to modernise the state’s urban infrastructure and provide efficient transportation corridors for residents, commuters and businesses.

“There were several attempts to solve this traffic problem in Mararaba, but at the end of the day, His Excellency, Governor Abdullahi Sule came up with the final solution and that is to provide a continuous flyover of 2.6 km long that will go over the challenging area without tampering with the business activities of the location, meaning we will have two flyover bridges and then connecting elevated road of 2.6km.

“We have five pedestrian bridges so that it will enable pedestrians to cross at any point without going all the way to the roundabout. That i what will provide the final solution to the challenges we are facing in Mararaba.

“The Mararaba project is costing the state government almost ₦40 billion. That’s the construction work alone and then we have the compensation of over ₦1.1 billion, followed by the cost of road furniture that will come up, which includes markings, signages and street light that we are also estimating may cost above ₦1 billion at the end of the project.

“In all, we will spend between ₦43 and N44 billion on the project. The project will enhance economic activities of the Mararaba area and the entire Nasarawa State because it will reduce the travel time from Abuja to Keffi from over two hours to less than 40 minutes.

“The governor wouldn’t have embarked on this project if the state is not getting enough funds from the federal government, and even as it is, we are the least in terms of revenue collection from the federal compared to other states. Yet, the governor is utilising the resources to get all these jobs done and any time the payment is due, His Excellency always approves the release of the funds without delay.”

The team also inspected several other landmark projects across the state, including the completed Lafia Flyover, Underpass and Interchange, the ongoing construction of the state-of-the-art Dalhatu Arab Specialist Hospital in Akwanga, and the construction of the Total Flyover Bridge and Underpass in Keffi, another strategic transportation project designed to address incessant road accident, traffic congestion and improve mobility within the commercial town.

Also inspected by the team is the completed Akwanga Interchange and Underpass, which represents another major investment in road infrastructure and urban mobility in the state.

The NUDB chief said the projects inspected demonstrate the growing emphasis on infrastructure renewal to support economic activities and improve the quality of life of Nasarawa people.

Briefing journalists at the end of the inspection tour of Benue and Nasarawa states, the Director of Media and Publicity of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors who is also the Senior Special Assistant to President Tinubu on Media & Special Duties, Tunde Rahman, expressed satisfaction with the way and manner the sub-national governments of Benue and Nasarawa states are responding to the yearnings and aspirations of their citizens with landmark infrastructure projects following increased federal allocation.

“We have now come to the end of our inspection tour of Benue and Nasarawa States. We have seen iconic road projects, we have seen bridges both by the federal government and the state government and we have seen interventions in healthcare, education and provision of water.

“It bears restating that what you have seen are some of the gains of the reforms undertaken by President Bola Tinubu as testified by Governor Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa and Governor Hyacinth Alia of Benue.

“When those reforms were initiated by the president, people were complaining that there were initial difficulties.

“But those difficulties soon gave way for benefits. And this flyover bridge in Mararaba is part of the benefit those reforms. Forget about the remonstration of the opposition who continue to claim that Mr President has not done anything. Seeing is believing; you have all seen for yourself.

“Somebody said in Nasarawa that Governor Abdullahi Sule had turned Nasarawa State into a huge construction yard. Same with Governor Alia of Benue State and I think that both governors have been very unanimous in stating that they were able to do what they did because the federal government reforms have freed resources to them and they now have more fiscal space to perform.

“You know that anybody that has done well in one term deserves to come back again for another term. Mr President has done well during this first term and he deserves to be re-elected in order to continue the work that he has done.

“Like I said, forget about the remonstration of the opposition. They continue to wallow in denial that Mr President has not done anything. From what you have seen across the states and in Abuja, Mr President has performed well and I think that Mr President deserves to be re-elected and I’m also here appealing to our people to look at the good work of Mr President, to look at the achievement of MrPresident and to let those achievements determine their voting decision when the time comes,” he concluded.

Tunde Rahman

Director, Media and Publicity

Renewed Hope Ambassadors National Media Team

August 10, 2026

World.title: Nigeria’s 650,000sq km rangelands threatened by degradation, desertification — Minister
World.content:
Nigeria’s 650,000-square-kilometre rangelands are facing increasing degradation, driven by desertification, agricultural and livestock expansion and overgrazing, the Minister of Environment, Balarabe Lawal, has said.

Mr Lawal, represented by Etim William, Director of the Desertification, Land Degradation and Drought Management Department in the ministry, raised the concern in Abuja on Monday while delivering a keynote address at Nigeria’s commemoration of the 2026 World Desertification and Drought Day.

The minister called for urgent action to restore degraded landscapes and strengthen Nigeria’s resilience to drought and climate change.

He said the degradation of rangelands, particularly in northern Nigeria, was undermining food security, increasing the vulnerability of rural communities and threatening the social and economic fabric of affected regions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Rangelands cover 650,000 square kilometres, largely in the northern states. They support most of Nigeria’s livestock sector; they are central to pastoral livelihoods, food security and rural economies,” Mr Lawal said.

He said a significant portion of the country’s rangelands had been degraded despite their importance to the economy and livelihoods of millions of Nigerians.

The United Nations marks World Desertification and Drought Day annually on 17 June. The 2026 global observance was hosted by Kenya under the theme, “Rangelands: Recognise, Respect, Restore,” in line with the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.

Nigeria held its national commemoration in Abuja on Monday as part of activities ahead of the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), scheduled to take place in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, from 17 to 28 August.

The Abuja event brought together representatives of government agencies, civil society organisations and environmental advocacy groups.

Link to farmer-herder conflicts

The minister said the degradation of rangelands had become particularly significant as Nigeria seeks sustainable solutions to persistent farmer-herder conflicts.

He linked the conflicts partly to shrinking grazing areas, climate change and drought, saying the United Nations’ designation of 2026 as the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists provides an opportunity to draw greater attention to the challenges facing the ecosystems and the communities that depend on them.

Mr Lawal said rangelands should not be regarded as “empty or unused lands” but as productive ecosystems that support communities, economies and cultures.

He called for greater recognition of pastoral communities and the incorporation of indigenous knowledge into efforts to manage and restore rangelands.

“The government is committed to reversing land degradation, restoring degraded rangelands and strengthening resilience against drought,” he said.

According to him, the government is scaling up programmes focused on ecosystem restoration, afforestation and reforestation, sustainable rangeland management, watershed restoration and community-based natural resource management.

He listed the Great Green Wall Initiative, the Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes (ACReSAL) project and the African Forest Landscape Restoration Initiative (AFR100) among the programmes being implemented.

Drought and land degradation threaten food security

Mr Lawal said desertification, land degradation and drought were imposing high costs on communities and economies, including threats to food security, soil productivity and biodiversity.

He warned that competition over dwindling productive land and access to clean water could further heighten tensions and conflicts among communities.

“Reversing desertification and mitigating the effects of drought cannot be overemphasised,” he said, adding that restoring degraded land could help sequester carbon, improve resilience to drought and climate change and create new green economic opportunities.

The minister said the 2026 World Desertification and Drought Day theme, “Rangelands: Recognise, Respect, Restore,” was particularly relevant to Nigeria because of the importance of rangelands to livestock production and rural livelihoods.

He urged governments at all levels to mainstream sustainable land management into their development plans and budgets.

He also called on traditional and community leaders to promote sustainable grazing, rotational pasture use and conflict-sensitive management of natural resources.

Farmers and pastoralists, he said, should adopt climate-smart practices that restore soil health and conserve water. At the same time, civil society organisations and the private sector should invest in land restoration, green jobs and sustainable value chains.

Government outlines priorities

Mr Lawal identified scaling up land restoration, expanding afforestation and reforestation, rehabilitating rangelands, strengthening drought preparedness and improving early-warning systems as immediate government priorities.

Other priorities, he said, include water harvesting, community contingency planning, supporting pastoral mobility and tenure security, recognising customary grazing routes and strengthening conflict-resolution mechanisms.

He also advocated sustainable livelihoods through agroforestry, sustainable livestock value chains and ecotourism, while urging the mobilisation of private-sector and international climate finance for long-term restoration and resilience.

The minister said Nigeria must invest in scientific research, innovation and capacity development to ensure that land-use practices improve soil fertility, conserve water, protect biodiversity and increase productivity.

He described the ceremonial tree planting held as part of the commemoration as more than a symbolic gesture, saying it represented a public commitment to translate environmental pledges into action.

“Let us recognise the value of our rangelands, restore degraded landscapes, and respect the natural systems that sustain us,” Mr Lawal said.

He said stronger collaboration among governments, communities, the private sector and development partners would help Nigeria build resilient landscapes capable of supporting sustainable livelihoods and inclusive national development.

In his remarks, CJID’s Executive Director, Akintunde Babatunde, who represented Ntiedo Ekott, said that, as a partner, the Centre is proud to support efforts to raise awareness and promote practical solutions to the growing challenges posed by land degradation, drought, and climate change.

“‎This year’s theme, “Rangeland: Recognise. Respect. Restore” is a timely reminder of the critical role rangelands play in supporting livelihoods, livestock production, biodiversity, food security, and the environment,” he said.

Mr Akintunde said recognising the value of rangelands is an essential step towards building resilient communities and sustainable ecosystems.

‎“‎Desertification and drought affect food security, livelihoods, and the resilience of communities, particularly those whose lives depend directly on agriculture and natural resources. Addressing these challenges requires collective action, stronger policies, sustainable land management, and meaningful community participation,” he said.

‎‎He reaffirmed CJID’s commitment to supporting initiatives that promote climate resilience, sustainable agriculture, environmental accountability, and informed public engagement.

World.title: I’m not lobbying to be APC, Tinubu’s campaigner DG – Wike
World.content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has debunked reports suggesting that he is lobbying to be appointed director-general (DG) of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC).

Mr Wike made the rebuttal in a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, on Monday in Abuja.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that a report by some sections of the media had listed the minister among top party members and government officials lobbying or being mentioned for the position of the APC presidential campaign DG.

Reacting, the minister, who is a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) but serving in the APC-led federal government, described the report as false saying, ”I did not at any time discuss leadership or even membership of the PCC with anyone.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He reiterated his unflinching support for the reelection of President Bola Tinubu, adding that he does not need to be the DG or even member of the PCC to ensure the reelection of Tinubu in Rivers and FCT.

“I am currently outside Nigeria, resting and relaxing after spending over 30 days inaugurating completed and new projects, and inspecting ongoing ones, especially those scheduled for commissioning in December and January.

“When I return, our focus will be the continuous delivery of our mandate in line with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda and to further enhance his electoral fortunes in Rivers and the FCT.

“Therefore, I do not need to be the DG or even member of the Presidential Campaign Council of Mr President’s political party to contribute my quota.

”I will ensure that Tinubu wins with wide margins in Rivers and the FCT,” Mr Wike said.

World.title: Heirs Life Assurance appoints Pastor Jerry Eze as Non-Executive Director
World.content:
Heirs Life Assurance, the specialist life insurance company of Heirs Insurance Group, has appointed Pastor Jerry Eze as an Independent Non-Executive Director on its Board, effective 10 August 2026.

The appointment reinforces Heirs Life Assurance’s commitment to expanding financial inclusion and accelerating insurance adoption by strengthening public trust, consumer education, and long-term financial resilience across Nigeria.

Despite being Africa’s largest economy, Nigeria’s insurance penetration remains below one percent – among the lowest globally – highlighting the need to expand financial protection and build greater public trust in insurance. As Heirs Life continues to pursue its mission of making insurance accessible to every Nigerian, Eze’s appointment brings a unique perspective on community engagement, value-based leadership, and broad societal impact.

Pastor Jerry Eze is the Founder and Lead Pastor of Streams of Joy International Ministry, a growing multinational ministry with 34 branches across West Africa, Southern Africa, Europe and North America. He is also the convener of the New Season Prophetic Prayers and Declaration (NSPPD), one of the world’s largest digital prayer platforms, reaching millions of people daily. Through his ministry and humanitarian initiatives, he has become one of Africa’s most influential voices, championing hope, compassion, and community transformation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Beyond ministry, Eze is the Founder of the Jerry Eze Foundation, a faith-led philanthropy where he provides housing support and grants to vulnerable and underserved communities. In 2026, he announced N1billion in grants to support young entrepreneurs across agriculture, technology, and manufacturing, further advancing enterprise development and economic opportunity.

Before entering full-time ministry, Pastor Jerry Eze built a career in development communications, serving as a Communications Specialist on a World Bank HIV/AIDS programme and with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).

He holds a Bachelor’s degree in History and International Relations from Abia State University and a postgraduate degree in Business Administration from Enugu State University of Science and Technology.

Speaking about the appointment, Tony O Elumelu, Chairman, Heirs Life Assurance, said:

“Pastor Jerry brings an exceptional combination of integrity, influence, and a deep understanding of people and communities. As we continue our mission to democratise access to insurance, his insight will help strengthen consumer trust, deepen financial inclusion, and reinforce our commitment to protecting the financial future of millions of Nigerians. We are delighted to welcome him to the Board of Heirs Life Assurance and the broader family of Heirs Insurance Group.”

Commenting on his appointment, Pastor Jerry Eze said:

“I am honoured to join the Board of Heirs Life Assurance at a defining moment for the insurance industry. Financial security empowers individuals, families, and businesses to pursue their aspirations with greater confidence and resilience.

“I look forward to working with the Board and Management to advance the company’s mission of making insurance more accessible, relevant, and impactful for every Nigerian”.

Heirs Life Assurance has become one of Nigeria’s leading specialist life insurance companies, ranking 7th on the Financial Times list of Africa’s fastest-growing companies. It is one of the three insurance businesses of Heirs Holdings, the leading pan-African investment company, with investments across 24 countries and four continents.

Combining an omni-channel digital presence with physical branches spread across the country, Heirs Life continues to redefine life insurance through innovation, customer-centric solutions, and a commitment to making financial protection accessible to every Nigerian.

Heirs Insurance Group, comprising Heirs Life Assurance, Heirs General Insurance, and Heirs Insurance Brokers, collectively serves over 3 million people directly and indirectly. The Group is championing financial inclusion and leading the digital insurance play in Nigeria, demonstrating its mission to democratise access to insurance.

World.title: Delta govt suspends works commissioner, gives reasons
World.content:
The Delta State Government on Monday suspended the State Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads) Reuben Izeze, for allegedly assaulting his aide, Simon Mudi.

The suspension notice is contained in a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Kingsley Emu in Asaba.

The suspension is linked to a viral video of a fracas at the Petroleum Training Institute (PTI), Effurun, in July during a Delta Central Stakeholders meeting of the All Progressives Congress.

Although the fracas did not take place in the APC meeting hall, the governor’s aide was assaulted on the premises after the meeting, prompting Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to order an investigation into the matter.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

As earlier reported by PREMIUM TIMES, the video shows participants fleeing in panic as several men pursued Mr Mudi, also known as “Temple,” striking him on the head with bottles and throwing chairs at him while he attempted to escape.

Mr Mudi was later seen in the clip dressed in an APC-branded safari receiving treatment in a hospital with visible bruises and a bloodied head.

Although the immediate cause of the attack could not be independently established, the violence underscored growing concerns that political tensions could escalate as parties begin positioning for the 2027 elections.

Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, who recently defected from the APC to the National Democratic Congress (NDC), said the incident reflected an emerging pattern of political violence in Delta.

In a statement issued by his spokesman, Godwin Anaughe, Mr Omo-Agege described the assault as “political thuggery”.

“A meeting of leaders from a registered political party was violently broken up, and a serving government official was assaulted with dangerous weapons in broad daylight. That this could happen at all says something deeply troubling about where Delta State’s politics is headed,” he said.

Mr Omo-Agege alleged, without presenting evidence, that the attackers were sponsored. He also linked the incident to an earlier alleged attack on NDC governorship candidate in the state, Chris Iyovwaye, who he claimed was prevented by hoodlums from entering his hometown of Agholokpe.

Claiming both incidents were connected, he alleged that the APC was preparing “a coordinated campaign of violence and intimidation” ahead of the 2027 elections to suppress opposition strongholds.

The former deputy Senate president called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Commissioner of Police in Delta and the State Security Service to investigate the incidents, prosecute those responsible and ensure a peaceful political environment before the next general election.

The Delta State Government had rejected the allegations, insisting that the incident should not be exploited for political purposes.

READ ALSO: Ten oil spills recorded in Niger Delta in July

Why Delta govt suspended commissioner – SSG

The SSG, Mr Emu said the decision to suspend the works commissioner was taken to allow security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into the incident.

He said the state administration remained committed to maintaining public safety, law and order, and to protecting the sanctity of human life.

According to the SSG, these principles will be upheld even when state institutions are involved.

He said the suspension is indefinite, pending the outcome of the investigation.

(NAN)

World.title: Atiku, Mark Aregbesola rally Osun electorate for ADC ahead of Saturday’s governorship election
World.content:
Former Vice-President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, on Monday appealed to the electorate in Osun State to support the party in the 15 August governorship election.

Atiku made the appeal while speaking at the ADC campaign grand rally in Osogbo, the state capital.

He said the ADC represented the interests of Nigerians, recalling his long-standing political relationship with the people of the state.

Atiku said he had previously campaigned in Osun for Governor Ademola Adeleke and for his presidential bid, adding that the people had supported him on both occasions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This is the fourth time I am standing on this podium. Each time I stood here, you have given me your vote. I cannot forget that because your daughter is in my house.

“I came here for the current governor, and I told you, people, to support him, and you voted for him.

“I came here on my presidential campaign; you voted for me, and I can’t forget that,” he said.

Atiku expressed optimism that the large turnout at the rally was a sign of victory for the ADC in Saturday’s election.

“I thank you very much for your turnout, which is quite impressive, and that has given us optimism that in the next elections, we are going to win; you are going to win,” he added.

In his remarks, the National Chairman of the party, David Mark, said the gathering was to celebrate the party’s forthcoming victory at the poll.

Mr Mark urged voters to turn out en masse on Saturday to vote and protect their votes, warning that anyone who attempted to rig the election would not go unpunished.

“What we are here to do is celebrate the victory that we are going to come to the ADC on Saturday.

“Our presidential candidate is here with us, and this shows the love he has for this party. By the time we swear in Najeem Salam in November, we will be here again to march with you to the Government House.

“On Saturday, protect your votes. Don’t allow anybody to rig you out. They will not rig and get away with it,” he said.

Former governor of Osun State and National Secretary of the ADC, Rauf Aregbesola, said the party was genuinely committed to the welfare of the people.

Mr Aregbesola said governance must be about service, opportunity and restoring confidence in leadership.

He said the ADC represented the true heirs of the late Premier of Wedtern Region, Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive tradition of free education, quality healthcare and social welfare.

He added that the party would reintroduce school feeding across public primary schools and expand other social intervention schemes abandoned by successive administrations.

Mr Aregbesola stressed that good governance should be a continuum and that beneficial programmes should not be discarded because of political differences.

He described the party’s candidate, Najeem Salam, as the face of continuity and urged the electorate to elect him as the next governor of the state.

According to him, Mr Salam’s agenda includes re-establishing O’YES to employ 20,000 youths, reviving the O’MEALS school feeding programme, expanding mechanised agriculture, and investing in rural infrastructure and technology.

“This election is about the future of Osun. Quality education, youth opportunities, farmer prosperity, and a government that truly serves the people,” he said.

He urged voters to come out on Saturday and vote for the ADC, saying the party had the experience and blueprint to restore prosperity and dignity to the state.

The party’s candidate, Mr Salaam, promised that his administration would prioritise the wellbeing of the people.

He said all sectors would be improved, warning that the party would not allow any form of rigging in the election.

The ADC candidate also promised to create jobs for 20,000 youth within his first 100 days in office.

“On Saturday, nobody will be allowed to rig us out. What they did in Ekiti State will not happen here.

“If we win the election, I want to tell you that our electricity will be stable. We have a solution to that, and it is a promise.

“Education from the primary to the secondary school for our children will be free, and we will also ensure that we have a committee that will review the tuition fees in our higher institutions, with a plan to bring them down,” he said.

(NAN)

World.title: FCMB, stakeholders set out roadmap to move Nigeria’s health sector from survival to scale
World.content:
Nigeria’s healthcare sector needs more than additional funding to expand. It needs businesses capable of attracting capital, deploying it effectively and building institutions that can grow sustainably, healthcare stakeholders have said.

That challenge was at the centre of the inaugural First City Monument Bank (FCMB) Healthcare Summit in Lagos, where the bank unveiled a N20 billion Healthcare Fund to support private healthcare businesses.

The fund will provide financing to hospitals, clinics, diagnostic centres, pharmaceutical companies, pharmacies, maternity homes and other businesses across the healthcare value chain.

The summit, themed “Financing Growth: Unlocking Opportunity, Building the Future of Healthcare,” brought together policymakers, healthcare providers, investors, financial institutions and development partners to examine how more private capital can be channelled into Nigeria’s health sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

At the heart of the discussions was a persistent financing problem: healthcare providers struggle to access affordable, long-term capital, while lenders and investors often require stronger governance, financial reporting and business structures before committing funds.

“Healthcare is a social imperative and an economic priority,” FCMB Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Yemisi Edun said in remarks delivered by Executive Director, Corporate Services and Service Management Felicia Obozuwa. “Building a strong healthcare system requires patient, affordable and long-term capital.”

Mrs Edun said financing alone would not be sufficient. Healthcare businesses also need sound governance, capable leadership and strategic partnerships to build resilient institutions.

Through the new fund, FCMB plans to finance infrastructure expansion, medical equipment, working capital, technology adoption and other investments aimed at improving efficiency and service delivery.

The push for more private capital comes as the government increases public investment in healthcare and seeks to expand capacity across the sector.

Government investment

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, said more than N339 billion has been disbursed through the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund over the past 12 years.

Of that amount, N235 billion was disbursed in the last three years under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative, he said.

Mr Salako added that another N32.9 billion was recently disbursed to support more than 8,300 primary healthcare centres, while the government is targeting about 13,000 facilities nationwide.

Beyond healthcare facilities, the government is seeking to increase domestic production of medicines and medical equipment.

Under the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain, Nigeria is targeting local production of 70 per cent of medicines and medical devices by 2030.

Mr Salako also highlighted initiatives aimed at addressing electricity constraints in healthcare facilities and creating long-term procurement opportunities for local manufacturers.

Making healthcare businesses bankable

For private healthcare operators, however, access to affordable capital remains a major obstacle to expansion.

The President of the Healthcare Federation of Nigeria (HFN), Njide Ndili, said affordable, long-term financing is one of the biggest barriers facing private healthcare businesses.

She said experience from HFN’s partnership with the PharmAccess Medical Credit Fund demonstrated that healthcare small and medium-sized enterprises could become bankable when financing is combined with technical support, capacity building and quality standards.

The challenge, therefore, is not simply increasing the amount of money available to healthcare providers but ensuring that businesses are prepared to attract and manage investment.

HFN will work with FCMB to develop a framework for pre-qualifying eligible healthcare facilities and helping businesses become investment-ready.

The federation, which has more than 400 member organisations and 4,000 professionals, will support businesses in strengthening governance, financial reporting, management capacity and growth plans before accessing financing.

From survival to scale

Discussions at the summit examined how healthcare operators can move beyond managing day-to-day pressures and build institutions capable of attracting long-term investment.

Participants explored blended finance, alternative lending structures and public-private partnerships as possible mechanisms for attracting more domestic and international capital.

An executive discussion on building healthcare businesses that attract investment also highlighted the importance of sound business management, governance, risk management and clear growth strategies alongside clinical performance.

Four broad priorities emerged from the discussions: expanding access to fit-for-purpose capital, improving the bankability of healthcare businesses, strengthening public-private partnerships and increasing domestic capacity in pharmaceuticals, diagnostics and medical equipment.

FCMB’s N20 billion fund is positioned within that broader agenda, complementing government investment with private financing for businesses seeking to expand facilities, purchase equipment, adopt technology and improve service delivery.

The summit was organised in partnership with the Health Business Academy for Africa.

For stakeholders, the next challenge is translating the financing commitments and partnerships announced at the summit into stronger healthcare businesses and increased capacity across the sector.

The broader goal is to create a healthcare ecosystem in which stronger institutions, sustainable financing and strategic partnerships translate into greater access to quality healthcare for Nigerians.

World.title: WAFCON Shame! More reasons Tinubu should act fast on football
World.content:
By Tony Ubani, Jacob Ajom and Solomon Nwoke

Nigeria has suffered another embarrassing setback in football following Super Falcons’ narrow 1-0 defeat to the Indomitable Lionesses of Cameroon. Like the Super Eagles, the Super Falcons will now chart the course of an African World Cup playoff to determine their fate of playing in the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil as CAF’s tournament schedule gives the losing quarter-finalists another route, with two classification play-off matches scheduled for Thursday, August 13, in Casablanca.

It will be unimaginable if, for the first time since the beginning of FIFA Women’s World Cup in 1991, the country’s green-white-green flag fails to flutter among those of best women football playing nations in Brazil next year when the 2027 edition kicks off.

Regrettably, the Super Falcons’ 1-0 defeat is a true reflection of how ill-prepared the team was for the continental tournament, which the NFF knew would also serve as World Cup qualifiers.

The fall of the Super Falcons shows how low Nigerian football has declined under the present leadership of the Nigeria Football Federation headed by Alhaji Ibrahim Gusau. In other climes, heads would have rolled. But not in Nigeria.

In Italy, when the national football team, the Azzurri failed to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup the government of ‎Italy responded to the national team’s playoff elimination by demanding a total overhaul of the country’s football federation.

Sports Minister, Andrea Abodi, explicitly called for the resignation of Italian Football Federation, FIGC, President, Gabriele Gravina, while lawmakers demanded structural reforms and stricter limits on non-European Union, EU, players to help nurture domestic talent.

Abodi publicly stated that the FIGC President, Gabriele Gravina, should step down. Multiple lawmakers echoed this demand, stating that the leadership needed to be held accountable for the decline of Italian football.

Gravina resigned. He did not leave alone. He was joined by Italian national team delegation chief, Gianluigi Buffon and head coach, Gennaro Gattuso, both of whom stepped down. Gravin’s predecessor, Carlo Tavecchio had also resigned in 2017 when the Azurri failed to qualify for the 2018 World Cup.

Multiple national football association (FA) presidents also resigned in the immediate aftermath of their national teams failing to qualify for or exiting early from the World Cup.

Yasser Al-Misehal resigned as President of the Saudi Arabian Football Federation after the Green Falcons suffered a group-stage exit at the 2026 World Cup.

South Korea’s Chung Mong-gyu stepped down as President of the Korea Football Association following South Korea’s group-stage elimination at the 2026 World Cup.

Libyan Football Federation (LFF), President, Abdelhakim Al-Shalmani also resigned from his post for failure to qualify for the World Cup. While heavily linked to team disputes and travel controversies, the decision was announced during an assembly where he stated he did not want to be associated with the failure of Libyan sports .

Scotland also joined the list of countries that made managerial changes after Steve Clarke resigned following the nation’s group-stage elimination. During his tenure, Clarke guided Scotland back to major international tournaments and ended the country’s 28-year absence from the FIFA World Cup.

The Scottish Football Association paid tribute to the 62-year-old, acknowledged his contribution to rebuilding the national team despite the disappointment of the World Cup campaign.

The scale of resignations continued, especially during the last World Cup in the Americas. From Europe to Africa and Asia, coaches who arrived at the tournament with lofty ambitions, saw their tenures come to an abrupt end after failing to meet the expectations of their football-loving nations.

But nothing like that happened in Nigeria. The very officials who presided over the Super Eagles failure to qualify for two consecutive World Cups are currently campaigning vigorously for re-election into the board of the NFF.

Former captain of the Green Eagles and 1980 AFCON winner Chief Segun Odegbami has called on government to act fast and halt the forthcoming NFF elections because, “We must rid NFF of scavengers who have nothing to offer.”

He insisted, it was nothing personal. “It’s not an Odegbami project, it’s a national call to save our football from the stranglehold of scavengers who have nothing to offer other than what they grab in the process. If people decide to peep from the window, I’ll go all the way,” Odegbami said.

In sports, result is the only yardstick for measurement of failure or success. The question being asked by Nigerians is should the the present leadership of the NFF return based on the results on ground?”

Tana Ayejina, the Deputy Editor of Punch Newspapers said, “No. After destroying Nigerian football for over a decade, what else do they have to offer? To cause more damage? Almost every member of the present board was part of the former which Gusau took over from. That board failed to take Nigeria to the World Cup. This present board was given another simple chance of taking Nigeria to the World Cup and they failed. A World Cup with 48 teams, 10 from Africa and Nigeria was not there and you say you want to come back. To do what?” he asked.

“In sports, if you are good, you move on, but if you are not good, you quit,” said Adekunle Salami, a senior editor at New Telegraph Newspapers. “For the NFF board to have failed to qualify Nigeria for two consecutive World Cups, the U17 is not competing, U23 are nowhere and U20 are all failing in their various qualifiers and no longer as competitive as they used to be. We are not playing at the Olympics. Indeed, the question one is forced to ask is, what are they (the board) still doing?”

Things got worse Sunday night when the Super Falcons, 10-time African champions were eliminated by Cameroon from WAFCON in Morocco.

Salami urged Nigerians with the wherewithal to challenge the present board members in the coming election. “What I expect is that Nigerians who have the capacity to right the wrongs that have been committed against Nigerian football should challenge them”.

That means things must change. How does the change come about when the people who are resisting change are still in charge of affairs?”

A former chairman of the League Management Company (now NPFL) Rumson Baribote said, “If we were in a saner clime, those who are at the helm of affairs should have humbly stepped aside honourably and relinquished their positions, but not here.”

Ayejina said that instead of vying to return, members of the current board should resign en mass for failing Nigeria. “In Italy and other countries that failed to qualify for the World Cup, their FA members resigned. I expect that NFF members should resign instead of seeking another term.”

Writing for Saturday Sports Vanguard, Douglas Baye-Osagie reasoned, “for a board that controls the emotions of over 250 million Nigerians worldwide, there must be professionalism. It cannot be business as usual or a group of men with half-baked credentials. Football is a billion-dollar industry with massive job opportunities for our youths. It should not be administered by passion without substance.”

Continuing, Baye-Osagie wrote,” The rule book that governs NFF Board elections is designed to protect incumbents, not performance. Elections are decided by state FA chairmen. A small, compromised pool of voters. Most depend on the board for grants, FIFA/FIFA Forward trips, and survival. You cannot expect independence from people whose jobs depend on the incumbent.”

A former Nigeria international, Ifeanyi Udeze observed that it is almost impossible to unseat Gusau through the present election format. Said he, “It is nearly impossible for an ex-international to contest or win the election under the current rules. We have to call for a change in the NFF Statutes. But then, former players must unite and advocate for such a change to come through.” He pointed out that “They (former players) have the numbers, whether you like it or not. And all of them have passed a vote of confidence in Gusau.”

Udeze maintained that the concentration of voting power among the state FA chairmen makes it difficult for ‘outsiders’, particularly former players, to break into the NFF leadership.

Another former international, Edema Fuludu agrees with Udeze. “There is no level playing field in NFF elections as presently structured. Unless you are a fool, you can’t throw your hat into the ring to contest against the incumbent NFF president. From which constituency?” he asked. “All the 36 state FA Chairmen, plus FCT are under him. That gives him 37 votes out of 45 or so votes. There is no room for fair contest. As it is now, someone like Okocha or Odegbami can only get one vote if they want to contest ”

Fuludu observed that the real actors – players, coaches and referees – whose roles necessitate the existence of administrators – were being ignored or schemed out in favour of those he called ‘outsiders’.

If Nigeria is serious about getting credible and knowledgeable leadership that can chart a noble path for our football, government must act now.

Reactions from governments whose teams even qualified for the World Cup but didn’t shine in the first round, have shown that the silence of Nigerian government over our back-to-back non-qualification is suspicious. The silence has emboldened the NFF leadership to launch an unbridled campaign train never witnessed before in NFF elections.

Ibrahim Gusau, the NFF President has been buying a lot of media space, moving from one geopolitical zone to another seeking endorsement, which he readily gets and telling Nigerians that he was not responsible for Super Eagles’ failure to qualify for the World Cup. Despite numerous court injunctions against his board, Gusau has since fixed September 26, 2026 for his anticipated re-election in Lafia, Nasarawa State.

Odegbami said, “The elections will be conducted away from any prying eyes to avoid any chances of transparency, and where bribery and corrupt practices can be conducted without consequence, far from the headquarters of the federation and the supervising National Sports Commission that would have ensured neutrality.”

In contrast, Saudi Arabia’s early FIFA World Cup exit prompted their federation chief to resign.

“The failure of the national team to qualify for the next round of the World Cup is a result that falls short of all our ambitions, and I bear full responsibility for it. I offer my apologies to everyone who hoped to see our team in a better position,” Yasser al-Misehal wrote before throwing in the towel.

“A sense of responsibility requires giving the opportunity to open a new chapter, and I have decided not to continue,’’ he added. That is leadership and responsibility. Why don’t we, in this part of the world take responsibility and accountability as part of the burden thrust upon leaders, an inextricable aspect of leadership?

In the case of South Korea, following their shock elimination from the group stage of the World Cup, President Lee Jae-myung publicly apologised to the nation and ordered the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism to launch a full-scale government investigation into the Korea Football Association, KFA.

The government’s rapid intervention brought great relief to the people as they try to fashion a way of making progress with fresh and progressive minds.

The country’s leader said he felt “not just confusion but utter bewilderment at the unexpected outcome,” He added that the early exit “appears to be a failure of organisation and personnel.”

The government rebuked the football authorities and took prompt actions. Keeping quiet like the Nigerian government has done, could imply consent.

World.title: ‘I never said military should reject salary increase’ — Peter Obi
World.content:
File image

Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has denied reports that he asked members of the Nigerian military to reject any salary increase until after the 2027 general election.

Obi described the report as false, saying it misrepresented his position on the welfare and remuneration of security personnel.

The former Anambra State governor made the clarification in a statement posted on his official X account on Tuesday.

“I Never Said Military Should Reject Salary Increase,” Obi said, urging Nigerians to disregard the report.

“I wish to address a recent report that falsely attributes a statement to me, suggesting that Nigerian soldiers should refuse any salary increments until after the elections. This assertion is entirely untrue,” he said.

Obi said he had consistently advocated improved welfare, equipment and protection for members of the security forces, particularly soldiers serving in difficult conditions.

“My profound respect for our security forces, particularly the Nigerian Army personnel who diligently serve and protect our nation under challenging conditions, is unwavering,” he said.

He recalled his previous concerns over the deaths of soldiers during security operations, particularly an incident involving what he described as a delayed rescue effort.

“My concern was palpable when soldiers were lost to insurgents due to a delayed rescue effort, prompting me to question how those defending us could be left vulnerable in their time of need,” he said.

Obi further pledged that the welfare and safety of military personnel would receive priority if he wins the 2027 presidential election.

“Should I be elected President, the well-being, resources, safety, and honour of our soldiers will be a paramount priority,” he said.

He added that security personnel deserved the government’s full backing, stressing that those responsible for protecting the country “must never be relegated to a secondary concern.”

The NDC candidate urged Nigerians to dismiss the report, describing it as misleading, while reaffirming his commitment to presenting what he called a clear vision for a secure and prosperous Nigeria.

“I implore the Nigerian populace to dismiss this misleading report. I remain committed to articulating a clear and consistent vision for a secure and prosperous Nigeria,” Obi said.

World.title: Low import bill pushes Nigeria’s trade surplus to $3.46b
World.content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

Driven by an 18.7 percent decline in import bill, Nigeria’s trade surplus rose by 32.06 percent month-on-month (MoM) to $3.46 billion in April 2026 from $2.62 billion in March 2026.

The Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, disclosed this yesterday in its April 2026 Economic Report.

CBN said: “The goods account recorded a higher trade surplus, mainly driven by a decline in import bill. Provisional data showed that the trade account recorded a surplus of $3.46 billion, compared to $2.62 billion in the preceding month.

“The performance was driven by 18.70 per cent decrease in import bills to $3.13 billion from $3.85 billion in March, as imports of both oil and non-oil products declined.”

Export receipts increased by 1.85 per cent to $6.59 billion from $6.47 billion, owing to higher non-oil export earnings.

In a breakdown of the trade receipts by composition, CBN said that oil exports accounted for 85.41 per cent of total export receipts, while non-oil exports constituted the balance.

In terms of imports, non-oil imports accounted for 81.75 per cent, while oil imports made up the balance.

On oil export, CBN said: “Oil export earnings moderated during the review period, driven by lower receipts from gas and refined petroleum product exports.

“Aggregate oil export earnings fell slightly to $5.62 billion in April, from $5.70 billion in March.

“A breakdown shows that receipts from gas exports and refined petroleum product exports decreased to $0.84 billion and $0.79 billion, respectively, compared with $0.86 billion and $1.35 billion in the preceding month.

“In contrast, receipts from crude oil exports increased to $3.99 billion, from $3.49 billion in March, driven by higher global crude oil prices.”

The apex bank noted that Non-oil export earnings improved in April, owing to a rise in global commodity prices.

“Earnings from non-oil products exports increased to $0.96 billion from $0.77 billion, driven largely by improved export receipts from cashew nuts and fertiliser.

“Analysis of Nigeria’s top 10 non-oil export destinations indicated India as the leading destination, accounting for 16.51 per cent, followed by Vietnam (10.96 percent), the US (8.71 percent), China (8.48 percent), and Germany (5.88 percent)”

On imports, CBN said: “Merchandise imports decreased, driven by lower oil and non-oil imports.

“A disaggregation showed that non-oil imports decreased to $2.56 billion from $2.81 billion in the preceding month, due to a decline in imports of agricultural goods and raw materials.

“Similarly, oil import fell to $0.57 billion from $1.05 billion, owing to increased domestic refining capacity.”

World.title: Customs targets N11trn through Adeniyi’s technology-led reforms
World.content:
Adewale Adeniyi Comptroller General of Customs

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) says it is on course to meet its ₦11 trillion revenue target for 2026, driven by technology-led reforms, improved trade facilitation and stronger border security.

The Comptroller-General of Customs, Dr Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this in a compendium obtained by News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).

He attributed the performance to automation, intelligence-led enforcement and stronger collaboration with stakeholders.

Adeniyi said that the service generated ₦4.03 trillion in the first half of 2026 alone.

He noted that the figure represented a significant jump compared to what was obtained in the same period in 2025 and put the NCS well ahead of its mid-year projections.

According to him, the improved performance is anchored on the deliberate removal of human discretion from core customs processes.

He said that the Service had replaced manual interventions with standardised rules, risk-based systems, and automated valuation references to block leakages.

“Modernisation within the Service is aimed at replacing officers’ discretion with standardised rules, risk-based systems, automated valuation references, and data-driven targeting to reduce vulnerability in customs operations.

“We removed human discretion, deployed technology, and built trust with compliant traders. When you do that, revenue will grow exponentially without hurting business,” he said.

To further improve efficiency, he said the NCS had adopted Time Release Studies as a tool to measure and reduce cargo clearance times at ports and borders.

The comptroller-general noted that the data-driven approach has been helping to cut delays, lower costs for businesses, and improve Nigeria’s ranking in global trade facilitation indexes.

On the security front, Adeniyi said that customs was deepening inter-agency collaboration to tackle smuggling, illicit financial flows, and wildlife trafficking.

“The NCS is working closely with the Army, Navy, DSS, EFCC, and NFIU in coordinated operations across land, sea, and air borders,” he said.

He listed some of the security gains, including the interception of pangolin scales, ivory, and other wildlife products, as well as the disruption of syndicates involved in cross-border crimes.

He said intelligence-led enforcement has become the new standard for the Service.

Speaking on the broader mandate of the Service, Adeniyi said that customs was evolving beyond revenue collection.

“The Nigeria Customs Service is not just about collecting duties.

”We are facilitators of trade, generators of data for national planning, and gatekeepers against smuggling.

“Our job is to ensure that Nigeria’s borders work for Nigeria – for revenue, for security, and for prosperity,”he said.

World.title: UN decries children exposure to unregulated AI, online harms
World.content:
The United Nations has urged governments and technology companies to urgently protect children from growing online risks.

The UN also called on advertisers, media organisations and researchers to prioritise children’s safety and participation in shaping digital policies.

It said young people increasingly faced disinformation, online harassment, algorithmic bias and the malicious use of Artificial Intelligence.

The warning was contained in a new UN brief released ahead of International Youth Day.

According to the report, more than eight in 10 young people aged between 15 and 24 worldwide are now online.

It said internet use among young people in low-income countries was almost twice that of the general population.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres had earlier called for an AI Child Safety Pledge to strengthen protection for children.

Guterres compared emerging artificial intelligence systems to untested medicine, warning against exposing children to poorly regulated technologies.

“No child should be a guinea pig for unregulated AI,” Guterres said, adding, “When a child is harmed, the answer must never be ‘the algorithm did it.”

The UN brief said many online harms affecting children were not accidental but partly due to business models designed to monetise attention, personal data, engagement and online spending.

The report identified algorithms encouraging prolonged use and manipulative digital designs among the major risks confronting young people.

It also highlighted “dark patterns”, loot boxes and other techniques capable of encouraging compulsive online behaviour.

The UN warned that children were particularly vulnerable because their habits, identities and relationships were still developing.

The risks include AI-generated harmful content and the use of artificial intelligence to facilitate exploitation.

The report also raised concern about increasingly hidden advertising techniques targeting children and encouraging online spending.

“Taken together, these practices normalise pervasive commercial surveillance and manipulative design,” the brief said.

It added that children were being exposed during some of the most impressionable years of their development.

The UN, however, stressed that children and young people should not be viewed only as victims of online risks.

It described them as creators, organisers, journalists, advocates and participants in public debate.

The report said youth-led movements continued to influence civic life and public conversations across different societies.

However, it warned that online spaces could also expose young organisers to harassment, intimidation and surveillance.

The UN, therefore, urged governments and researchers to include young people in policymaking on information integrity.

Charlotte Scaddan, UN Senior Adviser on Information Integrity, said children could contribute significantly to solving the digital information crisis.

“Protecting them and including them are not competing goals. We have to do both,” Scaddan said.

The report proposed legal and policy measures for Member States to strengthen online child protection.

It also urged technology companies to design platforms with stronger child-safety safeguards.

Advertisers were advised to respect children’s rights and avoid exploitative commercial practices.

The UN also called on news organisations to better serve young audiences and promote reliable information.

World.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, August 11, 2026
World.content:
The naira traded around ₦1,368 to the US dollar in the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, as the Central Bank of Nigeria’s reference rate continued to hover within the ₦1,360–₦1,370 range.

Data from the CBN and FMDQ showed the NFEM rate at about ₦1,368.22 per dollar, while the broader market benchmark remained around ₦1,368.37/$, indicating little movement from the previous trading session.

At the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the dollar was quoted at about ₦1,405 on Tuesday, leaving a gap of roughly ₦37 between the official and street rates.

The current spread suggests that pressure in the retail foreign exchange segment remains moderate, with the premium staying far below the wide differentials seen during periods of heightened volatility in 2024 and 2025.

The CBN maintains that the NFEM rate is determined using a volume-weighted average of transactions conducted in the official market, following the unification of Nigeria’s exchange-rate windows. FMDQ continues to publish daily market data for the Nigerian Autonomous Foreign Exchange Market (NAFEM), which serves as the benchmark for official dollar transactions.

Currency traders said demand from importers and manufacturers remained steady, while improved FX liquidity from autonomous sources helped keep the official rate relatively stable.

For individuals and businesses, the applicable exchange rate may vary slightly depending on the bank, bureau de change, transfer platform, or location of the transaction.

World.title: Visa application from Nigerians to S’Africa double despite xenophobic attacks—Envoy
World.content:
By Nkiruka Nnorom

South Africa’s Consul-General in Nigeria, Prof. Bobby Moroe, has said interest in his country remained high, with visa applications from Nigerians almost doubling in recent months, despite the persistent reports of xenophobic attacks.

Moroe stated this in an interview on Nigeria Info FM on Sunday, insisting that South Africa remained safe and opened for tourism, business and other forms of travel.

The reassurance came amid renewed concerns over xenophobic attacks in South Africa, where Nigerians and other African migrants have in recent months been targeted in pockets of violence across Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and parts of the Western Cape.

The attacks, often fuelled by claims of job competition and criminality, led to looting of shops owned by foreigners, assaults and forced displacements, sparking outrage in Nigeria and across the continent.

In response to the escalating violence, the federal government said it facilitated the repatriation of over 1,400 Nigerians who were stranded or feared for their safety in South Africa.

Moroe revealed that the surge in applications showed Nigerians still see South Africa as a viable destination despite safety concerns.

The Consul-General dismissed claims circulating online that South African missions in Nigeria had stopped issuing visas to Nigerians, describing the reports as untrue.

“I just want to give reassurance that South Africa is open for business, South Africa is open for tourism, and South Africa is open for any other form of visit. And it is also untrue to suggest that South African missions in Nigeria do not offer visas to Nigerians anymore.

“But I can assure you and the listeners, that it is safe to travel to South Africa. I indicated during the beginning of the show that the number of visa applications have almost doubled,” he said.

Moroe urged prospective travellers to obtain the necessary visas before departure and to respect South Africa’s immigration laws.

“It is everybody’s responsibility to ensure that before you travel, you ensure that you have your visa, you comply with the immigration laws of the country, you become a good ambassador of your country,” he advised.

He also cautioned Nigerians to familiarise themselves with South African laws, understand their rights, and know the locations of law enforcement agencies in case of emergencies.

“When you get to South Africa, you know and understand your rights, but you must also familiarise yourself with the laws of the country.

“You choose places that you want to visit… and ensure that you also are familiar with the location of law enforcement agencies, just in case something happens,’’ Moroe added.

The Consul-General expressed confidence that bilateral visits between both countries would continue to grow, stressing that South Africa valued its relationship with Nigeria.

World.title: Trump administration revokes over 175,000 visas in major enforcement sweep
World.content:
The United States has announced the cancellation of more than 175,000 visas issued to foreign nationals during the administration of President Donald Trump, citing alleged violations of visa conditions, criminal conduct and national security concerns.

In a statement released on Monday, the US Department of State said most of the visa revocations resulted from “law enforcement encounters involving criminal activity, with assault, driving under the influence, theft and drug-related offences among the leading causes”.

The department said additional cancellations were linked to “reckless driving, sexual assault, child abuse, fraud, embezzlement and other crimes”.

According to the State Department, the action was taken as part of its ongoing continuous-vetting programme, which is intended to ensure that visa holders comply with immigration rules and do not present a threat to the United States.

Officials said some affected individuals had been charged with serious offences, including “felony rape and sexual battery, kidnapping, human trafficking, sexual exploitation of minors, child sexual abuse offences and domestic violence”.

The department also disclosed that a US embassy in North Africa revoked more than 100 visas issued to parents accused of participating in “birth tourism” by travelling to the United States primarily to give birth so their children could obtain American citizenship.

Other cases cited by the department involved a foreign national arrested for allegedly driving with heroin while having a blood alcohol level more than three times the legal limit, as well as individuals accused of fraud and other financial crimes.
