World.title: Trump signs executive order calling for fewer childhood vaccinations
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

U.S. ‌President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Monday calling for fewer childhood vaccinations by limiting the inoculation schedule to 11 immunizations, ‌which he said would give U.S. children "gold-standard" protection and align the country with peer nations that recommend fewer shots.

The order advances a long-standing goal of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an anti-vaccine activist who has promoted a link between vaccines and autism that scientists have repeatedly debunked.

Public health experts say the U.S. schedule reflects decades of evidence and the specific health needs of Americans, and that fewer recommended ​shots will leave more children exposed to preventable diseases.

The order also ​recommended splitting the childhood measles, mumps ​and rubella vaccine into three shots and delivering the shots at separate medical visits.

Kennedy ​had in January cut the U.S. immunization schedule to remove shots against six out of 17 diseases — a move halted ​by a federal court ruling. The Trump order says ⁠that the federal ⁠government will now only support the ‌remaining 11 shots.

'This executive order ​is wrong'

The American Academy of Pediatrics and vaccine-maker Merck criticized the order.

"We are evaluating our next steps," said Richard Hughes IV, lead counsel for ‌the American Academy of Pediatrics, which sued earlier this year over Kennedy's changes to the childhood immunization schedule.

A nurse prepares to inoculate a child in Easley in March 2026. (Mary Conlon/The Associated Press)

Merck said there is no published scientific evidence showing any benefit to splitting the combination MMR shot into three, and that using the individual components increases the number of injections and can lead to delayed or missed immunizations.

"Effective immediately, my administration is recognizing gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations ‌for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases, along with the MMR, which hopefully will be split up," Trump said during ​a White House signing ceremony.

Demetre Daskalakis, former director of the CDC's National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, said breaking up combination vaccines and downgrading recommendations would deepen disparities and worsen vaccine coverage, warning that the resulting recommendations ‌in practice cannot be implemented.

Kennedy has previously led efforts to drop universal recommendations for hepatitis B shots for children and reduce the list of recommended vaccines, citing links to autism that scientists have repeatedly debunked.

U.S. President Donald Trump holds a signed executive order about vaccines as Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. looks on in the Oval Office of the White House on Monday. (Jacquelyn Martin/The Associated Press)

The executive order reaffirms Kennedy's overhaul despite the ongoing litigation.

Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, a physician who chairs the Senate health committee, condemned the order.

"I'm a doctor. This executive order ​is wrong. The president does not have the expertise to make these changes," Cassidy said, adding that breaking up vaccines "will mean children have to get more shots to get the same protection, not fewer shots."

Cassidy, however, ⁠has shepherded Trump's slate of health agency leaders through confirmation despite his own warnings about vaccine skepticism. He cast a decisive vote to confirm Kennedy in 2025. ⁠Cassidy lost his Republican primary in May to a Trump-endorsed challenger and will leave office in January.

Trump, Kennedy and other White House ⁠officials said ⁠the order means U.S. children would receive far fewer than ​the 72 injections recommended under the previous schedule.

Vaccine experts say that figure is inflated, because it counts combination shots such as MMR as multiple injections even though they ​are given in one shot, and assumes annual ⁠flu and COVID-19 doses.

WATCH | Winnipeg microbiology lab expanding to produce test vaccines: Winnipeg microbiology lab expanding to produce test vaccines | Duration 2:00 The National Microbiology Lab in Winnipeg, currently the only facility in Canada that can handle the most extreme infectious pathogens, is expanding. A new medical countermeasures lab, expected to open in 2033, will aim to better defend against the threat of future pandemics.

Dr. Elizabeth Mack, a pediatric critical care physician in Charleston, South Carolina, said breaking up the shots would increase the number of injections children receive, because they are currently given in combination.

She also said there were no licensed single-antigen measles, mumps or rubella vaccines available in the United States, making the recommendation unfeasible as written.

"We don't have a system that supports this," Mack said, questioning whether parents would be asked to make more visits and whether those visits would be reimbursed.

World.title: Hiker escapes after being attacked by grizzly bear in backcountry near Pemberton, B.C.
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A man managed to escape without being seriously injured after a grizzly bear attacked him while he was hiking alone near Pemberton, B.C.

The B.C. Conservation Officer Service (BCCOS) responded to the backcountry area of Rutherford Creek drainage on Sunday evening.

"The investigation determined the attack was defensive in nature and resulted from a close-range surprise encounter," said the BCCOS.

The man suffered non-life-threatening injuries, officials said, adding that he self-rescued and sought medical attention on his own.

"Officers have confirmed there is no ongoing threat to other backcountry users," said the BCCOS.

A predator attack team conducted an investigation and said anyone recreating in the area is encouraged to remain vigilant and be prepared for potential wildlife encounters.

Multiple first responder agencies collaborated on the rescue of a woman attacked by a grizzly bear including BC EHS, Pemberton SAR, RCMP, Conservation Officer Service and B.C. Wildfire Service on Aug. 2, 2026 (Pemberton Search and Rescue)

Grizzly bear breaks woman's neck

Sunday's incident marks the second grizzly bear attack in the region within a week — and both individuals were hiking alone.

A 72-year-old woman suffered a broken neck after a grizzly bear attacked her while she was hiking on Aug. 2 in the South Chilcotin near Pearson Ridge, roughly 70 kilometres north of Pemberton.

The woman was taken to the hospital by air ambulance in serious condition.

B.C. Emergency Health Services received a call at 3:20 p.m. PT on Aug. 2 for a person requiring medical attention near Tyaughton Lake, in the South Chilcotin area, after being attacked by a grizzly bear. (Pemberton Search and Rescue)

Pemberton Search and Rescue president David McKenzie said the woman also suffered several lacerations to her face, arms and neck.

"The bear was batting them around in the altercation," McKenzie said.

The Ministry of Environment said the attack was defensive in nature, from a female grizzly with at least one cub.

The bear was not removed nor killed, and no capture devices were set up.

Preventing grizzly bear encounters

Bear biologist and researcher Wayne McCrory said having campsites and trails that overlap with grizzly bear feeding areas will create a high level of conflict.

He’s done bear risk assessments for many national and provincial parks in the province over the last 40 years.

Conservation officer said anyone recreating in the area of the attack on Aug. 9, is encouraged to remain vigilant and be prepared for potential wildlife encounters. (Wayne McCrory)

"Where you have trails and campsites that avoid those areas, the conflict level goes way down," McCrory said.

Grizzlies feed in riparian spaces, such as moist spots along rivers or subalpine areas in high-elevation, he said.

"Most of the grizzly bear injury incidents occur after July, when the bears are more intensely feeding to gain a third of their body weight before hibernation."

McCrory said the trails where the attacks occurred should be assessed.

"Do more bear habitat mapping and professional risk assessments and look at readjusting some of the historic trails and campsites that are in high hazard areas," he said.

Research scientist Lana Ciarniello specializes in human-bear conflicts, and said trails should not go through grizzly habitat and closing areas during berry season can help.

"It's hard on bears," Ciarniello said. "We are taking up a lot of habitat and bears need a home."

Research scientist Lana Ciarniello has been in the field for 30 years and is pictured with a grizzly bear that has been immobilized to be prepared for release into the wild in May 2022. (Lana Ciarniello)

A current proposal from Recreation Sites and Trails B.C. would prohibit camping and motorized vehicles for the Brandywine Meadows area from June 1 to Nov. 1, as they say it is important habitat for grizzlies to raise their cubs.

"Don't forget this isn't only for the bears; this is also to protect the people," Ciarniello said.

Staying safe in the backcountry

McCory said grizzly bears are known to rub on trees and mark their territories.

"Grizzly bears are leaving their scent there," McCrory said.

Field studies can locate these tree markings, which are often visible with claw and teeth scratches or stumps on the tree that have been smoothed over and shiny from rubbing.

Grizzly bear hair is often left on the trees in the bark or protruding from stubs or limbs.

McCrory said grizzly hairs are usually light or white-tipped.

"If you find more than four grizzly bear marked trees along a trail, you know, that's the main travel route," McCrory said.

A grizzly bear seen on trail camera rubbing against a tree marking its territory, which alerts other bears and researchers of the animal. (Submitted: Wayne McCrory)

To avoid encounters with grizzlies, he said people should avoid travelling at dusk and dawn, and know how to use bear spray.

"That will help you survive a close, serious encounter," McCrory said.

Ciarniello said people should use their voice when in bear habitat, and travelling in a group also helps prevent attacks.

"Having a group of you, staying together [and] making noise, your chances are very, very reduced," Ciarniello said.

World.title: Suspect dead after Calgary police officer shot twice in traffic stop
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Calgary police say one of their officers was shot twice while conducting a traffic stop near Edworthy Park on Monday.

They say the officer is in stable condition and "in good spirits" after the southwest Calgary shooting.

"Today has been another very difficult day for the Calgary Police Service and our community," Chief Katie McLellan told reporters Monday afternoon. "Anytime an officer is injured in the line of duty, it affects our entire service and our policing profession."

McLellan says the man "was a known organized crime target."

At about 11:45 a.m., police were conducting a traffic stop when an occupant of the vehicle fired shots, striking one of the officers. Police say the reason behind the traffic stop is still being investigated.

The man fled into the park on foot, prompting a police chase McLellan says "was very dynamic and unfolded within seconds."

Calgary police searched Edworthy Park after they said one of their officers was shot twice while conducting a traffic stop on Monday. (Jo Horwood/CBC)

The man eventually carjacked another vehicle, drove it through the park until it got stuck, then resumed fleeing on foot, police say.

"On multiple occasions, our offender discharged rounds at our officers, and our officers returned fire," Insp. Darren Smith said.

Officers from around the city attended the scene, including to secure the area and search for the man.

"They were yelling at witness or bystanders to get behind vehicles, telling others to run," Smith said. "It was very much a chaotic and dynamic scene ... It was definitely, I would say, out of a movie scene."

Calgary Police Service Insp. Darren Smith, left, and Chief Katie McLellan speak to reporters after Monday's incident in Edworthy Park. (Ryan McLeod/CBC)

Officers chased the man on foot and tracked him through the air. Police said the man also shot at their Helicopter Air Watch for Community Safety (HAWCS) helicopter as it flew overhead.

They eventually found the man dead in the Bow River.

"We do know that he was subject to a self-inflicted gunshot wound. However, we cannot say whether or not any of our officers also struck the offender," Smith said.

The Calgary Fire Department assisted in the recovery of the body. A heavy police presence remained in the park Monday afternoon as officers searched for any additional evidence.

"There is no question that today's incident could have had far more tragic consequences, and we are incredibly grateful that our officer is expected to make a full recovery," McLellan said.

Alberta's police watchdog, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), is investigating the incident.

World.title: N.Y. jury convicts Montreal father of murder in death of 9-year-old daughter
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Melina Frattolin's loved ones and family members sobbed in a New York courthouse on Monday after a jury found the girl's father guilty of drowning her and hiding her body in a marsh last summer.

A group of family members held onto each other as the jury read out "Guilty" and convicted Luciano Frattolin, 46, of second-degree murder and concealment of a human corpse in the death of nine-year-old Melina.

Standing between his two attorneys, Frattolin kept a neutral expression, shaking his head slightly, before sitting down. He was taken away in handcuffs minutes later.

Once the trial was officially over, the family members hugged and cried between the benches.

Michael Langey, the Essex County District Attorney, said it felt good to hear the verdict after a year of working on this case.

"The grandparents were here, the aunts were here. They had to sit in the courtroom and there was a possibility, obviously, that he wasn't gonna get convicted. So it was a relief for them, and hopefully this could be some type of closure for them," he said outside the courthouse.

'Her daughter never came home'

Melina's mother, Kali Galanis, was not in the courtroom on Monday. She had not wanted to be there in case Frattolin testified, said Langey. Galanis lost her only daughter when Melina died, he added.

"She waited for her daughter to come home all night, looked out the window ... Her daughter never came home, and she had to get the call the next day that she was dead in a brook in Essex County, in New York," he said.

Melina's body was found last year in a marsh in a rural area of New York, partially covered by a fallen tree with a large rock on her chest.

The girl and her father were nearing the end of a weeklong trip in the United States when Frattolin reported his daughter missing on July 19, 2025.

Her body was found the next day near Ticonderoga, N.Y., about 400 kilometres north of New York City. The autopsy found she died from asphyxia due to drowning.

Frattolin reported his daughter had been kidnapped by two men who drove off in a white van, but investigators later arrested him for the child's murder.

Electronic data key to verdict

Electronic data played a big role in finding Melina's body and in the outcome of the trial, both through location data from Frattolin's phone and car, and through records of text messages and calls.

The prosecution called several police officers and experts over the trial who used car location data, cell phone data and surveillance camera footage to recreate Frattolin's movements on the day Melina died and prove the story he told to investigators was false.

"I think every second there was data in this case. We could see exactly where his vehicle was during the entire trip, and that was huge. Knowing that he wasn't where he was telling people he was was a big factor in them starting to turn the focus away from the abduction to, 'why are you telling us you're here when you're not here?"' said Langey.

Documents found in Frattolin's car helped prove intent, which was necessary in both charges the jury convicted him on. In the documents, Frattolin writes disparaging remarks about Galanis and mentions bringing his daughter to "the end."

"It was something that when you read it, there definitely was a plan. He definitely knew a life was coming to an end somewhere on this vacation, no matter where he went," said Langey.

"It was a tough case," said Eric Weyand, one of Frattolin's lawyers, walking out of the courtroom.

The jury deliberated for about an hour following a trial that lasted about three weeks.

Earlier in the day, the defence rested its case after Frattolin announced he would not testify in his defence.

"I really want to, but I was advised not to," he told the judge earlier.

The defence presented a single witness. The prosecution, who had the legal responsibility to prove their case beyond a reasonable doubt, presented over two dozen witnesses.

Defence argues inconsistencies

In the defence's closing argument, Brian Pilatzke, Frattolin's other lawyer, went back through the evidence presented over the last three weeks to fit it into Frattolin's version of events.

He argued that the inconsistent statements Frattolin made the night he reported Melina missing were due to English not being his first language, to stress and to exhaustion.

He added the police did not do enough to track the van when Frattolin reported the abduction, instead turning immediately to him as their suspect, and that they overlooked key evidence. The rock found on Melina's body was never tested for DNA, sweat or blood, he said.

Frattolin is scheduled to be sentenced on Oct. 14, and will remain in custody in Essex County in the meantime. He has a month to appeal the jury's decision.

Melina touched the hearts of people in the area, said Langey after the verdict was announced. Residents even adopted a section of the highway near Ticonderoga in her name.

"She really had no connection to the county, but I think whenever a child is murdered — everyone's got parents, they have children…. The community has rallied around it," he said.

He approached the case with the same energy as he would have for a community member, he said.

"It doesn't make a difference, whether she was from Essex County or Montreal or anywhere else. She was a nine-year-old that lost her life in our county, so I felt responsible for getting some type of justice for her," he said.

World.title: Former Miss Universe Canada calls out 'Feathered Headdress' and 'Arctic Beauty' costumes at pageant
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Former Miss Universe Canada winner Ashley Callingbull interrupted her own duties hosting the 2026 Miss Universe Canada pageant on the weekend to call out multiple instances of what she described as cultural appropriation at this year's event.

Just as director Sonny Borrelli was about to announce the top 20 contestants, Callingbull took the opportunity to speak.

"Sometimes there are mistakes that are made," said Callingbull.

"It's 2026. We should know better, but most importantly a part of reconciliation is that we educate and learn and understand and move on from these things in a good way."

On Aug. 4, Miss Universe Canada hosted its national pageantry costume competition in Windsor, Ont., where 35 contestants were competing for this year's crown.

During the costume portion, Karisa Haverkamp walked on stage wearing a turquoise, black and white feathered headdress and a small red painted hand on her cheek.

Jasleen Kaily, another contestant, walked out wearing a two-piece "Arctic Beauty" costume with brown fringes on the thighs, two braids and a maple leaf cutout on her back.

Organizers of the Miss Universe Canada pageant issued a statement saying the costume segment of the pageant will have guidelines in the future after Indigenous people reacted negatively to some of the contestants' outfits. (Miss Universe Canada/YouTube)

In an interview with CBC Indigenous on Friday, Callingbull said "my jaw just dropped on the floor."

"This cannot be real. I just couldn't get over that this was happening. Who allowed this on stage? Who approved this?" she said.

"Anything traditional or sacred should not be allowed. I was very, very upset."

On stage, Callingbull told the audience that Borrelli assured her there will be guidelines implemented and cultural liaisons moving forward.

Callingbull then spoke on stage to the Indigenous community, adding that the organizers released a statement earlier in the week but noting that the statement needed an apology.

"On behalf of all of us at Miss Universe Canada, it was not our intent to offend anybody and if we did, we take full responsibility, we will learn from it," said Borrelli, adding that Callingbull will be their cultural liaison moving forward.

Callingbull then spoke again.

"We're going to make sure that everyone is going to be respected and honoured properly," she said.

"And thank you for teaching us and we'll learn from it, we apologize again, we love you," said Borrelli.

Miss World Canada 2022 Emma Morrison said the costumes were culturally inappropriate and sexualized Indigenous people.

Morrison also said the hand print on Haverkamp's cheek, which she believes represented Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls (MMIWG), was not "the time or place" to make a MMIWG statement.

"When you're on stage, you're smiling to the judges and it just doesn't fit," added Morrison, who is Mushkegowuk Cree from Chapleau Cree First Nation in northern Ontario.

"The stage that we celebrated Ashley Callingbull on just two years ago is the same stage she is being disrespected on," said Morrison, adding that she believes the incident stems from a lack of Indigenous education.

Callingbull, who is Plains Cree and is from the Enoch Cree Nation in Alberta, is also the first Canadian and first Indigenous woman to win Mrs. Universe in 2015 and has championed accurate Indigenous representation in her modelling, acting and hosting career.

Callingbull said she immediately called the organizers the moment she saw the costumes.

"They were very apologetic and said they were being ignorant and that they didn't know any better. I told them, 'Unless you were living under a rock, we know that headdresses are not OK at Coachella, so they're not OK on stage,'" said Callingbull.

Both costumes can be found on the e-commerce websites Etsy and Fashion Nova. Etsy calls the headdress "perfect for music festivals, Burning Man style outfits, Halloween, carnival, parades and themed parties."

Statements and apologies come in

In a Friday statement, Miss Universe Canada said, "if any costume caused offense, hurt, or misunderstanding, please know that it was never our intention."

CBC Indigenous also contacted Borrelli for comment but was unable to schedule an interview.

The pageant said it is actively implementing a comprehensive costume guide that will establish clear guidelines and standards for all future pageant cycles.

"Within that statement there was really no direct apology," Morrison told CBC Indigenous on Friday.

In a post on her Instagram page, Haverkamp wrote she acknowledged and recognized that her outfit caused "hurt and offence" to the Indigenous community.

Haverkamp wrote she has learned from the incident and is committed to stand up and speak "for all women who have lost their voice because of violence, trauma and oppression."

Kaily also took to Instagram and apologized, saying, "My intention was never to disrespect or misrepresent Indigenous culture" and upon developing her costume she wanted to "recognize and celebrate one of the First Peoples of Canada."

CBC Indigenous attempted to contact Kaily and Miss Universe Canada but did not hear back.

CBC Indigenous reached out to Haverkamp for comment. She said she would talk to the Miss Universe Canada organization leadership before speaking and hasn't responded since.

Aleria McKay, the founder/director of Miss Indigenous Canada, is from Six Nations of the Grand River. (Submitted by Aleria McKay)

Aleria McKay, who is Onondaga from Six Nations of the Grand River in Ontario and the founder of Miss Indigenous Canada, said Miss Universe Canada has a history of cultural appropriation around Indigenous people, both on the national and international stage.

"The fact that they're just allowing those types of things on their stage is in my opinion shameful," said McKay.

Callingbull said the costume incident reminded her of her grandfather, who previously defended her when she faced racism in person.

"When he did that, he looked at me and said, 'You know if you never speak up, nothing's going to change.'"

World.title: Trump backs Infantino as 3 soccer federations accuse FIFA president of 'deception' in open letter
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

U.S. President Donald Trump says that embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino should stay firmly in place atop the global soccer body, saying it would be "a terrible mistake" to oust him.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup … ever presented," Trump said in a social post on Monday evening lauding Infantino's performance during the recently concluded global soccer tournament.

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Trump's comments came hours after UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs football in the Caribbean, North and Central America, issued an open letter on Monday ‌attacking Infantino over his conduct during the proposed sale of a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup.

The statement, which stopped just short of openly calling for a new leadership, said that Infantino had broken trust "through deception" with the now abandoned proposal, had "placed himself above the collective" and the three confederations called for a fully independent review ​of what had happened.

"Football's strength has always been its unity," their open letter ​to the football family said. "We call for that unity to be honoured now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it."

On this side of the border, Prime Minister Mark Carney recently stated he does not have confidence in Infantino's leadership "given what transpired and given the nature of what transpired."

Football world in open revolt

The Swiss administrator, Infantino, has faced open revolt in the football world since he proposed and ​then abandoned a plan to carve off the commercial rights to the World Cup and sell 20 per cent of them ⁠to private investors to raise about $4.2 ⁠billion US ($5.8 billion Cdn).

The Joshua Kushner-founded Thrive Capital was connected to the proposal Infantino had revealed. Kushner is the brother of Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

WATCH | FIFA ends plan to sell stake after backlash: FIFA scraps plans to sell World Cup stakes after fierce backlash | Duration 1:57 FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in future World Cups to private investors is dead after furious backlash, most notably from Europe's powerful soccer body, UEFA.

UEFA, backed by the AFC and CONCACAF, have threatened to boycott FIFA ‌tournaments until they receive a promise that no similar schemes will be proposed in the future.

"Leadership in football is not a possession," they said in Monday's statement. "It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it."

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the ⁠collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned."

They also criticized a FIFA emergency meeting in Morocco last week, saying there was only one elected official present, while also calling for an independent review which FIFA would have no role in, to determine what led to this "profound failure ‌of judgment."

On Friday, Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) President Lise Klaveness, seen by some as a potential candidate to replace Infantino, called on the 56-year-old to step down from the presidency immediately. Klaveness has long been an outspoken critic of Infantino.

Some federations still support president

After quelling in-house dissent at the emergency meeting on Wednesday, FIFA apologized to the 211 federations and Infantino rallied his support among the six ​confederations that make up the world governing body.

Africa's confederation CAF released a statement on behalf of its 54 members backing Infantino on Thursday with CONCACAF member Mexico following suit along with South ⁠American countries Argentina, Paraguay, Ecuador and Bolivia.

On Friday, as Infantino attended the inauguration of Colombia's new president Abelardo De La Espriella, ⁠FIFA released a blistering attack on the critics of the president.

It warned against what it called a "concerted and ongoing effort" to undermine Infantino, ⁠saying ⁠attempts to challenge his leadership must follow the governing ​body's statutes and democratic procedures.

FIFA also echoed the statements of several of the bodies that supported Infantino, as well as one from South American confederation ​CONMEBOL.

FIFA's statement came after reports by The ⁠Daily Telegraph about payments made by UEFA to a former employee during Infantino's time as the European governing body's general secretary, allegations he has denied and that FIFA has rejected as unfounded.

Almost 70 of FIFA's 211 member associations have said publicly they will vote for Infantino with around a dozen either withdrawing previously promised support or saying they will not vote for him.

UEFA apart, the confederations who say they have lost confidence in Infantino are not completely united, ⁠with several Asian nations backing him as ‌well as Mexico from CONCACAF.

World.title: How a former flight attendant posing as a pilot got free flights for years — and finally got caught
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A former flight attendant from Toronto has pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court in connection with a fraud scheme reminiscent of the 2002 Steven Spielberg film, Catch Me If You Can.

Dallas Pokornik used fake identification to pose as a pilot and get hundreds of free flights on multiple airlines from January 2020 to October 2024, the U.S. Attorney's Office for Hawaii said in a statement released Friday.

Pokornik, 34, boasted online for years about his global travels, according to a social media account reviewed by CBC News. Until 2024, the account regularly shared photos and videos from destinations such as London, England; Los Angeles; Mexico City and Phuket, Thailand.

"Many of my friends are married. Many of my friends are having kids," a caption reads for a selfie video that appears to show Pokornik rolling a carry-on suitcase through London's Heathrow Airport in December 2023.

Canadian-born Pokornik pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud in U.S. district court in Honolulu, Hawaii. (Dallas Pokornik/Facebook)

"I'm over here trying to avoid checking my bag and hoping for a window seat."

He was arrested in Panama and extradited to the U.S. in January.

Pokornik faces up to 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000 US after pleading guilty last week in U.S. district court in Honolulu to one count of wire fraud. Pokornik also agreed to pay restitution to three unnamed U.S.-based "victim airlines," including one in Hawaii.

"This individual took advantage of travel security protocols for his own benefit and he will now face the consequences of his actions," said CJ Ammons, the acting special agent in charge of the U.S. Homeland Security investigations office in Honolulu.

Asked by CBC News in January 2026 about the case involving Pokornik, Porter Airlines said it was unable to verify 'any information related to this story.' (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

U.S. prosecutors said Pokornik had worked as a flight attendant for an unspecified Toronto-based airline from July 2017 until October 2019.

A plea agreement seen by CBC News says Pokornik later showed a "false and fictitious" identification badge — claiming he was still employed by the Canadian airline — to obtain "travel benefits, including airline tickets that are reserved for pilots," from the companies identified only as airlines 1, 2 and 3.

Prosecutors said Pokornik even requested a cockpit seat reserved for pilots, known as a jump seat.

A Facebook account linked to Dallas Pokornik shared pictures and videos from several destinations, including Guadalajara, Mexico. (Facebook/Guadalajara)

His fraudulent scheme came to a halt after an employee of one of the U.S.-based airlines took a picture of the forged identification. The photo was passed on to Pokornik's former employer, who confirmed the badge was fraudulent "because, among other things, it listed an expiration date in the year 2027," the plea agreement states.

Dan Bubb, a former pilot who flew for a regional airline in Las Vegas for about five years, starting in the late 1990s, said the case is surprising and "very unfortunate."

"But given a world of artificial intelligence and advanced technology, I think it's kind of a wake-up call to all of us that people can manufacture authentic-looking IDs, which seems to be the case here," Bubb, now a professor in residence at the University of Nevada, told CBC News.

He noted that anyone strapping in to a jump seat needs to show the captain their pilot's licence and company ID. "I think, moving forward, pilots are going to be a lot more vigilant about this, so I don't see this happening again," Bubb said.

John Gradek, a faculty lecturer in aviation management at McGill University's School of Continuing Studies, said Pokornik's experience in the industry also likely made it more difficult for authorities to uncover what was happening.

"This is not somebody off the street who doesn't understand the business. This is somebody within the business," Gradek said. "But even with all of that knowledge, at the end of the day, he still got caught."

The case has drawn comparisons to the hit 2002 movie Catch Me If You Can, in which Leonardo DiCaprio plays Frank Abagnale Jr., a cheque-forging con artist. Abagnale Jr. claimed in a book that he had posed as a Pan American World Airways pilot, among other roles, in a multimillion-dollar fraud.

From left: Tom Hanks, Jennifer Garner, Steven Spielberg, Frank Abagnale Jr. and Leonardo DiCaprio pose for photographers at a special screening of the film Catch Me If You Can in Los Angeles on Dec. 16, 2002. (Rene Macura/The Associated Press)

Likewise, Pokornik never worked as a pilot for a Toronto-based airline, according to a Hawaii federal grand jury indictment.

Among major Canadian carriers, only Porter Airlines is headquartered in Toronto.

A Porter spokesperson told CBC News on Monday the company is "unable to verify any details related to this story."

The Montreal-based Air Canada and WestJet, which has its headquarters in Calgary, both said they have no record of Pokornik ever having been an employee.

Pokornik's sentencing hearing is scheduled for Dec. 8.

WATCH | Pokornik has pleaded guilty to wire fraud: Former flight attendant who posed as a pilot for free flights pleads guilty to wire fraud | Duration 2:00 A former flight attendant from Toronto has pleaded guilty to wire fraud in Hawaii in connection with a case reminiscent of the film Catch Me If You Can. U.S. federal prosecutors say Dallas Pokornik used a fake ID to pose as a pilot to get hundreds of free flights between 2020 and 2024.

Court records show he remains out of jail — with conditions — as he awaits his sentencing. U.S. authorities seized his Canadian passport in January.

Pokornik's case is separate from Project Icarus, led by Ontario's Peel Regional Police. In June, the investigation prompted the high-profile arrest of a former Air Canada pilot accused of operating hundreds of flights over nearly 17 years without a necessary licence.

Geoffrey Wall, 59, was charged with several offences, including fraud, public mischief and uttering forged documents.

World.title: Chile’s Municipalities, Senapred Meet Ahead of Storm Forecast
World.content:
SANTIAGO, Chile â As Chile prepares for an approaching winter storm system, the Association of Municipalities of Chile (Amuch) held a high-level coordination meeting with the National Disaster Prevention and Response Service (Senapred) to strengthen municipal emergency response measures.

The discussions focused on improving collaboration among municipalities, national agencies, and private service providers to better protect residents during severe weather events.

Power Companies Face Pressure Over Response Times

A central topic in the meeting was the performance of electric utilities during past emergencies. JosÃ© Manuel Palacios, mayor of La Reina, expressed concern over delayed responses from power companies in recent years.

âWe are exploring ways, together with Senapred and other institutions, to develop more efficient actions and hold the companies accountable to meet the response times our residents need,â Palacios said.

Rural Water Supply Risks Tied to Electricity

For rural municipalities, electrical outages pose a dual threat, as potable water systems often rely on electric power. Paula GÃ¡rate, mayor of Melipilla, emphasized the heightened vulnerability of rural areas during storms.

âLosing electricity also means losing access to potable water. Many rural water systems depend on electricity, and that remains our greatest concern,â GÃ¡rate noted.

Coordinated Municipal Efforts to Mitigate Risks

Senapred Director Alicia CebriÃ¡n highlighted the essential role of municipal governments in both preparation and response phases.

âMunicipalities play a crucial role in coordination, information gathering, and implementing mitigation works to reduce the impact of winter threats on residents,â CebriÃ¡n stated.

She underscored that emergency prevention and mitigation is a shared responsibility across public agencies and institutions. âPublic authorities who are directly involved in disaster management bear this responsibility, and we are committed to fulfilling it,â she added.

Winter System Expected to Test Emergency Readiness

The coordination meeting comes as Chileâs central regions brace for a frontal system expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds. Authorities emphasized that ongoing preparation and inter-agency cooperation will be key to minimizing disruption and protecting vulnerable communities.

World.title: Brian Wilson, Legendary Beach Boys Co-Founder, Dies at 82
World.content:
LOS ANGELES â Brian Wilson, the legendary musician, songwriter and co-founder of The Beach Boys, has died at the age of 82, his family announced.

“We are heartbroken to announce that our beloved father Brian Wilson has passed away,” the family said in a statement. “We are at a loss for words right now. Please respect our privacy at this time as our family is grieving. We realize that we are sharing our grief with the world.”

Born in 1942 in Hawthorne, California, Wilson formed The Beach Boys in 1961 with his younger brothers Carl and Dennis, cousin Mike Love, and friend Al Jardine. The band became one of the most influential and commercially successful acts in music history, selling over 100 million records worldwide.

Wilson was the creative force behind the groupâs distinctive harmonies and groundbreaking studio sound. His 1966 album Pet Sounds is regarded as a masterpiece that reshaped the boundaries of pop music production.

Among The Beach Boys’ many hits, Wilson co-wrote and produced I Get Around, Help Me, Rhonda, and Good Vibrations. Rolling Stone ranked The Beach Boys 12th on its list of the “100 Greatest Artists of All Time.”

Tributes poured in following news of his death. Nancy Sinatra shared a photo with Wilson on Instagram, writing, âHis cherished music will live forever as he travels through the Universe and beyond. God bless you, sweet Brian.â

Sean Ono Lennon called Wilson the “American Mozart” and a “one of a kind genius from another world,” adding: âAnyone who really knows me knows how heartbroken I am about Brian Wilson passing. Not many people influenced me as much as he did. I feel very lucky that I was able to meet him and spend some time with him. He was always very kind and generous.”

Throughout his life, Wilson faced significant personal struggles. Diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 1984, his condition was linked by doctors to earlier psychedelic drug use. In early 2024, his family revealed he had developed dementia.

Wilson’s wife, Melinda, with whom he shared 24 years of marriage and five adopted children, died earlier in 2024. He also had two daughters, Carnie and Wendy, from his first marriage.

Despite his health battles, Wilsonâs legacy remains unparalleled. His influence on songwriting, vocal harmony, and studio innovation continues to inspire generations of musicians.

World.title: Chile and Norway Deepen Antarctic Cooperation with New Agreement

Chile and Norway signed a memorandum of understanding on Antarctic cooperation Monday, reinforcing their shared commitment to peace, science, and environmental protection in the region.

The agreement, signed by Chilean Foreign Minister Alberto van Klaveren and Norwegian Minister of International Development Ã smund GrÃ¸ver, aims to strengthen bilateral coordination under the Antarctic Treaty System. It outlines enhanced collaboration on scientific research, climate monitoring, and the preservation of marine ecosystems through frameworks such as the Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meetings and the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

The accord includes provisions for regular dialogue between scientific and governmental institutions in both countries and seeks to optimize joint efforts in Antarctic and sub-Antarctic research. Both nations also pledged support for the Polar Codeâs implementation, aiming to improve safety and environmental standards for ships operating in polar waters.

Operational and logistical cooperation between Chileâs and Norwayâs national Antarctic programs will also be explored, particularly in alignment with CCAMLRâs conservation objectives.

This renewed alliance builds on the long-standing historical ties between the two nations and reaffirms their role as active stewards of one of the worldâs most fragile and strategically vital environments.

World.title: Japan Tops Global Waste Index 2025; U.S., Israel, and Chile Rank as Worst Polluters
World.content:
Japan has emerged as the world leader in waste management, while Israel, Chile, and the United States rank among the worst-performing countries, according to the Global Waste Index 2025 released by Slovak-based waste technology company Sensoneo.

The report, which ranks all 38 OECD member states based on their waste generation and disposal practices, highlights significant disparities in global waste management. Sensoneoâs index evaluates countries on per capita waste generation, recycling, incineration, and landfill use.

Israel and Chile ranked last and second-to-last, respectively, primarily due to their heavy reliance on environmentally damaging landfilling practices. Israel sends 524 of the 650 kilograms of waste it generates per person each year directly to landfills. Chile recycles just 1% of its waste and sends more than 95% to landfill.

The United States, which increased its per capita waste generation from 811 to 951 kilograms since 2022, remains the highest generator of municipal solid waste globally. The U.S. disposes of nearly half of that â 447 kilograms â in landfills annually. Neighboring Canada also performed poorly, landfilling 67% of its annual 694 kg per capita waste.

At the other end of the spectrum, Japan ranked No. 1, followed by South Korea and Estonia, all of which combine relatively low waste generation with efficient disposal methods. Japan sends only 3 kilograms per capita to landfill, relying heavily on incineration (245 kg) and maintaining a controlled recycling rate.

European countries dominated the top 10 rankings, with Austria, Germany, Finland, Belgium, Sweden, Norway, and Switzerland all demonstrating strong waste management systems. Austria topped the recycling chart with 334 kilograms of municipal waste recycled per person annually â accounting for 42% of its total waste.

Meanwhile, Spain fell four places to 27th despite minor improvements. The country reduced its landfill and incineration rates slightly while increasing recycling by 10 kilograms per capita. However, its overall waste generation rose by 10 kg compared to the 2022 index.

The index revealed that in 12 of the 38 countries, over half of all waste is still landfilled â including in developed nations like Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By contrast, Switzerland was the only country to report zero landfill disposal, while Belgium, Finland, Estonia, and Japan landfilled less than 3 kg per person.

Other key findings include:

New Zealand , Finland , and Iceland posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita.

, , and posted the largest reductions in waste generation per capita. From an environmental standpoint, incineration is considered preferable to landfilling, but excessive reliance on either suggests a need for stronger waste reduction and recycling strategies.

About the Index and Sensoneo

First launched in 2019, the Global Waste Index is published every three years by Sensoneo, a company specializing in digital transformation for waste management systems. The 2025 edition is based on the latest available national data.

Sensoneo operates in 87 countries and provides waste monitoring solutions to cities, industries, and governments. It is the only company to have successfully implemented deposit return systems (DRS) IT infrastructure in nine countries, achieving recycling rates above 90%.

In Madrid, Sensoneo is deploying 11,100 smart sensors, marking the worldâs largest smart waste monitoring installation to date.

World.title: South Korean Model and Actor Kim Jong Suk Dies at 29, Family Urges Respect Amid Speculation
World.content:
South Korean model and television personality Kim Jong Suk has died at the age of 29, his family confirmed on June 6. The news has shocked fans and colleagues across the countryâs entertainment industry, where Kim rose to prominence following his appearance on tvNâs 2022 reality dating show Skip Dating.

Kim, who began his career in modeling before transitioning to television, had been steadily gaining popularity in recent years. His sudden death has prompted an outpouring of grief and speculation online.

While the exact cause of death remains unconfirmed, some media reports have linked Kimâs passing to an incident in Hanam involving a violent altercation between a young man and his girlfriend. According to the reports, law enforcement responded to the scene, after which the man allegedly died by suicide after jumping from a high-rise building.

Amid widespread online discussion and conjecture, Kimâs family issued a public plea for restraint, asking the public and media to refrain from spreading misinformation or making disrespectful assumptions.

Kimâs older sister posted on social media, expressing the family’s devastation and emotional exhaustion. âWe ask for privacy and understanding during this difficult time,â she wrote, emphasizing the familyâs wish to grieve in peace.

Details regarding funeral arrangements have not been made public.

World.title: At least 132 dead in the magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck western Colombia
World.content:
At least 132 dead in the magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck western Colombia

11th Tuesday, August 2026 - 08:51 UTC Full article

Pereira and its metropolitan area account for most of the dead

At least 132 people were killed and 570 injured by the magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck western and central Colombia on Monday, according to the latest report submitted by the Colombian Association of Capital Cities at 7:00 p.m. local time. Authorities warned the figure is preliminary and that rescue work is continuing.

The quake struck at 07:34, with its epicenter near the municipality of San José del Palmar, in Chocó department, at a depth of more than 80 kilometers, according to the Colombian Geological Service. It is the strongest recorded in the country in the past decade.

Pereira and its metropolitan area account for most of the dead. Departmental tolls released by governors and mayors correspond to different cutoff times and do not match one another: Chocó governor Nubia Carolina Córdoba-Curi reported 12 dead and 84 injured in that department, while the mayor of Manizales confirmed two deaths. Fatalities were also reported in Valle del Cauca and Antioquia.

| URGENTE: Momento del derrumbe de un edificio de 3 pisos tras el terremoto de magnitud 7,4 en Pereira, Colombia. pic.twitter.com/r3v2lW5pU3 — Alerta News 24 (@AlertaNews24) August 10, 2026

The government put the number of damaged homes at more than 1,500, with 37 destroyed and 61 buildings completely collapsed, along with damage to 18 health centers, 52 schools, 17 community centers and 18 roads. The civil aviation authority suspended operations at seven air terminals: Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura.

Damage to the hospital network is among the most critical. In Cali, the Hospital Universitario del Valle partially collapsed and seven large health care institutions were closed and evacuated because of structural damage. Valle del Cauca governor Dilian Francisca Toro said at least five intensive care patients were trapped under rubble. Cali mayor Alejandro Eder reported at least twenty collapsed structures with people trapped inside and requested rescue teams from Bogotá and Medellín. The capital's mayor, Carlos Fernando Galán, dispatched a hundred rescue workers.

De la Espriella agreed to declare a national disaster situation and is leading a unified command post at the National Disaster Risk Management Unit, with additional posts in Armenia and Quibdó. The foreign ministry is coordinating international cooperation. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc was ready to provide assistance.

The Colombian Geological Service reported two aftershocks, of magnitude 2.8 and 4.8. The agency also recorded an emission of ash and gases from the Puracé volcano, in Cauca department, on orange alert since July, coinciding in time with the earthquake.

World.title: De la Espriella gives the first earthquake toll and entrusts Colombia to Jesus Christ
World.content:
De la Espriella gives the first earthquake toll and entrusts Colombia to Jesus Christ

10th Monday, August 2026 - 19:16 UTC Full article

The toll, as of 12:30 local time, is preliminary

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella reported 111 dead and 87 injured on Monday from the magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck the west and center of the country, in an address containing extensive religious references. “I entrust our country to the Lord Jesus Christ,” he said after chairing a meeting of the unified command post set up at the National Disaster Risk Management Unit.

The toll, as of 12:30 local time, is preliminary. The president listed 1,575 homes damaged and 37 destroyed, 61 buildings collapsed, 18 health centers, 52 schools and 17 community centers damaged, 18 roads affected and six airports out of service. The priority, he said, is rescuing people trapped under rubble. The government agreed to declare a national disaster situation, to be signed during the day.

De la Espriella announced he would personally lead the response and issue updates every two or three hours. He will travel to Quibdó, capital of Chocó, with the health and defense ministers, while Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara Restrepo heads to the coffee-growing region and Transport Minister Elsa Noguera to Valle del Cauca. Command posts have been set up in Bogotá, Armenia and Quibdó. The foreign ministry will coordinate international cooperation, and the president said the country's allies had offered assistance.

“Today all Colombians, without ideological distinctions, have to unite behind a single cause: the victims of this natural disaster,” he said. He argued that those affected would recover “with the help of God,” of the government and of the international community, and asked God to “protect Colombia.” Unlike his earlier appearances, he did not close with his customary slogan, “Firm for the Homeland.”

Religious language has been a constant feature since before he took office. The president was sworn in on Friday using the constitutional formula “I swear to God,” closed a speech to troops in Cali with “Long live Christ the King,” and included an interfaith segment in the ceremony. Days earlier he had gathered his incoming cabinet at a spiritual retreat, after which he said that “God must be placed at the center of every decision.”

Those statements have opened a debate over the scope of state secularism. The 1991 constitution established a non-confessional state, and in 1994 the Constitutional Court struck down a provision requiring the president to renew annually the country's official consecration to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Senator Jennifer Pedraza walked out of the inauguration session, saying the ceremony threatened the secular character of the state. Constitutional lawyer Juan Manuel Charry has argued, by contrast, that a public official retains personal convictions while exercising office.

World.title: Colombia records its strongest earthquake in a decade, geological service says
World.content:
Colombia records its strongest earthquake in a decade, geological service says

10th Monday, August 2026 - 14:29 UTC Full article

The quake struck at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT), with its epicenter about five kilometers east of the municipality of San José del Palmar, in Chocó department, some 240 kilometers west of Bogotá

A magnitude 7.4 earthquake shook western and central Colombia on Monday, causing damage in several cities and affecting six airports. It is the strongest earthquake recorded in the country in the past decade, according to the Colombian Geological Service (SGC). No official casualty figures have been released so far.

The quake struck at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT), with its epicenter about five kilometers east of the municipality of San José del Palmar, in Chocó department, some 240 kilometers west of Bogotá. The SGC initially reported magnitudes of 6.6 and 6.7 before raising the figure to 7.4 in a later bulletin. The focus was located at more than 80 kilometers depth, an intermediate range that explains why the tremor was felt across such a wide area. The agency has recorded two aftershocks, of magnitude 2.8 and 4.8, the second widely felt.

The earthquake was felt in Bogotá, Cali, Medellín, Popayán, Manizales, Armenia and Pereira, as well as in Panama, Ecuador and Venezuela. Buildings and hospitals were evacuated in the Panamanian capital. The National Disaster Risk Management Unit ruled out a tsunami threat along the Pacific coast.

In Manizales, one of the cathedral towers was severely damaged and left leaning against the main body of the church. At Pereira's Matecaña international airport, part of the roof came down in a passenger transit area. The civil aviation authority reported damage at the Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura terminals and suspended air operations at all of them pending structural assessment.

In Cali, the country's third city, facades came away, buildings collapsed and power, gas and water services were cut. Firefighters and rescue teams deployed to inspect structures while the municipal risk management council carries out its damage assessment. Injuries have been reported in Quibdó and at Pereira airport, without confirmed figures.

President Abelardo de la Espriella, who took office on Friday, ordered the establishment of a unified command post to coordinate the response and announced he would travel to Pereira. “You are not alone. The state is present and acting,” he wrote on his X account. He also requested a detailed report from the head of the national disaster risk management unit.

Colombia is one of the few countries in the world where three tectonic plates converge, and it records an average of 50,000 earthquakes a month, most of them imperceptible. The deadliest events in its recent history were the 1999 Armenia quake, magnitude 6.2 with close to 1,000 dead; the 1994 Páez quake, with about 800; and the 1983 Popayán quake, with 287.

World.title: Reform UK in talks with El Salvador over sending foreign prisoners to Bukele's jails
World.content:
Reform UK in talks with El Salvador over sending foreign prisoners to Bukele's jails

10th Monday, August 2026 - 09:23 UTC Full article

The precedent invoked by Reform UK is the arrangement reached by Donald Trump's administration with El Salvador

Britain's Reform UK party, led by Nigel Farage, has opened contacts with the government of El Salvador to transfer foreign prisoners to jails in that country should it win the next United Kingdom general election, which must be held by 2029 at the latest. The report was published on Monday by the newspaper The Sun and has not been confirmed by San Salvador.

The party's home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, set out its prisons policy on Sunday night. “We will deport all foreign nationals from our jails. If their home countries won't take them back we will send them to serve their sentences in countries like El Salvador and Kosovo,” he said. Yusuf put the number of foreign nationals in British prisons at more than 10,000 and argued that the space freed up would keep dangerous offenders behind bars.

According to The Sun, a delegation headed by party chairman Lee Anderson will travel to Central America in the coming months to assess the feasibility of the scheme, which would involve renting prison places funded by the United Kingdom. The announcement also includes creating 12,000 places through temporary prisons and ending early release for those convicted of serious offenses.

The proposal emerges as Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces criticism over his early release program, which takes effect in October and would affect some 5,000 inmates. Burnham took office in July following the resignation of Keir Starmer, without a general election.

The precedent invoked by Reform UK is the arrangement reached by Donald Trump's administration with El Salvador. In March 2025, the United States deported 238 Venezuelans to the Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT), opened in 2023 in Tecoluca with a stated official capacity of 40,000 inmates. As MercoPress reported in April 2025, President Nayib Bukele then announced plans to double the capacity of the facility, which held more than 15,000 prisoners.

CECOT is the emblem of Bukele's security policy and also its most contested element. Cells have no windows and family visits are not permitted, and human rights organizations have documented arbitrary detentions and deaths in custody under the state of exception in force since March 2022, which has produced more than 91,000 detentions without judicial order. In April 2026, 413 of the 486 defendants in the largest trial in Salvadoran history against the Mara Salvatrucha leadership appeared by video link from the prison, as MercoPress reported.

Farage is seeking on Thursday to regain the Clacton seat he vacated in July to trigger a by-election. His resignation came amid an investigation by the parliamentary standards commissioner into an alleged undeclared gift of five million pounds, on which no findings have been reached.

World.title: De la Espriella sets ten armed group leaders as his target for his first 90 days
World.content:
De la Espriella sets ten armed group leaders as his target for his first 90 days

10th Monday, August 2026 - 08:32 UTC Full article

The first results came over the weekend

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has pledged to capture or kill ten leaders of illegal armed groups during the first 90 days of his term, which began on Friday in Cali. The commitment, made during his campaign, is the centerpiece of the “shock plan” with which the new president seeks to reverse the negotiation policy of his predecessor, Gustavo Petro.

De la Espriella inherits a country with nearly 29,000 members of organized armed groups and at least 14 zones of active dispute between illegal actors, according to security force estimates compiled by the Fundación Ideas para la Paz. The most critical areas are Catatumbo and Arauca, on the Venezuelan border; Cauca and Nariño, on the Pacific coast; Putumayo, bordering Ecuador; and the jungle department of Guaviare.

Those identified include Néstor Gregorio Vera Fernández, known as Iván Mordisco, head of the self-styled Estado Mayor Central, a federation of structures that split from the former FARC. Also Alexander Díaz Mendoza, alias Calarcá Córdoba, who leads the Estado Mayor de los Bloques y Frente, a breakaway from that group and now its rival; Jobanis de Jesús Ávila, alias Chiquito Malo, top leader of the Clan del Golfo, with more than 10,000 members; and the commanders of the 33rd Front and of the National Liberation Army's Northeastern War Front in Catatumbo, to whom the president gave a one-month ultimatum during a visit to Cúcuta. None has been convicted of the acts authorities attribute to them.

The first results came over the weekend. On Sunday, De la Espriella announced the killing of alias Ruso or Alemán, identified by the government as the man sent from Arauca to take command of the 28th Front, along with three other alleged members, in a joint military intelligence and air force operation in the area bordering Meta, Guaviare and Vichada. The same day, at least five alleged members of the Carlos Patiño structure died in an offensive in rural El Tambo, in Cauca, where several families were confined to their homes. On Saturday, a vehicle loaded with explosives had detonated beside a toll plaza under construction near Santander de Quilichao.

The International Crisis Group warned in a briefing published on inauguration day that the severity of the planned offensive carries risks. Decapitating these organizations tends to fragment them and to trigger internal disputes over territorial control, the document states, adding that Colombian forces are already operating at the limit of their capacity.

“The strategy of going after leaders tends to generate more violence, at least in the short and medium term,” said Elizabeth Dickinson, the organization's deputy director for Latin America. The most cited precedent is Dairo Antonio Úsuga, alias Otoniel, captured in 2021 and extradited to the United States: the Clan del Golfo grew stronger afterward.

World.title: Keiko Fujimori starts her term in Peru with 60% approval, Datum poll finds
World.content:
Keiko Fujimori starts her term in Peru with 60% approval, Datum poll finds

9th Sunday, August 2026 - 20:58 UTC Full article

The poll is the first national measurement since Fujimori took office on July 28, after winning the June 7 runoff by one of the narrowest margins in Peruvian electoral history

Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori has begun her five-year term with a 60% approval rating, against 24% disapproval and 16% who gave no opinion, according to a Datum Internacional survey published on Sunday by the newspaper El Comercio.

The poll is the first national measurement since Fujimori took office on July 28, after winning the June 7 runoff by one of the narrowest margins in Peruvian electoral history. The Fuerza Popular leader took 50.135% of valid votes, or 9,223,396 ballots, against 49.865% for Roberto Sánchez of Juntos por el Perú, who received 9,173,755. The gap was 49,641 votes.

Despite that result, approval exceeds disapproval in every macro-region. It stands at 66% in the north, 64% in Lima and Callao, 62% in the central region and 54% in the Amazon east. In the south, where she lost the election, approval reaches 44% against 39% disapproval. By age group, the strongest backing comes from those aged 18 to 24, at 71%.

Sixty-two percent of respondents said they feel optimistic about the country's future, while 32% said they were pessimistic. On her first address to the nation, 62% said they had seen, heard or read about it; among those, 84% rated it positively and 13% negatively.

Expectations of the new administration center on the economy. Seventy-one percent expect the government to boost private investment, 66% to create jobs and 65% to improve the economy. Sixty-two percent believe it will bring order to the country, 60% that it will reduce crime and 51% that it will reduce corruption.

Security drew the widest consensus. Eighty-seven percent said they agreed with the armed forces joining National Police duties and with soldiers patrolling the streets, a measure announced by Fujimori. Some 86% support the military leading citizen security in jurisdictions under a state of emergency, and 85% back its taking charge of security in prisons.

On the new bicameral Congress, installed on July 24 after 34 years of a single-chamber system, 47% anticipate a confrontational relationship with the executive and 44% expect dialogue. Fuerza Popular is the largest bloc, with 22 of 60 senators and 41 of 130 deputies, short of an absolute majority. Sixty-seven percent said Congress should grant the legislative powers the executive has announced it will request on El Niño prevention, citizen security, economic affairs and labor.

The survey covered 1,205 people nationwide between August 5 and 7, with a margin of error of 2.8% and a 95% confidence level.

World.title: De la Espriella sworn in before Congress in Cali, delivers first speech to the military
World.content:
De la Espriella sworn in before Congress in Cali, delivers first speech to the military

8th Saturday, August 2026 - 07:52 UTC Full article

Abelardo de la Espriella delivers his first speech as president at the Pichincha Battalion in Cali

Abelardo de la Espriella took office as president of Colombia in Cali on Friday, the first time a Colombian leader has been sworn in outside Bogotá, and delivered his first speech at an Army battalion rather than before Congress, breaking with the country's institutional tradition.

The oath was taken at the Santiago de Cali University Arena, an auditorium seating more than 2,500. Senate President Honorio Henríquez placed the presidential sash on him before the full Congress. Shortly afterwards, De la Espriella moved to the Pichincha Battalion, where he spoke for more than an hour before the commanders of the armed forces and the police.

“The time has come to restore order, authority and freedom,” he said. He declared himself president of all Colombians, thanked Jesus Christ for sustaining the country through a history marked by violence, and said his victory was a victory for Colombian democracy against what he called totalitarian Bolivarian models.

The change of venue was decided at the last minute. The president-elect had intended to be sworn in at a military garrison, which Gustavo Petro blocked by barring military and police facilities from making preparations, arguing that a civilian should take office before the people and not before arms. Congress authorized only the university venue. Congresswoman Mafe Carrascal, of the Pacto Histórico, said moving the speech to a battalion amounted to bypassing the legislature.

His announcements included a tax reform aimed at discouraging evasion, the elimination of the wealth tax, the publication of a list of narco-terrorist organizations, the eradication of coca crops and financial inclusion for informal workers. He also promised measures on health, education and energy, and ordered action against all criminal structures.

De la Espriella, a 47-year-old criminal defense lawyer with no previous experience in public office, won the June 21 runoff by 250,830 votes, less than one percentage point over Iván Cepeda, the narrowest margin in a Colombian runoff in 32 years. He will govern until 2030 alongside Vice President José Manuel Restrepo.

The ceremony brought together ten heads of state, two vice presidents and fifteen foreign ministers, among them King Felipe VI of Spain and the presidents of Argentina, Javier Milei; Ecuador, Daniel Noboa; Paraguay, Santiago Peña; and Panama, José Raúl Mulino. In the morning, the new president held bilateral meetings with Milei, Noboa, Chile's José Antonio Kast, the US delegation and the king.

The United States sent a mid-ranking delegation led by acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, along with the director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, Sara Carter, and the vice president's national security adviser, Cliff Sims. Donald Trump, JD Vance and Marco Rubio did not travel.

Nayib Bukele, Keiko Fujimori, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Claudia Sheinbaum and Yamandú Orsi also stayed away. Petro, who does not recognize the election result, left the Casa de Nariño in the morning and said the popular mandate must be respected. Pacto Histórico lawmakers led marches in Bogotá, Barranquilla and Cali. Former presidents Juan Manuel Santos and Ernesto Samper were excluded from the guest list; Álvaro Uribe attended.

At the end of the day, Cepeda announced the creation of a shadow cabinet to oppose the new government.

The ceremony included remarks by a rabbi, an evangelical pastor, a Catholic priest and a monsignor. More than 11,000 security personnel guarded the city and Kfir jets flew over Cali during the speech. The choice of venue reflects a campaign pledge to govern from the regions: De la Espriella has said he will make Barranquilla an alternate capital and turn Cali and Medellín into satellite seats of the presidency.

World.title: US border wall expansion threatens memory of Porvenir massacre
World.content:
A border wall construction project in Big Bend National Park in West Texas began last week, with a separate, nearby access road threatening the archaeological landscape of Porvenir, the site of a 1918 massacre of ethnic Mexican villagers.

Contractors began work Thursday on 17 miles of low, noncontiguous barrier fences and patrol roads, with conservationists reporting bulldozers clearing native vegetation.

One new access road appears to cut directly through Porvenir, which was a small farming community along the Rio Grande over 100 years ago.

On Jan. 28, 1918, Texas Rangers, local ranchers and apparently U.S. Army soldiers removed 15 unarmed ethnic Mexican residents (13 men and two teenage boys) from their homes and executed them, according to a lengthy report in Texas Monthly last week.

The location remains a sacred place for descendants and an archaeological site. A 2015 excavation found military-issued cartridge casings, evidence that challenged the historical narrative that the killings were carried out solely by vigilantes and Texas Rangers. The Texas Historical Commission erected a marker in 2018 after descendants campaigned for recognition.

Archaeologist David Keller told Texas Monthly that a newly built access road about 16 feet wide crosses the eastern third of the archaeological area and has been traversed by heavy machinery.

He said contractors and local officials indicated the route could eventually be widened to 100 or 120 feet.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is managing the project through Customs and Border Protection (CBP).

The CBP said the barriers, though low and not connected, are intended to prevent off-road vehicles from traveling to and from the Rio Grande, adding that the Porvenir access route is not finalized and public feedback will be considered.

DHS awarded a US $1.7 billion contract in May for the work, which has drawn widespread bipartisan opposition.

Even supporters of President Donald Trump have opposed the project for using billions of taxpayer dollars to build low fencing in a rugged, remote part of Texas where few illegal crossings have been recorded.

Podcaster Joe Rogan, who endorsed Trump in 2024, called the plan “B.S.” on his podcast, the San Antonio Current reported.

“This is the most heinous attack on an American national park in generations,” Laiken Jordahl, national public lands advocate for the Center for Biological Diversity, said in a statement posted to Instagram.

The Current reported that it was the first time in U.S. history that the federal government waived such a broad set of environmental protections for construction inside a national park.

With reports from Texas Monthly, AZFamily, San Antonio Current and Texas Standard

World.title: Mexico sends over 300 firefighters to British Columbia
World.content:
Listen to this article

More than 300 Mexican firefighters and technical personnel specializing in forest fires have travelled to British Columbia (B.C.), Canada, to support emergency efforts during the intense wildfires that have led to the evacuation of more than 20,000 people in the areas of Summerland and Peachland.

The Mexican teams arrived in separate contingents during the first few days of August, with the first group, comprising more than 100 people, arriving in Abbotsford on Aug. 3, and more than 200 crew arriving subsequently. A fourth delegation left on Sunday.

We’re beyond grateful to our friends and partners in Mexico for sending hundreds of firefighters to B.C. They’re joining a team of roughly 2,000 wildfire service personnel who are working tirelessly to get these fires under control. pic.twitter.com/5i8vFQFStr — David Eby (@Dave_Eby) August 6, 2026

Groups are deployed primarily throughout Fraser Canyon and the Thompson/Okanagan region, where they are participating in firefighting and control operations.

The contingent also features an incident management team, marking the first from Mexico to be deployed to B.C. under the mutual aid agreement between the two countries.

The tasks that the Mexican crew carry out include direct fire attack and the extinguishing of hot spots using hand tools and pumps, as well as reconnaissance and monitoring of areas where heat persists. They also participate in felling trees deemed hazardous and installing equipment to ensure a water supply during suppression operations.

B.C. Premier David Eby recognized the crew’s work and gave a welcoming speech as one of the contingents arrived at the airport.

“Mexico heard the call and, as you can see, has stepped up in a significant way,” Eby said.

Okanagan Falls park acting as base camp for over 300 wildfire firefighters from B.C. and Mexico

Watch this video on YouTube

Meanwhile, Minister of Forests Ravi Parmar said that he felt proud of the firefighters’ joint work.

“I’m proud of the wildland firefighters from Canada and Mexico who are not thinking about borders but are answering the call, as we do when our neighbours need us,” Parmar said.

Mexico’s envoys are made up of experienced personnel from the National Forestry Commission (Conafor), the National Commission of Protected Natural Areas (Conanp), state and municipal environmental agencies, Civil Protection, rural fire management brigades and civil society organizations.

The arrival of the firefighting crews comes as B.C. faces more than 100 active wildfires spanning 156 square kilometers. In addition to Mexico, British Columbia has received support from Australia, New Zealand and other Canadian provinces and territories.

With reports from Now Toronto, Publimetro, CBN Noticias and the CBC

World.title: Navy ramps up security presence in Mazatlán after high July homicide count
World.content:
After Mazatlán in July recorded its highest monthly homicide total of the year, the Mexican Navy on Saturday announced the deployment of more than 1,700 of its personnel to the Sinaloa port and resort city.

In a statement, the Navy Ministry (SEMAR) said that the deployment was occurring “within the framework of ‘Operation Sable’ Mazatlán” and was aimed at the “strengthening of security” in the city, the second largest in Sinaloa after state capital Culiacán.

The deployment comes after 36 homicides in Mazatlán in July, the city’s highest monthly total of murders in 2026, according to the newspaper El Sol de Mazatlán. It also follows the arrival of 900 Mexican Army troops in Mazatlán on July 23. The bolstering of the army’s presence in the city was part of a security reinforcement in response to a series of armed attacks.

In its statement, SEMAR said that the navy deployment reflects “the institution’s ongoing commitment to the well-being” of Mazatlán residents and tourists.

The ministry said that “operational actions will be focused on strategic areas … with the priority objective of reestablishing peace and public order and weakening illicit infrastructure that fuels schemes of violence and places the health of the population at risk.”

The term “illicit infrastructure” was a reference to clandestine drug laboratories and the cartel assets that support the distribution of narcotics, such as vehicles.

In its statement, SEMAR also issued what it called a “respectful call” for citizens and tourists to have “full confidence and certainty in the deployed forces.”

The ministry said that the central focus of the Mexican Navy’s operations is to “protect Mexican families while acting at all times with strict adherence to human rights, the proportional use of force and the current legal framework.”

“Its presence in the streets and on the coast has the sole aim of providing a safe and protected environment,” SEMAR said.

Violence in Mazatlán

Of the 36 people murdered in Mazatlán in July, 32 were men and four were women, El Sol de Mazatlán reported on Monday. The newspaper wrote that two cases were investigated as femicides, while two of the victims were minors.

Among the armed attacks in Mazatlán last month was one allegedly perpetrated by the “Los Chapitos” faction of the Sinaloa Cartel against marines, two of whom died from wounds they sustained. Marines returned fire and killed 10 criminals.
