World.title: 'Images disturb me deeply': Congress's Sam Pitroda questions 'use of force' against Jharkhand students
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sam Pitroda on Monday backed protesting students in Jharkhand as an agitation over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations intensified in Ranchi.

Criticising the governmentâs use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons, Pitroda called for âreform, accountability and compassionâ as the protests entered their 18th day.

The development comes as the Jharkhand studentsâ 'Vidhan Sabha gherao' march in Ranchi on Monday saw police use lathis and water cannons to disperse protesters. The march was organised over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

The protesters are demanding, among other measures, the cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.

In a series of posts on X, the Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) global chairman said the grievances of young people should be addressed through dialogue.

"The images from Ranchi disturb me deeplyâ, he wrote.





Pitroda said students should not be met with force, calling them India's future and expressing solidarity with Jharkhand's youth.

In another post, Pitroda said, "Democracy requires governments to create space for peaceful dissent, dialogue and resolution."

Pitroda's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students, urging the Jharkhand government to address their grievances.

The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government is run by a JMM-led coalition in which the Congress is a partner.

Pitroda also said the protesting youth deserved to be heard respectfully and urged authorities to address their concerns over fair examinations, transparent recruitment, employment opportunities and their prospects for the future.

"These are not unreasonable demands. India owes its youth a system they can trustâ, he added in the post

He further said the concerns of students needed to be viewed in the context of the sacrifices made by their families.

"Behind every protesting student is a family that has sacrificed - often for years for education and the hope of a job.

Pitroda criticised the JMM-led Jharkhand government over the handling of recruitment and examination-related grievances, saying delays in recruitment and failures in examinations risk eroding young people's trust in the system. He called for "reform, accountability and compassion" in addressing their concerns.

Calling India's youth its "greatest assets", Pitroda said the country's demographic dividend could turn into frustration if education does not translate into opportunities and examinations fail to inspire confidence.

"We must redesign education, assessment and employment systems for this generation â not punish them for demanding change," he said.

On Monday, police and protesters clashed during the march outside the Jharkhand Assembly.

Police resorted to at least three rounds of lathicharge, while tear gas shells and water cannons were also used to disperse demonstrators.

Injured protester alleged that police began the lathicharge without warning.

The police have, however, given a different account of the events. Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said a stone was thrown at a police jawan and alleged that some "anti-social elements" attempted to provoke police and officials during the protest.

Addressing a press conference, Bhajantri said the police had exercised restraint throughout the demonstration and used "mild force" only after a situation arose in which a jawan's life was allegedly at risk.

Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said most students were peaceful but alleged that a section of protesters damaged barricades and pelted stones.

The protest also affected Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi after taking part in the march.

Mahto had been on hunger strike for nine days at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium before joining the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march despite his deteriorating health. He was later admitted to hospital.

The police action drew criticism from political leaders across party lines. On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong.

Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X, on Monday.

He further urged the Jharkhand government to address the students' grievances.

"The Jharkhand government must continue to hear these students out and resolve their issues immediately," he added.

The JPSC and JSSC examinations have been at the centre of protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has registered an Enforcement Case Information Report under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.

World.title: 'New Parliament,  PM house, why not new govt schools in villages?' CJP's Dipke announces nationwide campaign
World.content:
CJP announces nationwide campaign to improve government schools on August 15.

The âSarpanch Challengeâ

CJP backs Jharkhand protests

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages, seeking to address the "neglect of rural educational infrastructure".The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to work together to improve basic facilities in government schools.Dipke said he would launch the initiative from his village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, by approaching the village head and requesting him to take steps to improve government schools there.âThe coming 15th August is our 80th Independence Day. But, if anything has been neglected or ignored the most in the last 80 years, it is the government schools in our villages,â Dipke said on Monday.âWe have made a new Parliament, a new PM house. Why have we not been able to build new schools in our villages? Do we not consider the children of farmers and labourers the future of our country?â he asked.Dipke said children in villages continue to face difficulties in accessing schools and basic facilities such as drinking water and toilets.âEven today, village children have to walk a long distance to go to school. After going there, they donât find water or toilet facilities,â he said, highlighting the difficulties faced by girls in particular.âI feel that on this 15th August, if we should pay attention to anything, if we should make a new start, we should start by improving our government schools,â he said.As part of the campaign, the CJP has appealed to sarpanches across the country to take up the task of improving government schools in their respective villages.Dipke said he would personally approach the village head in Hingoli and urged other sarpanches to do the same in their villages.The organisation has termed the initiative the âSarpanch Challengeâ, under which it plans to publicly recognise village heads who improve their schools by sharing before-and-after photographs on its social media platforms and giving credit to the sarpanches concerned.âWe will give you credit so that after seeing you, after seeing the schools that you have improved, many other village heads also start improving schools in their villages," Dipke said.The CJP has also called for a citizen-led social audit of government schools.Parents whose children study in government schools have been asked to visit the institutions and check basic facilities, including electricity, clean drinking water, functional washrooms and mid-day meals.âYou go to your children's schools and see if basic facilities are available. See if there is electricity, waterâ¦ Do your children get washroom facilities? Do they get mid-day meals?â Dipke said.He urged parents to record videos if basic facilities were unavailable. The CJP said it would soon issue a printable audit form through which citizens could record the facilities available at their children's schools and those that were missing.The form will be shared through links on campaign videos on the CJP's official social media platforms and completed forms and video evidence can be emailed to the organisation.The campaign aims to ensure that children of farmers and wage labourers studying in village schools have access to facilities comparable to those available to children in cities.âIf not, you make videos of it. Because your children's schooling should be good. That is your fundamental right," Dipke said.âLet us all make a promise to the children who live in villages that we will improve their schools. Together, we can do this,â he said, concluding his video with the message, âReal India lives in villagesâ.In a separate video, Dipke also extended his support to Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was hospitalised after his health deteriorated during a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.Calling the alleged police action against protesters âcruel and inhumanâ, Dipke drew a parallel with student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. âBe it Jantar Mantar or Jharkhand, such police brutality against students is cruel and inhuman,â he said.âCJP stands firmly with Devendra bhai and his struggle. He is a true hero. We salute his courage and strength!â he added.Mahto has been at the centre of the ongoing JPSC-JSSC agitation in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike and joined the students' Vidhan Sabha gherao march on Monday, arriving at the protest in an ambulance as his health deteriorated.The CJP, which began as an online satirical platform, later took its campaign to the streets. Its 36-day agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar against examination irregularities was called off on July 25 following the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

World.title: 'At no cost' will Mann complete tenure: Congress' Warring predicts AAP govt collapse in Punjab
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring took a dig at chief minister

, saying the ongoing Vidhan Sabha session could be his last. The sharp jibe at Punjab CM came months prior to Punjab's assembly elections set for early next year.

Warring also claimed that the Aam Aadmi Party government could soon lose its majority because of growing discontent among its MLAs.

While bidding farewell to Mann, Warring said the chief minister would "at no cost" complete his tenure. He claimed that even if the Punjab assembly elections are held as scheduled in February 2027, Mann would not remain chief minister until then.

"The Aam Aadmi Party is likely to implode very soon as the government is losing its majority.

Many MLAs are just waiting for the opportune moment, which is not very far," he said.

Warring claimed that most AAP MLAs were "completely alienated and disillusioned" with their own government. "For four and a half years, they have felt suffocated and they are now waiting for the breather," he said.

The Punjab Congress chief alleged that despite receiving a strong mandate, the AAP government had failed both the people of Punjab and its own MLAs.





"Mann has proved to be the worst ever chief minister Punjab had, for which they will never forgive him," he said.

Warring also criticised CM Mann for continuing to rely on his image as a comedian after becoming chief minister.

He said Mann had failed to understand that his role had changed after taking charge of the state.

"Unfortunately, Mann could not make the difference that his stage had changed and he was no longer required to survive through narrating jokes and anecdotes.

People of Punjab had not elected you to make them laugh, for that they already had enough of your comedy," he said.

Also read:

The PCC president said people had voted for Mann expecting "badlaav" (change), but alleged that he had instead given up his authority to "outsiders" to protect his position as chief minister.

"Instead, you surrendered all your authority to outsiders while guarding your chief ministerial chair, for which you sacrificed the interests of Punjab.

History will never forgive you for that," Warring warned CM Mann.

Earlier, on August 5, Warring said he wanted to contest the 2027 assembly election against Mann and urged the Congress leadership to field him from Mann's constituency.

Addressing a gathering in Faridkot, Warring said the final decision would be taken by Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi.

"While Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge have to make a decision.

I am not in a position to do that. Either don't field me at all, or if you do field me, field me against Bhagwant Mann. I will contest," he said.

The remarks come as political parties prepare for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The AAP, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have already started preparations for the polls.

The AAP won the 2022 Punjab assembly elections with a strong majority, forming its first government in the state and ending the Congress' tenure in power.

World.title: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.

Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.

"We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said.

"We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.

In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.

World.title: India move will muddle border talks: China
World.content:
GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.

The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.

Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation.

"India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.

The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.

World.title: Jharkhand protest: Police defend ‘mild force’, to scan CCTV for miscreants - key points
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Police will examine CCTV footage to identify people they allege disrupted a largely peaceful student protest in Ranchi on Monday, as top officials defended the use of âmildâ and âminimumâ force to disperse job aspirants marching towards the Jharkhand Assembly.

The agitation, which entered its 17th day, saw police use water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge during the âVidhan Sabha Gheraoâ march by students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

While police said protesters refused repeated requests to clear the route and alleged that some people damaged barricades, pelted stones and tried to stop vehicles, student protesters accused police of using force without warning.

An injured protester claimed that at least 100 young men were beaten during the lathicharge.

Police to analyse CCTV footage

Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said police would examine CCTV footage from the protest to identify those allegedly responsible for disrupting the demonstration.

"Police will analyse CCTV footage to identify anti-social elements who disrupted the peaceful students' protest," Rakesh Ranjan told reporters.





Ranjan said 14 police personnel were injured during Mondayâs protest, including one who suffered a major injury. According to him, police used only the minimum force required to bring the situation under control.

"We had previously communicated--and it was agreed--that the siege of the Legislative Assembly complex would be entirely peaceful. The police exercised considerable restraint, and we allowed the students to proceed gradually as far as they wished to go.

We employed the minimum amount of force necessary based on the unfolding situation, and as a result, the current situation is peaceful," SSP Ranjan said in the joint presser.

He alleged that some protesters repeatedly tried to create a disturbance, including attempts to stop vehicles and objects being thrown at them.

"The police used minimal force; we allowed the protesters to do whatever they wished to do all day long.

We made every effort to reason with them and persuade them gently. There were some individuals who did not listen and repeatedly tried to create a ruckus. Attempts were made to stop passing vehicles--including those of officials--and objects like shoes and slippers were hurled at them," Ranchi SSP added.

DC says stone was thrown at jawan

Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri also defended the police action, saying the force had exercised restraint throughout the protest and intervened only after a police personnel was allegedly put in danger.

"On July 24, some students and student leaders launched an indefinite protest. Since it had started without permission--and given the upcoming Durand Cup and Tribal Festival--a request was made for them to relocate; they subsequently moved to Jaipal Singh Stadium on July 28," DC Bhajantri said.

He said the protest continued at the stadium while talks were held between student representatives and a state government committee.

The agitation later intensified after student organisations called for a siege of the Assembly.

"Throughout this, our police force demonstrated restraint and strove to avoid using force. Amidst this, certain anti-social elements attempted to provoke the police and officials; a stone was thrown at a jawan, and another jawan was being crushed by the crowd, placing his life in danger. Consequently, the police used mild force to rescue the jawan," the DC said.
