World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Former Darwin councillor sentenced over 'insidious' domestic violence
World.content:
Renowned Australian landscape photographer and former Darwin councillor Paul Arnold has avoided jail despite being convicted of a string of domestic violence charges described by a judge as "serious", "cowardly" and "insidious".

Arnold was today sentenced in the Darwin Local Court to a two-year intensive community corrections order (ICCO), with nine months to be served under home detention.

In November last year, Arnold was found guilty on more than a dozen charges, including assault, deprivation of liberty and damage to property.

The bulk of the offences related to seven separate incidents that occurred over the course of his troubled 18-month relationship with his former partner, Leanne Thompson, before the pair separated in early 2023.

Paul Arnold with his defence barrister Jon Tippett KC. (ABC News: Olivana Lathouris )

Arnold, 54, was also charged with and later convicted of aggravated stalking and breaching a domestic violence order.

The court heard during one incident, Arnold pushed Ms Thompson into a towel rack, headbutted her and threw her make-up bag on the ground.

In a separate event, Arnold took Ms Thompson's phone and blocked her from leaving his bedroom.

'No remorse at all', judge finds

In sentencing Arnold today, Darwin Local Court Judge Therese Austin said the offending was a "serious example" of domestic violence, describing his conduct as "insidious", "controlling" and "nasty".

Judge Austin said the offending had resulted in "ongoing and profound" impacts on the victim, including "physical, psychological and emotional harm".

"I find there is no remorse at all for the harm you have inflicted on Ms Thompson," she said.

Leanne Thompson has previously spoken out about the abuse she faced. (ABC News: Dane Hirst)

Arnold pleaded guilty to two counts of damage to property but not guilty to all other charges, and during his evidence he denied ever being physically violent toward Ms Thompson.

During her sentencing remarks, Judge Austin said parts of Arnold's evidence were "so implausible, unbelievable, and uncredible (sic)" there was "no reasonable possibility" they were true.

Arnold served as a City of Darwin councillor for three years before resigning in May 2023.

He was also the owner of a gallery in Darwin's CBD which has since collapsed financially.

Paul Arnold inside his Darwin CBD art gallery in 2022. (ABC News: Jane Bardon)

Arnold's barrister, Jon Tippett KC, previously told the court his client had suffered extra punishment due to negative media coverage of the case and had suffered a major decline in his mental health.

Today, Judge Austin acknowledged Arnold had been subject to "a degree of public humiliation" but found the attention was "to be expected" as a result of his standing in the community.

She accepted Arnold was "labouring under severe depression" and his mental illness would make prison "more onerous" for him.

Judge Austin said while Arnold would not serve any actual prison time, the ICCO was a "strict regime".

Arnold was also ordered to complete a men's behavioural change program.

World.title: Trump signs order to reduce childhood vaccines and break up MMR shots
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has issued an executive order calling for American children to be immunised against fewer diseases.

The vaccination schedule put forward by his administration recommends immunising children against 11 diseases, six fewer than what is currently recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Doctors say the order is based on pseudoscience, and will harm children.

Here's what to know about the order.

So, what are changes?

In short, the revised schedule called for by Mr Trump seeks to reduce the number of diseases and viruses American parents are advised to vaccinate their children against.

The six vaccinations the Trump administration would drop from the routine childhood immunisation schedule are:

RSV

Hepatitis A

Hepatitis B

Meningococcal ACWY

Rotavirus

Influenza

The order advocates separating the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine into three separate, single-disease shots, despite scientific consensus that the combined shot is safe and effective.

It also directs the nation's health department to improve research on vaccines, which are already extensively studied.

Why did he order the changes?

The changes appear to be motivated by misinformation, public health experts say.

In signing the order, Mr Trump promoted his long-held but discredited theory that childhood shots should be spaced out into separate medical visits.

That's despite public health experts raising concerns that spacing out shots in such a way could lead to an increased risk that children become infected with a vaccine-preventable disease before returning for another visit.

Why childhood vaccination is falling The decline in childhood vaccination rates should alarm governments and the health sector, according to the peak body for doctors.

Childhood vaccines (and how and when to give them in combination) go through rigorous studies, and safety tracking continues for years as the shots are used.

Kush Desai, a spokesperson for the president, told the Associated Press the plan to develop single-disease vaccines would "give parents more options on timing and frequency for their children", and increase vaccine uptake.

Mr Trump also repeatedly suggested the number or timing of vaccines could play a role in rising rates of autism spectrum disorder.

But scientific consensus based on decades of studies firmly concludes that there is no link.

Secretary of Health Robert F Kennedy Jr, a longtime vaccine critic, also said American children get 72 shots under the current schedule.

But that number includes vaccines administered during pregnancy and individual components of combined shots that inoculate against several diseases.

The schedule currently recommended by the CDC is similar to those in Australia, the UK and Canada.

The Trump administration erroneously said American children receive 72 shots under the current immunisation schedule. (AP: Jacquelyn Martin)

The Royal Australian College of GPs Specific Interests Child and Young Person's Health chair, Tim Jones, said the announcement would increase harm to children.

He disputed Mr Trump's recommendations, which he told the ABC were informed by pseudoscience and would "muddy the waters on the safety and effectiveness of childhood immunisation".

"He is harming infants who have no ability to advocate for their own health by continuing to peddle harmful, unsubstantiated claims at parents," he said.

Senator Bill Cassidy, the Republican chair of the Senate health committee, also slammed the executive order in a social media post, saying vaccines are safe and do not cause autism.

"I'm a doctor. This executive order is wrong," the Louisiana senator wrote.

"Breaking up vaccines will mean children have to get more shots to get the same protection, not fewer shots. It will increase hesitancy and make children less safe.

"The president does not have the expertise to make these changes."

Can Trump change vaccine policy?

It's not exactly clear.

In the US, vaccination recommendations are approved by the CDC director on the advice of a committee of experts.

Trump's health chief is dividing Republicans on vaccines US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr's anti-vaccination agenda is gaining ground, but resistance is coming from all sides.

Mr Trump ordered the Department of Health and Human Services in December to review how peer nations approach vaccine recommendations and consider revising US guidelines.

The department responded by cutting the number of vaccines it recommends for every child, but that move was later blocked in court.

That ruling was part of an ongoing lawsuit brought by medical organisations that argued the Trump administration did not follow standard legal procedure.

But Lawrence Gostin, a public health law expert at Georgetown University, said the Supreme Court's interpretation of Mr Trump's power may allow him to supersede CDC director Erica Schwartz if she does not agree to the new recommendations.

"This is clearly the first test for Dr Erica Schwartz," he said.

"The president is placing her in an untenable position."

What about vaccine mandates?

In most US states, children must be immunised against certain diseases to attend day care or enrol in school.

That's not something the president has the authority to change.

In fact, the executive order only advises states with school vaccine mandates to consider updating their laws to reflect the administration's preferred schedule, according to a White House fact sheet.

The president does not have the power to scrap vaccine mandates in schools. (Reuters: Jim Young)

Are there concerns about vaccine uptake?

Yes.

Doctors have raised concerns that the Trump administration's misinformation around vaccines could stoke vaccine hesitancy.

Mr Trump's executive order comes as students are returning to classrooms after their summer breaks.

Federal data shows US kindergarten vaccination rates have been dropping, with the share of children with exemptions rising to an all-time high in the 2024-25 school year.

The nation is contending with a measles outbreak so severe, experts say it could result in the US losing its measles elimination status.

Dr Jones said the outbreak has so far impacted more than 2,400 Americans, almost all of whom were unvaccinated, and caused three deaths.

Medical experts have linked the rise to slumping vaccination rates, a trend many attribute in part to vaccine scepticism espoused by Mr Kennedy.

Just this month, Mr Kennedy urged parents to vaccinate their children against measles, though he took no responsibility for the surge.

Mr Trump's executive order would needlessly contribute to increased fear and avoidance of vaccination both in the US and around the world, Dr Jones added.

"Without confidence in the lifesaving properties of widespread vaccination of children further children are going to die of preventable diseases — a travesty."

ABC/AP

World.title: Mother allegedly 'laughed' while intellectually disabled teenage son was tortured
World.content:
The mother of a teenager with an intellectual disability who was allegedly tortured, zip tied, wrapped in plastic and dumped in bushland allegedly "laughed" as she watched her son being beaten, a court has heard.

Warning: This story contains details that some readers may find disturbing.

Eleven people have been charged, including six minors, after the 17-year-old was found by joggers in bushland at Pallarenda, Townsville, on July 18.

During a bail application for the boy's mother in Townsville Magistrate's Court on August 11, police prosecutor Lescha Lawson said the alleged assault started after the mother of the boy made "false allegations against the child" that he was a paedophile.

The court earlier heard that the teenager was allegedly assaulted at a residence, and when he crawled away to escape, the alleged assault continued in the street with a horse whip and metal rods.

One of the co-accused allegedly made a phone call which led to more people arriving at the scene before the teenager was wrapped in plastic, zip tied and transported in the boot of a car and dumped in bushland, the proceedings previously heard.

'Tormenting' mother allegedly 'laughed' during alleged torture

On Tuesday, Ms Lawson said the mother allegedly "actively participated in the assault and encouraged" others.

The victim required surgery after sustaining multiple injuries. (ABC News: James Tugwell)

She said the mother allegedly watched on while her son was bashed with metal rods, "joking" about the assault, "tormenting" him and saying, "he deserved it".

Ms Lawson said the teenager allegedly told police: "His mother laughed as she watched him be beaten by a number of people with metal bars."

The court heard the boy has undergone two surgeries for injuries that include a broken nose, two lacerations to the scalp, a spinal fracture, a tibia fracture and substantial bruising.

Issues finding enough lawyers

Defence lawyer Mikaila Ward told the court there was a "lack of particularisation" about which of the alleged offenders were involved and to what degree.

She said there was "no forensic evidence linking my client to the offence".

The victim was allegedly dumped in bushland near Pallarenda in Townsville. (ABC News: James Tugwell)

She said the boy's mother said she asked her son to leave and watched him walk out the door before she headed to bed.

Ms Ward said the co-accused all provided different versions of events to police and flagged potential issues with finding separate legal representation for all the co-accused.

"There are 11 charged so, finding representation could be an ongoing issue," she said.

'Reprehensible' and 'incomprehensible'

Magistrate Steven Mosch said the alleged offending was "incomprehensible".

"It is reprehensible that the biological mother of the defendant was said to be present — if not actively engaged and encouraging others to do so," he said.

He read from documents tendered by the police which alleged methamphetamine had been smoked at the residence before the alleged assault.

The mother was refused bail and her case was adjourned to September.

'Just dealing with this sick f**k'

Meanwhile, when another co-accused applied for bail in Townsville Magistrates Court on August 11, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Service lawyer Matt Morton said his client "strongly" contested the allegations, and allegedly "put herself in the firing line to protect the child".

However, Ms Lawson argued the woman did not call police at the time of the alleged offending and had been identified by the 17-year-old as an alleged perpetrator.

The court heard the woman was not at the initial social gathering at the house but allegedly arrived at the house after an alleged phone call from another co-accused.

Police have charged 11 people over the incident. (ABC North Qld: James Tugwell)

Ms Lawson said the woman allegedly sent text messages to another co-accused saying: "I'm coming now, sorry. I was a little scared. I'm sorry. I thought jail time for me lol".

The woman allegedly texted another person later in the night saying she was "just dealing with this sick f**k".

Ms Lawson said those text messages suggested the woman was "more than a mere bystander".

Magistrate Mosch said the texts suggested "some proactive involvement".

He rejected that woman's bail application. Her case was also adjourned to September.

World.title: Inside Donald Trump's 'Hunger Games'-style athletics contest
World.content:
Anderson Reid, representing Puerto Rico, sprinted onto a military-style bootcamp course to the cheers of supporting families and friends.

Thrift Shop by Macklemore & Ryan Lewis played as he crawled, sprinted and carried jerry cans, vying to top the times of 119 other teenagers between the ages of 14 and 17 for a chance to win a university scholarship.

Anderson Reid says contestants did not have to currently live in the state or territory they represented, but did not clarify what ties he had to Puerto Rico. (Instagram: andersonreid88)

The Patriot Games 2026 were announced in December 2025 by US President Donald Trump, who billed it as "an unprecedented four-day athletic event featuring the greatest high school athletes".

"One young man and one young women from each state and territory, but I promise there will be no men playing in women's sports," he said.

From 50 states and a few more

One hundred and twenty competitors made it to Ohio to compete in the three-day-long athletic competition, commemorating the United States 250th anniversary.

The ABC has identified participants from Puerto Rico, Guam, the Shawnee Tribe and the US Virgin Islands, but not from American Samoa or other Native American groups.

However, there has been speculation some athletes might not live in the state or territory they represent.

Reid is representing Puerto Rico, but does not appear to live there, with one Instagram commenter asking, "Isn't he from Texas?"

Videos on Reid's YouTube channel show clips from Daikin Park stadium in Houston, Texas.

Responding to another comment on Instagram, Reid said "[Contestants] don't have to be currently living in the state or territory they are representing".

"They do have to have some sort of association with it such as living there or having social [family] ties to it," Reid said.

Little is known about the Freedom 250 Patriot Games selection committee, which chose the athletes based on video applications and personal essays. (AP: Nate Manley)

The idea behind the Patriot Games drew immediate comparison to The Hunger Games, a series of books by Suzanne Collins, which were later adapted into a multi-billion-dollar film franchise.

Patriot Games organisers Freedom250 said the event would "bring together outstanding young Americans from across the nation to compete, inspire, and showcase the values that have shaped the United States for nearly 250 years".

It's a unique qualification process, as unlike the Junior Olympics or national sports competitions, the pre-selection method did not involve qualifying rounds, but rather a video application process.

'I didn't think I'd get on'

Chris Brennan is representing North Carolina at the Patriot Games, and has been sharing each step of the experience on his social media.

In an interview with Trump-aligned influencer Adam Francisco Brennan said he stumbled across the Patriot Games online.

US President Donald Trump promoted the event as a showcase of the nation's best student athletes. (Supplied: X/Freedom250)

"I was just on Instagram one day, scrolling, scrolling and I saw an  and I was like, 'Hey, I heard Trump talking about that,'" Mr Brennan said.

"I clicked, submitted, I made a quick 5-minute video application.

"Honestly I think it was a little bit of luck and a little bit of my personality."

Chris Brennan posts conservative content on Instagram and, in an interview, said women couldn't compete with men athletically. (Instagram: notchris71)

Brennan then made it into the next round, and was asked to write an essay and answer "personal questions".

He later interviewed several of his fellow competitors in Baltimore, and they described stumbling on the Patriot Games like he did.

"I think it was on TikTok and I did it as a joke with my friend," Owen Carter of South Carolina said.

"I didn't think I'd get on."

The youth from North Carolina also runs a social media page called Club America, which features Christian content and Charlie Kirk quotes.

Some competitors said they prepared for the Patriot Games with cardio and pre-existing fitness routines.

Campbell Remus of Minnesota also participates in "Ninja Warrior" contests and other athletic competitions. (AP: Nate Manley)

Campbell Remus from Minnesota said she trains year round for track, cross country and the "Ninja Warrior" obstacle and fitness challenge, while Mr Carter said he went for "a lot of runs" despite not having much time to prepare.

On August 9 the athletes completed the presidential physical fitness test, a former national benchmark of core, upper body and cardio fitness retired in 2013. They also competed in team games of dodgeball and kick ball.

Joshua Chechile of Vermont participated in the 55-metre hurdles during day one of the Patriot Games, one of many different athletic events. (AP: Nate Manley)

The next day, competitors completed a multi-sport skill challenge called the varsity circuit, along with a military style bootcamp obstacle course.

The games will conclude at 7pm on August 11, local time, with semi-finals, finals and team competitions like tug of war.

'Follow my dreams without financial burden'

In her application video, incoming freshman Sophie Skidmore of West Virginia appeared with her neck adorned in sports medals.

"I'm always looking for my next challenge," she said.

"As for the scholarship it would help me follow my dreams without financial burden."

Skidmore was eliminated in day two of the qualifiers.

Trump commemorates America 250 The occasion was complicated by severe storms that gathered near Washington, forcing event organisers to order an earlier evacuation.

The top male and female athlete will each receive a $US125,000 university scholarship, but according to a report by the Education Data Initiative, the average cost of attending an out-of-state, public school in the US is more than $US182,000.

World.title: Slater still firing at 54 at Tahiti Pro, eliminating Medina
World.content:
Kelly Slater has advanced to the third round of the Tahiti Pro after the 54-year-old American overcame Brazil's Gabriel Medina and ​some heavy wipeouts at the 2024 Paris Olympics venue of Teahupo'o.

Slater's emotional Margaret River exit Surfing legend Kelly Slater holds back tears as his career effectively ends at Western Australia's Margaret River Pro, although the 11-time world champion is hoping for one last wildcard in Fiji.

Slater, who recently underwent hip surgery, retired from full-time competition in 2024 and welcomed a third child earlier this year ​but showed he had ‌lost none of his competitive edge against three-times world champion Medina.

In dangerous, challenging waves, Slater got smashed on his first attempt and was hit even harder on ‌his second wave, breaking his board in two.

But the Floridian recovered ⁠and threaded a long, deep tube that scored a 9.73 ‌out of 10 to take ​the lead.

He ‌then backed it up with another excellent score to advance over Medina, who beat Slater in an epic final at the same venue in 2014.

"I don't know if I'll ever have another heat with him, and ​he ‌got me last time," said Slater, who dominated the first day of competition.

He said he had been motivated by criticism of the ⁠decision to award him a wildcard ‌to compete.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

"You see those comments, ‌a lot of people doubting me or saying [the opportunity] should have gone to ‌a local wildcard," he said. "Even after all this time, I have something to prove."

Slater finished with an excellent two-wave ‌total ​of 19.06 out of ⁠20 to set up a third-round meeting with reigning champion Jack Robinson of Australia, who was pushed hard by countryman Callum Robson in round two.

California's Griffin Colapinto, who was born six years after ⁠Slater won the first of his 11 world titles, was the only man to better Slater's ‌performance in ‌the second round, racking up a perfect 10-point ride ​on his way to a season-high heat total of 19.6 out of 20.

Reuters

World.title: The medics offering healthcare to homeless people 'no questions asked'
World.content:
For the team behind Street Side Medics, the service comes down to an "exceptionally simple idea".

Founder Daniel Nour wanted to provide healthcare to people in insecure housing situations who are often too preoccupied with basic daily struggles to seek out medical attention.

But there are still barriers.

"I think that there's some distrust that will still take us time to work on," Dr Nour told ABC Radio Canberra.

" The system potentially has burnt some people and there is a level of trust that takes time to build. "

Street Side Medics will operate weekly in Canberra to provide medical care primarily to people who are homeless or in insecure housing. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

Dr Nour said there were many reasons for people's reluctance to seek out healthcare, including financial barriers, Medicare status, previous negative experiences, stigma and embarrassment.

"Inevitably at times they're more concerned about where they're sleeping, what they're eating, shelter, companionship, and not why they're short of breath or not why their stools might be brown or black."

'Huge sense of gratitude'

Street Side Medics has already been providing care in Sydney and Melbourne and is starting to expand to other jurisdictions.

It partners with other organisations, including those addressing the need for food and shelter.

The team includes a general practitioner, nurses, allied health professionals and volunteers.

Anyone can access the service, regardless of name, status or living arrangements.

Street Side Medics was set up by former Young Australian of the Year, Dr Daniel Nour. (ABC News: Lydia Feng)

Dr Nour said they had soft-launched in Canberra, prior to their official opening this week, and he had already seen some positive impacts.

"For the people that we're treating, there's a huge sense of gratitude that there is now a service dedicated to them on their terms," he said.

He said the fact that they were made up of volunteers was key to the success of the enterprise.

"Every doctor that is there on any given night or nurse or health professional is doing it because they truly care," he said.

"They want to see an improvement in the lives of some of our most vulnerable Australians."

Street Side Medics was started on the understanding that accessing healthcare can be challenging for a variety of reasons. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

The service has received unanimous support from governments, and Dr Nour said many Australians were "doing it a little bit tougher in the current climate".

"Accessing health care services can be challenging for any one person, let alone really if you have some barriers that limit you."

Helping an 'invisible population'

Sarah Peters is a doctor with the mobile clinic and said she saw it as a "great opportunity".

"I'm someone that's volunteered overseas in the Australian Aid Volunteer Program and I think it's really important to remember that there's need in our own backyard and there's an invisible population here that really need access to care," she said.

" And for me, as somebody who cares about women's health, I know that there's a lot of intersectionality between people suffering and not being able to see a doctor when they need it. "

Dr Peters said the program was not only free, but took a "no questions asked" approach to patient care.

The team hopes people will develop relationships with them as they seek medical care. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

"Particularly for those in homeless or insecure housing situations, we will attend to any medical need," she said.

" We'll take their blood, send them for investigations, refer them as required, give them medication, give them support. "

Canberra's medical services are at a "saturation point", according to Dr Peters, and a difficult environment in which to get care, particularly without a fixed address to enable Medicare.

Funding for bulk billing in ACT but experts not sold Expressions of interest are being sought to find organisations who are interested in establishing three bulk billed clinics in Canberra.

In June, it was announced three new bulk-billing clinics would open in the ACT thanks to federal funding, but it is unclear how they will be financed long-term.

With this in mind, Street Side Medics is also focused on providing continuity of care.

Dr Peters said this aspect, and the positive connections she could make with individuals, was rewarding.

"We don't ask questions or turn anyone away no matter where they're from or what their Medicare status is, we are not judgemental," she said.

"We don't force people to disclose anything they don't want to. And doing that, we hope that they will continue to come back to us and we make continuity plans, follow them up.

"They know us and we know them."

Nic Brown is the chief executive of Street Side Medics, which started out in Sydney and then Melbourne. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

Street Side Medics chief executive Nic Brown said they would run the service in one location but intended to expand to others over time.

He said 50 per cent of people they saw did not have a Medicare card.

"We know that bulk billing rates in the ACT are low," Mr Brown said.

"And so there's a whole variety of factors, notwithstanding a focus on just trying to ... get their next meal.

" Healthcare can drop down the list of priorities. Taking the van where people are removes some of those barriers. "

After successfully running in Sydney and Melbourne, the team has expanded to the ACT. (ABC News: Adam Kennedy)

The van currently operates once a week in Civic, in partnership with Vinnies Roadhouse at the Griffin Centre on Genge Street.

Mr Brown said they were keen to hear from other services that might want to work with them at other locations.

"Please reach out, because we'd love to partner."

World.title: Former Beauty and the Geek contestant pleads not guilty to murder
World.content:
A former Beauty and the Geek contestant accused of murdering her partner has denied the allegation and has flagged a potential mental health defence, a court has heard.

Warning: This story contains content some readers may find distressing.

Tamika Chesser today appeared in the Adelaide Magistrates Court and entered not guilty pleas to murdering Julian Story and destroying his remains to pervert the course of justice.

A lawyer for Ms Chesser told the court that investigations were underway into the 35-year-old's mental competence.

Mr Story's dismembered body was found in the couple's unit at Port Lincoln, on Eyre Peninsula, in June last year after emergency services responded to reports of a fire.

The body of Julian Story, who was allegedly murdered, was found last year. (Supplied: SAPOL)

The 39-year-old's head was found by a member of the public in scrubland east of the town in July, and was confirmed to belong to Mr Story in September.

Ms Chesser was a contestant on the television show Beauty and the Geek in 2010.

She has been housed in secure forensic mental health facility James Nash House since her arrest.

Ms Chesser will next appear in the Supreme Court for arraignment later this year.

World.title: Calls for Alice Springs-style curfew in NT town rejected by police
World.content:
Northern Territory Police have claimed they cannot trigger a youth curfew in Katherine, after the community was left shocked by a dangerous driving spree in the regional outback town last week.

A car was allegedly stolen from outside a business on Thursday and taken on an hours-long joy-ride around the town, with occupants seen hanging out of the windows and putting residents at risk.

The 13-year-old boy who was allegedly behind the wheel and a 15-year-old boy have been charged over the incident, while police today said an 11-year-old boy had also been summonsed to appear before court.

Loading...

Police said they were continuing to work to identify four other alleged offenders.

Dozens of residents of the town about 300 kilometres south of Darwin took to the streets last week to express their fear and frustration over ongoing youth crime in the town.

At the time, some urged police to declare a youth curfew — a call that was backed last night by Marion Scrymgour, the Labor Member for the seat of Lingiari, which includes Katherine.

"I support calls from the community and Katherine Town Council for the NT government to urgently intervene and stop the spike in youth crime that is having a devastating effect on the town and its residents," she said in a statement.

" I call on the chief minister … to declare a curfew in Katherine to give the community the support and respite it deserves. "

Under laws introduced in 2024, the NT police commissioner can trigger a snap order banning people from a certain area, including a town centre.

Marion Scrymgour says curfews can act as a "much-needed, short-term circuit breaker". (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

NT Police Assistant Commissioner Travis Wurst told Darwin radio station Mix 104.9 today the recent behaviour in Katherine was "unacceptable", but ruled out declaring a curfew in response.

"That's not applicable to this scenario," he said.

Assistant Commissioner Wurst said the dangerous driving spree did not reach the "public disorder" threshold under the act and it would take a "riot" to trigger such a response.

"It does not fit the definition as the legislation is constructed," he said.

Travis Wurst says the situation in Katherine does not meet the legal threshold to declare a "public disorder" response. (ABC News: Dane Hirst)

Police have said their response will instead be based around surging resources into the town, and having a higher visibility on its streets during the period of unrest.

Assistant Commissioner Wurst said he would be meeting with Katherine Mayor Joanna Holden today.

Minister calls for parental responsibility

The public disorder laws were used to calm a wave of violence and crime in Alice Springs in 2024, which Ms Scrymgour said acted as a "much-needed, short-term circuit breaker" and restored town safety.

Member for Katherine and NT Education Minister Jo Hersey has not backed community calls for a curfew, citing the possibility of reputational damage to the region.

"We just need to be very careful that we don't go down that same road that Alice Springs did, where we do detrimental damage to our community, where people don't want to come to Katherine," she told Mix 104.9 today.

Jo Hersey says the court system is "where sometimes it falls down" in regards to youth crime. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

"We just need to make sure that these children are not repeatedly out on the streets, breaking into cars, stealing from people, and that they are dealt with in a manner that the law is there for them, and that they are not getting bailed and out on the streets."

Mrs Hersey blamed the ongoing incidents on "the judiciary, that's where sometimes it falls down".

Katherine residents gather en masse to protest crime spree Some Katherine residents are calling for a youth curfew to be imposed after a group of joy-riding youths nearly collided with a mother and her 2-year-old daughter while they were driving home.

She also called for the parents of the children and teenagers involved in the recent crime wave in the township to take more responsibility.

"Parents need to be responsible," she said.

"Know where your young person is at night-time, and if you can't know where that young person is, well, maybe that's where someone else needs to step in."

The NT's Country Liberal Party government came to power in late 2024 on a tough-on-crime platform, but has not yet made any firm announcements about new plans to tackle the issue in Katherine.

World.title: Kuniko grabs NSW gold-silver project steering wheel
World.content:
Sponsored BusinessCompaniesBulls N' Bears Kuniko grabs NSW gold-silver project steering wheel Brought to you by BULLS N’ BEARS Penny Taylor August 11, 2026 — 4:56pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Kuniko Limited has seized a controlling 51 per cent stake in the high-grade Commonwealth-Silica Hill gold-silver-copper project in New South Wales more than 12 months ahead of schedule after completing the initial A$1.5 million expenditure commitment under its earn-in agreement with Impact Minerals with the company now takingoperational control of its flagship asset. Having taken up position at the helm, the company believes Commonwealth could host a far larger district-scale mineral system than previously recognised. The Commonwealth and Silica Hill deposits sit just 200 metres apart at the heart of Kuniko’s flagship project in New South Wales’ prolific Lachlan Fold Belt. Kuniko Limited and Impact Minerals beginning phase 2 diamond drilling at Commonwealth-Silica Hill NSW About 100 kilometres north of Orange, the project is in the heart of what can only be described as elephant country for minerals. It lies along trend from Alkane Resources’ giant Boda-Kaiser porphyry copper-gold discovery, while Newmont’s Cadia-Ridgeway and Evolution Mining’s Cowal and Northparkes operations are also part of the district. Modern geological, geophysical and drilling programs completed since September 2025 have transformed Kuniko’s understanding of the project. What began as a straightforward resource expansion program has evolved into something much bigger, with management believing it could host a far broader mineral system than previously recognised.



‘To reach the 51% ownership milestone is a clear demonstration of our confidence in the Project and its significant growth potential.’ Kuniko Limited managing director Maja McGuire That growing confidence appears to justify the company’s decision to fast-track its ownership. A phase-one drilling campaign delivered a 100 per cent hit rate and discovered the Silica Hill mineralised system beyond the existing mineralised footprint. The standout hole returned a bonanza 0.5-metre interval grading a stunning 347 grams per tonne (g/t) gold equivalent, comprised of 20,603g/t silver and 27g/t gold. The broader Stage 1 exploration program also outlined an approximately five-kilometre prospective mineralised corridor by combining MobileMT survey results, geochemistry and drilling data. It identified multiple high-priority drill targets within one kilometre of the existing project, including the historic Welcome Jack, Walls and Stringers workings, which extend across a two-kilometre trend and have seen little modern drilling. Together they provide several walk-up targets capable of expanding the project’s highly prospective five-square-kilometre mineralised system.



Management believes the results have laid the foundations for the project’s next phase of growth. Kuniko Limited managing director Maja McGuire said: “With majority ownership now secured, Kuniko is well positioned to continue driving exploration success at Commonwealth, with a clear pathway towards increasing its interest to 70% while advancing drilling, resource growth and regional exploration activities to unlock the considerable potential of this highly prospective gold-silver system.” Now, attention turns back to the drill bit. Phase-two drilling is underway, with assay results expected to feed into an updated mineral resource estimate targeted by the end of 2026. Kuniko will continue testing high-priority regional targets while completing a regional targeting review integrating geological, geochemical, gravity and MobileMT datasets. It also plans to evaluate additional opportunities along the approximately five-kilometre corridor. The company can increase its interest to 70 per cent by spending a further A$1.5 million on exploration over the next two years. Management expects to complete the Stage 2 earn-in through the current work program.



Upon reaching a 70 per cent interest, the parties will enter a formal joint venture. Under that arrangement, Impact Minerals will retain a 30 per cent interest free-carried through to a decision to mine before choosing whether to contribute its pro-rata share of future project expenditure or dilute its interest. Commonwealth is interpreted as a precious-metals-rich polymetallic volcanogenic massive sulphide system, while nearby Silica Hill hosts an epithermal stockwork vein system with high-grade silver mineralisation. Management’s decision to continue earning towards a 70 per cent interest reflects the confidence generated by the Stage 1 exploration program. Impact Minerals previously defined historical JORC (2012) inferred mineral resource estimates containing about 88,800 ounces of gold and 3.3 million ounces of silver. The resources remain open along strike and at depth, providing what the company believes is considerable scope for further growth. Phase 2 drilling is designed to validate, update and expand the known mineralised footprint. Having gone from being a guest at the party to running the show, Kuniko is now firmly in the driver’s seat at Commonwealth-Silica Hill. Every major exploration program has expanded the opportunity and management believes the project is only just getting started. With control secured and the drill bit still turning, the next task is no longer proving the system exists—it is discovering just how big it can become. World.title: Bears switch attention from Paulo to dumped Raider
World.content:
Perth has emerged as the likely destination for out-of-favour Canberra prop Corey Horsburgh as the Raiders eye a Brisbane forward to bolster their pack.

Canberra coach Ricky Stuart on Tuesday dropped Horsburgh for Saturday’s clash against Cronulla after a “brain explosion” proved costly in Sunday’s loss to Newcastle. The Bears had been in negotiations with Parramatta prop Junior Paulo about a two-year deal, but weren’t prepared to meet an asking price above $900,000 a season.

Corey Horsburgh’s career at the Raiders is likely over. Getty Images

They have now turned their attention to Horsburgh, with Bears coach Mal Meninga meeting the Maroons enforcer on Tuesday. The Raiders, meanwhile, are keen on Broncos forward Jaiyden Hunt. The Broncos want to keep Hunt, but Canberra’s interest is an indication they don’t expect to have Horsburgh on their books next year, sources not authorised to comment, said.

Brisbane were also in negotiations with Horsburgh, but are unlikely to have the salary cap space required to make a serious play.

World.title: ‘We don’t take chances’: Allegedly armed man Tasered on Sydney street
World.content:
Updated NationalNSWCrime ‘We don’t take chances’: Allegedly armed man Tasered on Sydney street Jack Gramenz Updated August 11, 2026 — 4:53pm ,first published August 10, 2026 — 6:59pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A man allegedly carrying four knives and a hammer as he and another man tried to run from police after a suspected drug deal on a busy Sydney street remains in hospital after being Tasered by responding officers. The 43-year-old man is expected to be charged with weapon and drug offences once released from care. Police were called to Emerald Square shopping centre on Belmore Street, Burwood about 4.15pm on Monday following reports of “suspicious activity”, NSW Police said in a statement. “We do believe that it was possibly a drug transaction taking place, but that’s all forming part of our inquiries, and the investigation is continuing,” Detective Chief Superintendent Christine McDonald said on Tuesday.



Two men allegedly “fled immediately” when officers tried to speak to them, but were quickly chased down. After “several attempts and challenges asking him to drop the weapon,” one officer drew his firearm as another Tasered the allegedly armed man, McDonald said. A 43-year-old man was Tasered by police responding to reports of “suspicious activity” in Burwood. Nine News Footage of the incident appears to show him fall to the ground, before sitting up, seemingly holding two knives, then being Tasered and pinned to the ground by officers after they yell for him to drop the blades. Another man, 26, has been given a court attendance notice for resisting arrest.



McDonald said she was proud of responding officers who used their training and skills to defuse a situation that “could have been much worse”. The Tasered man allegedly had two knives in his hands, and two more in his bag, where officers also allegedly found a hammer, cannabis and methamphetamine, she said. “He was in a busy area that was crowded with people. We don’t take chances when it comes to someone with knives in a public place,” McDonald said on Tuesday. She said it was extremely concerning people walked around with weapons. “It’s not worth carrying knives in public because you will be arrested by police and further charges will be laid,” McDonald said.
